title.raw: 卷四五 列傳第三七 文苑 Volume 45 Biographies 37: Men of Letters

sentences.zh: 夫玄象著明，以察時變，天文也；

translations.literal: The dark signs of heaven show their brightness to observe the changes of the seasons—that is celestial pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's dark signs shine forth to read the seasons' turn—that is celestial pattern.

sentences.zh: 聖達立言，化成天下，人文也；

translations.literal: Sages and the accomplished set forth words and transform the empire—that is human pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Sages and the accomplished set words in the world and transform it—that is human pattern.

sentences.zh: 達幽顯之情，明天人之際，其在文乎。

translations.literal: To reach the sentiments of hidden and manifest and clarify the boundary between Heaven and man—is this not found in wen?
translations.idiomatic: To sound the feelings of hidden and manifest and clarify where Heaven and man meet—is that not the work of wen?

sentences.zh: 逖聽三古，彌綸百代，制禮作樂，騰實飛聲，若或言之不文，豈能行之遠也？

translations.literal: Listening far back to the three antiquities, spanning a hundred generations, establishing rites and composing music, making substance soar and fame fly abroad—if words lacked pattern, how could their influence travel far?
translations.idiomatic: Listening back through the three antiquities and spanning a hundred generations, they set rites and made music, lifting substance and sending fame abroad—yet if words lacked pattern, how could their reach endure?

sentences.zh: 子曰：「文王旣沒，文不在茲？

translations.literal: The Master said, "When King Wen was already gone, was not the culture here?
translations.idiomatic: The Master said, "When King Wen was already gone, was not the culture here?

sentences.zh: 」大聖踵武，邈將千載，其間英賢卓犖，不可勝紀，咸宜韜筆寢牘，未可言文，斯固才難，不其然也。

translations.literal: " The Great Sage followed in his footsteps, nearly a thousand years distant; in between, outstanding worthies beyond counting—all should have laid down the brush and stilled the writing desk, not speaking of wen—yet talent was hard to find; was it not so?
translations.idiomatic: " The Great Sage followed in his wake, nearly a thousand years on; between them outstanding men beyond count—all might have laid down brush and stilled the desk and left wen unspoken—yet talent was scarce; was it not so?

sentences.zh: 至夫遊、夏以文詞擅美，顏回則庶幾將聖，屈、宋所以後塵，卿、雲未能輟簡。

translations.literal: As for You and Xia, who excelled in literary phrasing, Yan Hui who nearly reached sagehood, Qu Yuan and Song Yu who followed in the dust, and Sima Xiangru and Yang Xiong who could not lay down the bamboo slip—
translations.idiomatic: You and Xia excelled in literary phrasing; Yan Hui nearly reached sagehood; Qu Yuan and Song Yu followed in the dust; Sima Xiangru and Yang Xiong could not lay down the slip—

sentences.zh: 於是辭人才子，波駭雲屬，振鵷鷺之羽儀，縱雕龍之符采，人謂得玄珠於赤水，策奔電於崑丘，開四照於春華，成萬寶於秋實。

translations.literal: then literary talents and fine minds surged like waves and clustered like clouds, shaking the phoenix's pinions and letting the carved dragon's brilliance run free; men said they had gained the dark pearl at Red Water and driven lightning across Kunlun, opening fourfold radiance upon spring flowers and amassing ten thousand treasures in autumn fruit.
translations.idiomatic: then men of letters and fine minds surged like waves and clustered like clouds, shaking phoenix pinions and letting carved-dragon brilliance run free; they were said to have taken the dark pearl at Red Water and driven lightning across Kunqiu, opening fourfold radiance on spring flowers and heaping ten thousand treasures in autumn fruit.

sentences.zh: 然文之所起，情發於中。

translations.literal: Yet where wen arises, feeling stirs from within.
translations.idiomatic: Yet wen arises when feeling stirs within.

sentences.zh: 人有六情，稟五常之秀；

translations.literal: Man has the six feelings and receives the excellence of the five constants;
translations.idiomatic: Man has six feelings and receives the excellence of the five constants;

sentences.zh: 情感六氣，順四時之序。

translations.literal: feeling responds to the six qi and follows the sequence of the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: feeling answers the six qi and follows the four seasons' order.

sentences.zh: 其有帝資懸解，天縱多能，摛黼黻於生知，問珪璋於先覺，譬雕雲之自成五色，猶儀鳳之冥會八音，斯固感英靈以特達，非勞心所能致也。

translations.literal: Those who possess Heaven's endowment suspended and released, Heaven's unbounded many gifts, weaving brocade patterns from innate knowing and seeking jade tablets from foreknowing sages—as if carved clouds formed five colors of themselves, as if the ritual phoenix secretly matched the eight tones—such men are moved by heroic spirit to stand apart; it is not what laboring mind can achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Those Heaven-endowed and Heaven-talented, weaving brocade from innate knowing and seeking jade from foreknowing sages—as if carved clouds took five colors of themselves, as if the ritual phoenix matched the eight tones in secret—are lifted by heroic spirit; no laboring mind can force that.

sentences.zh: 縱其情思底滯，關鍵不通，但伏膺無怠，鑽仰斯切，馳騖勝流，周旋益友，強學廣其聞見，專心屏於涉求，畫繢飾以丹青，雕琢成其器用，是以學而知之，猶足賢乎已也。

translations.literal: Even if feeling and thought sink to the bottom and the key-bolt will not turn, so long as one bows the breast without slackening and drills upward with utmost keenness, racing among masters and turning with worthy friends, strengthening study to broaden sight and hearing and concentrating the mind to bar vain seeking—painting and adorning with cinnabar and green, carving and polishing into useful vessels—then learning and thereby knowing still suffices to make one worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Even when feeling and thought stall and the key will not turn, if one bows the breast without slackening, drills upward with keenness, races among masters and turns with worthy friends, strengthens study to widen sight and hearing and bars the mind from vain seeking—painting with cinnabar and green, carving into useful vessels—then to learn and know still makes one worthy enough.

sentences.zh: 謂石為獸，射之洞開，精之至也。

translations.literal: To take stone for beast and shoot it so the hole opens clear—that is the utmost of skill.
translations.idiomatic: To take stone for beast and shoot until the hole opens clean—that is skill at its utmost.

sentences.zh: 積歲解牛，砉然遊刃，習之久也。

translations.literal: Year upon year to dissect the ox until the blade hums through the gaps—that is long practice.
translations.idiomatic: Year upon year to dissect the ox until the blade hums through the gaps—that is long practice.

sentences.zh: 自非渾沌無可鑿之姿，窮奇懷不移之情，安有至精久習而不成功者焉。

translations.literal: Unless one's form were Chaos that nothing can carve and one's heart held an unshifting feeling for the extreme, how could there be success through utmost skill and long habit?
translations.idiomatic: Unless one's form were Chaos that nothing can carve and one's heart held feeling that would not shift, how could utmost skill and long habit ever succeed?

sentences.zh: 善乎魏文之著論也：「人多不強力，貧賤則懾於饑寒，富貴則流於逸樂，遂營目前之務，而遺千載之功，日月逝於上，體貌衰於下，忽然與萬物遷化，斯志士大痛也。」

translations.literal: Well said is Emperor Wen of Wei's treatise: "Most men do not strengthen their force; in poverty and low estate they shrink before hunger and cold, in wealth and honor they drift into ease and pleasure, then scheme for the business at hand and abandon merit for a thousand years. The sun and moon flee above while the body declines below; suddenly one transforms with the ten thousand things—this is the great pain of men of resolve."
translations.idiomatic: Well said is Emperor Wen of Wei's treatise: "Most men do not strengthen their force; poor and lowly, they shrink before hunger and cold; rich and honored, they drift into ease and pleasure; they scheme for what lies before them and abandon work for a thousand years. Sun and moon flee overhead while the body fails below; suddenly one transforms with the ten thousand things—that is the great pain of men of resolve."

sentences.zh: 沈休文云：「自漢至魏，四百餘年，辭人才子，文體三變。

translations.literal: Shen Yue said, "From Han to Wei, more than four hundred years—men of letters and fine minds; literary forms changed thrice."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue said, "From Han to Wei, more than four hundred years—men of letters and fine minds; literary forms changed thrice."

sentences.zh: 」然自茲厥後，軌轍尤多。

translations.literal: Yet from then until afterward, tracks and ruts were especially many.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from then on, tracks and ruts multiplied all the more.

sentences.zh: 江左梁末，彌尚輕險，始自儲宮，刑乎流俗，雜惉懘以成音，故雖悲而不雅。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi in late Liang, frivolity and peril were still more honored, beginning in the crown prince's quarters and reaching the floating customs, mixing turbid clamor to make sound—thus though mournful, it was not refined.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Yangzi in late Liang, frivolity and peril were honored still more, beginning in the crown prince's quarters and spreading through floating custom, mixing turbid clamor into music—so that though mournful, it was not refined.

sentences.zh: 爰逮武平，政乖時蠹，唯藻思之美，雅道猶存，履柔順以成文，蒙大難而能正。

translations.literal: Down to Wuping, government strayed and the age was worm-eaten; only the beauty of literary thought and the elegant way still survived—treading softness and compliance to make wen, enduring great calamity yet remaining upright.
translations.idiomatic: Down to Wuping, government strayed and the age rotted; only literary thought's beauty and the elegant way survived—treading softness and compliance to make wen, enduring great calamity yet keeping upright.

sentences.zh: 原夫兩朝叔世，俱肆淫聲，而齊氏變風，屬諸弦管，梁時變雅，在夫篇什。

translations.literal: Tracing the two dynasties' declining age, both indulged in licentious sound; yet Qi changed the wind and lodged it in string and pipe, while Liang changed the ya and placed it in chapters and stanzas.
translations.idiomatic: Both dynasties in their declining age indulged licentious sound; yet Qi changed the wind and put it in string and pipe, while Liang changed the ya and put it in chapters and stanzas.

sentences.zh: 莫非易俗所致，並為亡國之音；

translations.literal: All were brought about by changing custom and together were music of a perishing state;
translations.idiomatic: All came from changing custom and together made music of a perishing state;

sentences.zh: 而應變不殊，感物或異，何哉？

translations.literal: yet responding to change was not different while being moved by things sometimes differed—why?
translations.idiomatic: yet responding to change was the same while being moved by things sometimes differed—why?

sentences.zh: 蓋隨君上之情欲也。

translations.literal: It followed the ruler's desires and feelings above.
translations.idiomatic: It followed the desires and feelings of the ruler above.

sentences.zh: 有齊自霸圖云啟，廣延髦儁，開四門以納之，舉八纮以掩之，鄴京之下，煙霏霧集，河間邢子才、鉅鹿魏伯起、范陽盧元明、鉅鹿魏季景、清河崔長孺、河間邢子明、范陽祖孝徵、樂安孫彥舉、中山杜輔玄、北平陽子烈並其流也。

translations.literal: When Qi from its hegemonic design onward broadly extended eminent worthies, opened four gates to receive them, and raised eight cords to cover them, below Ye capital mist and fog gathered—Hejian Xing Zicai, Julu Wei Boqi, Fanyang Lu Yuanming, Julu Wei Jijing, Qinghe Cui Changru, Hejian Xing Ziming, Fanyang Zu Xiaozheng, Le'an Sun Yanju, Zhongshan Du Fuxuan, and Beiping Yang Zilie were all of that current.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi from its hegemonic design onward extended eminent worthies, opened four gates to receive them, and raised eight cords to gather them, below Ye mist and fog clustered—Hejian Xing Zicai, Julu Wei Boqi, Fanyang Lu Yuanming, Julu Wei Jijing, Qinghe Cui Changru, Hejian Xing Ziming, Fanyang Zu Xiaozheng, Le'an Sun Yanju, Zhongshan Du Fuxuan, and Beiping Yang Zilie were all of that stream.

sentences.zh: 復有范陽祖鴻勳亦參文士之列。

translations.literal: There was also Fanyang Zu Hongxun, who likewise joined the ranks of literary gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Fanyang Zu Hongxun also joined the ranks of literary gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 天保中，李愔、陸邛、崔瞻、陸元規並在中書，參掌綸誥。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, Li Yin, Lu Qiong, Cui Zhan, and Lu Yuangui were all in the Secretariat, participating in drafting edicts and commands.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era, Li Yin, Lu Qiong, Cui Zhan, and Lu Yuangui were all in the Secretariat, sharing in the drafting of edicts and commands.

sentences.zh: 其李廣、樊遜、李德林、盧詢祖、盧思道始以文章著名。

translations.literal: Li Guang, Fan Xun, Li Delin, Lu Xunzu, and Lu Sidao first became famous for their writings.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang, Fan Xun, Li Delin, Lu Xunzu, and Lu Sidao first won fame through their writings.

sentences.zh: 皇建之朝，常侍王晞獨擅其美。

translations.literal: In the Huangjian reign, Regular Attendant Wang Xi alone monopolized the beauty of it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangjian reign, Regular Attendant Wang Xi alone held the beauty of it.

sentences.zh: 河清、天統之辰，杜臺卿、劉逖、魏騫亦參知詔敕。

translations.literal: In the Heqing and Tiantong eras, Du Taiqing, Liu Ti, and Wei Qian also participated in knowing edicts and commands.
translations.idiomatic: In the Heqing and Tiantong eras, Du Taiqing, Liu Ti, and Wei Qian also shared in edicts and commands.

sentences.zh: 自愔以下，在省唯撰述除官詔旨，其關涉軍國文翰，多是魏收作之。

translations.literal: From Yin downward, within the Secretariat they only compiled and drafted appointments and dismissal edicts; documents touching military and state affairs were mostly written by Wei Shou.
translations.idiomatic: From Yin downward, within the Secretariat they only compiled appointments and dismissal edicts; documents touching military and state affairs were mostly Wei Shou's work.

sentences.zh: 及在武平，李若、荀士遜、李德林、薛道衡為中書侍郎，諸軍國文書及大詔誥俱是德林之筆，道衡諸人皆不預也。

translations.literal: In Wuping, Li Ruo, Xun Shixun, Li Delin, and Xue Daheng were secretariat vice ministers; military and state documents and great edicts and commands were all Delin's brush—Daheng and the others did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping, Li Ruo, Xun Shixun, Li Delin, and Xue Daheng were secretariat vice ministers; military and state papers and great edicts were all Delin's brush—Daheng and the rest did not take part.

sentences.zh: 後主雖溺於群小，然頗好諷詠，幼稚時，曾讀詩賦，語人云：「終有解作此理不？

translations.literal: Though the Later Sovereign was drowned among petty men, he was quite fond of reciting and chanting; in childhood he had read poetry and fu and said to people, "Will there in the end be someone who understands how to make this principle?
translations.idiomatic: Though the Later Sovereign was drowned among petty men, he was quite fond of recitation; as a child he had read poetry and fu and said to people, "Will there in the end be someone who understands how to make this art?

sentences.zh: 」及長，亦少留意。

translations.literal: " When he grew up he also gave it some attention.
translations.idiomatic: " When he grew up he gave it some attention as well.

sentences.zh: 初因畫屏風，敕通直郎蘭陵蕭放及晉陵王孝式錄古名賢烈士及近代輕豔諸詩以充圖畫，帝彌重之。

translations.literal: At first, because of painted screens, he ordered Unhampered Attendant Xiao Fang of Lanling and Wang Xiaoshi of Jinling to record ancient worthies, martyrs, and recent frivolous poems to fill the pictures; the emperor valued this all the more.
translations.idiomatic: At first, for painted screens, he ordered Unhampered Attendant Xiao Fang of Lanling and Wang Xiaoshi of Jinling to record ancient worthies, martyrs, and recent frivolous poems to fill the pictures; the emperor valued this still more.

sentences.zh: 後復追齊州錄事參軍蕭愨、趙州功曹參軍顏之推同入撰次，猶依霸朝，謂之館客。

translations.literal: Later he again summoned Qi province recorder-assistant Xiao Yi and Zhao province merit-clerk Yan Zhitui to enter and compile together, still following the hegemonic court—calling them lodge guests.
translations.idiomatic: Later he again summoned Qi recorder-assistant Xiao Yi and Zhao merit-clerk Yan Zhitui to compile together, still under the hegemonic court—calling them lodge guests.

sentences.zh: 放及之推意欲更廣其事，又祖珽輔政，愛重之推，又托鄧長颙漸說後主，屬意斯文。

translations.literal: Fang and Zhitui wished to broaden the affair further; Zu Ting was also assisting in government and cherished Zhitui; through Deng Changyong he gradually persuaded the Later Sovereign to set his mind on this literature.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and Zhitui wished to broaden the work further; Zu Ting was also assisting in government and cherished Zhitui; through Deng Changyong he gradually persuaded the Later Sovereign to set his mind on this literature.

sentences.zh: 三年，祖珽奏立文林館，於是更召引文學士，謂之待詔文林館焉。

translations.literal: In the third year Zu Ting memorialized to establish the Forest of Literature Hall; literary gentlemen were again summoned and called awaiting-edict gentlemen of the Forest of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Zu Ting memorialized to establish the Forest of Literature Hall; literary gentlemen were summoned again and called awaiting-edict gentlemen of the Forest of Literature.

sentences.zh: 珽又奏撰《御覽》，詔珽及特進魏收、太子太師徐之才、中書令崔劼、散騎常侍張雕、中書監陽休之監撰。

translations.literal: Ting again memorialized to compile the Imperial Overview; an edict ordered Ting and specially advanced Wei Shou, Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince Xu Zhicai, Secretariat Director Cui Jie, scattered-cavalry regular attendant Zhang Diao, and Secretariat Supervisor Yang Xiuzhi to supervise the compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Ting again memorialized to compile the Imperial Overview; an edict ordered Ting, specially advanced Wei Shou, Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince Xu Zhicai, Secretariat Director Cui Jie, scattered-cavalry regular attendant Zhang Diao, and Secretariat Supervisor Yang Xiuzhi to supervise it.

sentences.zh: 珽等奏追通直散騎侍郎韋道遜、陸乂、太子舍人王劭、衛尉丞李孝基、殿中侍御史魏澹、中散大夫劉仲威、袁奭、國子博士朱才、奉車都尉眭道閑、考功郎中崔子樞、左外兵郎薛道衡、幷省主客郎中盧思道、司空東閤祭酒崔德、太學博士諸葛漢、奉朝請鄭公超、殿中侍御史鄭子信等入館撰書，幷勑放、愨、之推等同入撰例。

translations.literal: Ting and the others memorialized to recall unhampered scattered-cavalry vice minister Wei Daoxun, Lu Yi, crown prince household retainer Wang Shao, commandery-wei aide Li Xiaoji, palace investigation censor Wei Tan, palace standard grandee Liu Zhongwei, Yuan Shuang, National University doctorate Zhu Cai, chariot-of-the-court commandant Sui Daoxian, merit-examination bureau director Cui Zishu, left outer-troops bureau gentleman Xue Daohang, joint-province guest-bureau director Lu Sidao, Minister of Works eastern-pavilion sacrifice wine Cui De, Grand Academy doctorate Zhuge Han, court gentleman attendant Zheng Gongchao, palace investigation censor Zheng Zixin, and others into the hall to compile books, and also ordered Fang, Yi, and Zhitui to enter the compilation rules together.
translations.idiomatic: Ting and the others memorialized to recall unhampered scattered-cavalry vice minister Wei Daoxun, Lu Yi, crown prince household retainer Wang Shao, commandery-wei aide Li Xiaoji, palace investigation censor Wei Tan, palace standard grandee Liu Zhongwei, Yuan Shuang, National University doctorate Zhu Cai, chariot-of-the-court commandant Sui Daoxian, merit-examination director Cui Zishu, left outer-troops gentleman Xue Daohang, joint-province guest-bureau director Lu Sidao, Minister of Works eastern-pavilion sacrifice wine Cui De, Grand Academy doctorate Zhuge Han, court gentleman attendant Zheng Gongchao, palace investigation censor Zheng Zixin, and others into the hall to compile, and also ordered Fang, Yi, and Zhitui to enter the compilation rules together.

sentences.zh: 復令散騎常侍封孝琰、前樂陵太守鄭元禮、衛尉少卿杜臺卿、通直散騎常侍王訓、前南兗州長史羊肅、通直散騎常侍馬元熙、幷省三公郎中劉瑉、開府行參軍李師上、溫君悠入館，亦令撰書。

translations.literal: They again ordered scattered-cavalry regular attendant Feng Xiaoyan, former music-commandery grand administrator Zheng Yuanli, commandery-wei vice director Du Taiqing, unhampered scattered-cavalry regular attendant Wang Xun, former southern Yanzhou chief clerk Yang Su, unhampered scattered-cavalry regular attendant Ma Yuanxi, joint-province three-offices bureau director Liu Min, opening-office acting retainer Li Shishang, and Wen Junyou into the hall, also to compile books.
translations.idiomatic: They again ordered scattered-cavalry regular attendant Feng Xiaoyan, former music-commandery administrator Zheng Yuanli, commandery-wei vice director Du Taiqing, unhampered scattered-cavalry regular attendant Wang Xun, former southern Yanzhou chief clerk Yang Su, unhampered scattered-cavalry regular attendant Ma Yuanxi, joint-province three-offices director Liu Min, opening-office acting retainer Li Shishang, and Wen Junyou into the hall, also to compile.

sentences.zh: 復命特進崔季舒、前仁州刺史劉逖、散騎常侍李孝貞、中書侍郎李德林續入待詔。

translations.literal: They again commanded specially advanced Cui Jishu, former Renzhou inspector Liu Ti, scattered-cavalry regular attendant Li Xiaozhen, and secretariat vice minister Li Delin to continue entering as awaiting-edict.
translations.idiomatic: They again commanded specially advanced Cui Jishu, former Renzhou inspector Liu Ti, scattered-cavalry regular attendant Li Xiaozhen, and secretariat vice minister Li Delin to continue entering as awaiting-edict.

sentences.zh: 尋又詔諸人各舉所知，又有前濟州長史李翥、前廣武太守魏騫、前西兗州司馬蕭溉、前幽州長史陸仁惠、鄭州司馬江旰、前通直散騎侍郎辛德源、陸開明、通直郎封孝謇、太尉掾張德沖、幷省右民郎高行恭、司徒戶曹參軍古道子、前司空功曹參軍劉顗、獲嘉令崔德儒、給事中李元楷、晉州治中陽師孝、太尉中兵參軍劉儒行、司空祭酒陽辟疆、司空士曹參軍盧公順、司徒中兵參軍周子深、開府參軍王友伯、崔君洽、魏師謇並入館待詔，又敕右僕射段孝言亦入焉。

translations.literal: Soon an edict also ordered each man to recommend those he knew; there were also former Jizhou chief clerk Li Xu, former Guangwu grand administrator Wei Qian, former western Yanzhou marshal Xiao Gai, former Youzhou chief clerk Lu Renhui, Zhengzhou marshal Jiang Gan, former unhampered scattered-cavalry vice minister Xin Deyuan, Lu Kaiming, unhampered gentleman Feng Xiaojie, grand marshal retainer Zhang Dechong, joint-province right-populace bureau gentleman Gao Xinggong, Secretariat household-census retainer Gu Daozi, former Minister of Works merit-clerk retainer Liu Yi, Huojia magistrate Cui Deru, giving-the-affairs attendant Li Yuankai, Jinzhou acting administrator Yang Shixiao, grand marshal central-troops retainer Liu Ruxing, Minister of Works sacrifice wine Yang Bijiang, Minister of Works scholar-census retainer Lu Gongshun, Secretariat central-troops retainer Zhou Zishen, opening-office retainer Wang Youbo, Cui Junqia, and Wei Shijian—all entered the hall as awaiting-edict; an edict also ordered right vice director of the masters of writing Duan Xiaoyan to enter as well.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered each man to recommend those he knew; there were also former Jizhou chief clerk Li Xu, former Guangwu administrator Wei Qian, former western Yanzhou marshal Xiao Gai, former Youzhou chief clerk Lu Renhui, Zhengzhou marshal Jiang Gan, former unhampered scattered-cavalry vice minister Xin Deyuan, Lu Kaiming, unhampered gentleman Feng Xiaojie, grand marshal retainer Zhang Dechong, joint-province right-populace gentleman Gao Xinggong, Secretariat household-census retainer Gu Daozi, former Minister of Works merit-clerk retainer Liu Yi, Huojia magistrate Cui Deru, giving-the-affairs attendant Li Yuankai, Jinzhou acting administrator Yang Shixiao, grand marshal central-troops retainer Liu Ruxing, Minister of Works sacrifice wine Yang Bijiang, Minister of Works scholar-census retainer Lu Gongshun, Secretariat central-troops retainer Zhou Zishen, opening-office retainer Wang Youbo, Cui Junqia, and Wei Shijian—all entered the hall as awaiting-edict; an edict also ordered right vice director of the masters of writing Duan Xiaoyan to enter.

sentences.zh: 《御覽》成後，所撰錄人亦有不時待詔，付所司處分者。

translations.literal: After the Imperial Overview was completed, among those recorded and compiled some did not await edict in time and were handed to the relevant office for disposition.
translations.idiomatic: After the Imperial Overview was completed, some of those recorded did not await edict in time and were handed to the relevant office for disposition.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸人，亦有文學膚淺，附會親識，妄相推薦者十三四焉。

translations.literal: Of all these men, some thirteen or fourteen in ten also had shallow literary learning, attached themselves to kin and acquaintances, and recklessly recommended one another.
translations.idiomatic: Of all these men, perhaps thirteen or fourteen in ten also had shallow literary learning, clung to kin and acquaintances, and recklessly pushed one another forward.

sentences.zh: 雖然，當時操筆之徒，搜求略盡。

translations.literal: Even so, those who wielded the brush at the time were sought out nearly to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, those who wielded the brush at the time were sought out almost to the last.

sentences.zh: 其外如廣平宋孝王、信都劉善經輩三數人，論其才性，入館諸賢亦十三四不逮之也。

translations.literal: Beyond them, such as Guangping Song Xiaowang and Xindu Liu Shanjing and a few others—in talent and nature, thirteen or fourteen in ten of the hall's worthies did not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond them, such as Guangping Song Xiaowang and Xindu Liu Shanjing and a few others—in talent and nature, thirteen or fourteen in ten of the hall's worthies did not match them.

sentences.zh: 待詔文林，亦是一時盛事，故存錄其姓名。

translations.literal: Awaiting edict at the Forest of Literature was also a grand affair of the age; therefore their names are preserved in the record.
translations.idiomatic: Awaiting edict at the Forest of Literature was itself a grand affair of the age; therefore their names are preserved here.

sentences.zh: 自邢子才以還，或身終魏朝，已入前史；

translations.literal: From Xing Zicai onward, some ended their lives in the Wei court and already entered the earlier histories;
translations.idiomatic: From Xing Zicai onward, some ended their lives in the Wei court and already entered the earlier histories;

sentences.zh: 或名位旣重，自有列傳；

translations.literal: some had name and rank already weighty and have their own separate biographies;
translations.idiomatic: some had name and rank already weighty and have their own biographies;

sentences.zh: 或附其家世；

translations.literal: some are attached to their family lines;
translations.idiomatic: some are attached to their family lines;

sentences.zh: 或名存後書，輒略而不載。

translations.literal: some have names preserved in later books—here they are briefly omitted from recording.
translations.idiomatic: some have names preserved in later books—here they are briefly omitted.

sentences.zh: 今綴序祖鴻勳等列於《文苑》者焉。

translations.literal: Now in sequence I set forth Zu Hongxun and those listed in Men of Letters.
translations.idiomatic: Now I set forth in sequence Zu Hongxun and those listed in Men of Letters.

sentences.zh: 自外有可錄者，存之篇末。

translations.literal: Beyond these, whatever can be recorded is kept at the chapter's end.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these, whatever can be recorded is kept at the chapter's end.

sentences.zh: 祖鴻勳，涿郡范陽人也。

translations.literal: Zu Hongxun was a man of Fanyang in Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Hongxun came from Fanyang in Zhuo commandery.

sentences.zh: 父慎，仕魏歷雁門、咸陽太守，治有能名。

translations.literal: His father Shen served Wei as grand administrator of Yanmen and Xianyang; in governance he had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen served Wei as grand administrator of Yanmen and Xianyang; in governance he had a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 卒於金紫光祿大夫，贈中書監、幽州刺史，諡惠侯。

translations.literal: He died as golden-gleaming grand master for splendid virtue, posthumously enfeoffed as Secretariat Supervisor and inspector of You province, with the posthumous title Marquis Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He died as golden-gleaming grand master for splendid virtue, posthumously enfeoffed as Secretariat Supervisor and inspector of You province, with the posthumous title Marquis Hui.

sentences.zh: 鴻勳弱冠與同郡盧文符並為州主簿。

translations.literal: At twenty sui Hongxun and Lu Wenfu of the same commandery together served as provincial recorder.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty sui Hongxun and Lu Wenfu of the same commandery together served as provincial recorder.

sentences.zh: 僕射臨淮王或表薦鴻勳有文學，宜試以一官，敕除奉朝請。

translations.literal: The vice director of the masters of writing, the Prince of Huaiyang, once memorialized recommending Hongxun for literary learning and that he should be tried in an office; an edict appointed him court gentleman attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Vice director of the masters of writing the Prince of Huaiyang once memorialized that Hongxun had literary learning and should be tried in office; an edict appointed him court gentleman attendant.

sentences.zh: 人謂之曰：「臨淮舉卿，便以得調，竟不相謝，恐非其宜。

translations.literal: Someone said to him, "The Prince of Huaiyang recommended you, and you immediately gained assignment—yet you never thanked him; I fear that is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to him, "The Prince of Huaiyang recommended you, and you immediately gained assignment—yet you never thanked him; I fear that is not fitting.

sentences.zh: 」鴻勳曰：「為國舉才，臨淮之務，祖鴻勳何事從而謝之？

translations.literal: " Hongxun said, "To recommend talent for the state is the Prince of Huaiyang's duty—what business has Zu Hongxun in following to thank him?
translations.idiomatic: " Hongxun said, "To recommend talent for the state is the Prince of Huaiyang's duty—what business has Zu Hongxun in following to thank him?

sentences.zh: 」彧聞而喜曰：「吾得其人矣。

translations.literal: " When Yu heard it he was pleased and said, "I have got my man."
translations.idiomatic: " When Yu heard it he was pleased and said, "I have got my man."

sentences.zh: 」及葛榮南逼，出為防河別將，守滑臺。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong pressed southward he went out as separate general defending the river and held Hua Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong pressed southward he went out as separate general defending the river and held Hua Terrace.

sentences.zh: 永安初，元羅為東道大使，署封隆之、邢邵、李渾、李象、鴻勳並為子使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an, Yuan Luo was eastern-route grand ambassador and appointed Feng Longzhi, Xing Shao, Li Hun, Li Xiang, and Hongxun all as deputy envoys.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yong'an, Yuan Luo was eastern-route grand ambassador and appointed Feng Longzhi, Xing Shao, Li Hun, Li Xiang, and Hongxun all as deputy envoys.

sentences.zh: 除東濟北太守，以父老疾為請，竟不之官。

translations.literal: He was appointed grand administrator of eastern Jibei; because his father was old and ill he requested leave and in the end did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand administrator of eastern Jibei; because his father was old and ill he requested leave and in the end did not take office.

sentences.zh: 後城陽王徽奏鴻勳為司徒法曹參軍事，赴洛，徽謂之曰：「吾聞臨淮相舉，竟不到門，今來何也？

translations.literal: Later the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, memorialized Hongxun as legal-affairs retainer in the Secretariat; he went to Luoyang, and Hui said to him, "I heard that when the Prince of Huaiyang recommended you, you never came to the door—why have you come now?
translations.idiomatic: Later the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, memorialized Hongxun as Secretariat legal-affairs retainer; he went to Luoyang, and Hui said to him, "I heard that when the Prince of Huaiyang recommended you, you never came to the door—why have you come now?

sentences.zh: 」鴻勳曰：「今來赴職，非為謝恩。

translations.literal: " Hongxun said, "I come now to take up duty, not to thank for favor."
translations.idiomatic: " Hongxun said, "I come now to take up duty, not to thank for favor."

sentences.zh: 」轉廷尉正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 後去官歸鄉里，與陽休之書曰：

translations.literal: Later he left office and returned to his native district; he wrote to Yang Xiuzhi:
translations.idiomatic: Later he left office and returned to his native district; he wrote to Yang Xiuzhi:

sentences.zh: 陽生大弟：吾比以家貧親老，時還故郡。

translations.literal: Elder Brother Yang: lately, because my family is poor and my parents old, I have from time to time returned to my home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Elder Brother Yang: lately, because my family is poor and my parents old, I have from time to time returned to my home commandery.

sentences.zh: 在本縣之西界，有雕山焉。

translations.literal: On the western border of this county there is Eagle Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On the western border of this county there is Eagle Mountain.

sentences.zh: 其處閑遠，水石清麗，高巖四匝，良田數頃。

translations.literal: The place is secluded and far, its waters and stones clear and lovely; high cliffs surround it on four sides, and good fields number several qing.
translations.idiomatic: The place is secluded and far; waters and stones are clear and lovely; high cliffs ring it on four sides, and good fields number several qing.

sentences.zh: 家先有野舍於斯，而遭亂荒廢，今復經始。

translations.literal: My family once had a rustic lodge there, but it fell to ruin in the turmoil; now I am building it anew.
translations.idiomatic: My family once had a rustic lodge there, but turmoil left it in ruins; now I am building it anew.

sentences.zh: 即石成基，憑林起棟。

translations.literal: Taking stone for foundation and leaning on the woods to raise beams.
translations.idiomatic: Taking stone for foundation and leaning on the woods to raise beams.

sentences.zh: 蘿生映宇，泉流繞階。

translations.literal: Creepers reflect on the eaves; springs wind around the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Creepers reflect on the eaves; springs wind around the steps.

sentences.zh: 月松風草，緣庭綺合；

translations.literal: Moon, pine, wind, and grass—along the courtyard, brocade pavilions;
translations.idiomatic: Moon, pine, wind, and grass—along the courtyard, brocade pavilions;

sentences.zh: 日華雲實，傍沼星羅。

translations.literal: sun's glory, clouds, and fruit—beside the pool, stars scattered.
translations.idiomatic: sun's glory, clouds, and fruit—beside the pool, stars scattered.

sentences.zh: 簷下流煙，共霄氣而舒卷；

translations.literal: Beneath the eaves drifting smoke rises and falls together with the sky's breath;
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the eaves drifting smoke rises and falls with the sky's breath;

sentences.zh: 園中桃李，雜椿柏而蔥茜。

translations.literal: in the garden peach and plum mix with cedar and cypress in verdant profusion.
translations.idiomatic: in the garden peach and plum mix with cedar and cypress in verdant profusion.

sentences.zh: 時一褰裳涉澗，負杖登峰，心悠悠以孤上，身飄飄而將逝，杳然不復自知在天地間矣。

translations.literal: From time to time I lift my robe and ford the stream, lean on my staff and climb the peak; my heart drifts lonely upward and my body seems about to float away—so remote that I no longer know myself to be between Heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: From time to time I lift my robe and ford the stream, lean on my staff and climb the peak; my heart drifts lonely upward and my body seems about to float away—so remote that I no longer know myself to stand between Heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 若此者久之，乃還所住，孤坐危石，撫琴對水，獨詠山阿，舉酒望月，聽風聲以興思，聞鶴唳以動懷。

translations.literal: When this had lasted long, I would return to where I dwelt, sit alone on a perilous rock, stroke the zither facing the water, chant alone on the mountain slope, raise my cup and gaze at the moon, listen to the wind's sound to stir thought and hear the crane's cry to move the breast.
translations.idiomatic: When this had lasted long, I would return to where I dwelt, sit alone on a perilous rock, stroke the zither facing the water, chant alone on the mountain slope, raise my cup and gaze at the moon, listen to the wind to stir thought and hear the crane's cry to move the breast.

sentences.zh: 企莊生之逍遙，慕尚子之清曠。

translations.literal: I look up to Master Zhuang's free wandering and admire Master Shang's clear expanse.
translations.idiomatic: I look up to Master Zhuang's free wandering and admire Master Shang's clear expanse.

sentences.zh: 首戴萌蒲，身衣缊襏，出藝粱稻，歸奉慈親，緩步當車，無事為貴，斯已適矣，豈必撫塵哉！

translations.literal: I wear on my head the budding sedge, on my body coarse cloth; going out I gather millet and grain, returning I serve my kindly parent; easy pace counts as carriage, having nothing to do is honor—this is already enough; must one brush the dust?
translations.idiomatic: I wear budding sedge on my head and coarse cloth on my body; going out I gather millet and grain, returning I serve my kindly parent; easy pace counts as carriage, having nothing to do is honor—this is already enough; must one brush the dust?

sentences.zh: 而吾生旣繫名聲之韁鎖，就良工之剞劂。

translations.literal: Yet my life is already bound by the bridle of fame and reputation and goes to the good artisan's carving.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my life is already bound by the bridle of fame and reputation and goes to the good artisan's carving.

sentences.zh: 振佩紫臺之上，鼓袖丹墀之下。

translations.literal: I shake my girdle-pendants above the Purple Terrace and beat my sleeves below the cinnabar steps.
translations.idiomatic: I shake my girdle-pendants above the Purple Terrace and beat my sleeves below the cinnabar steps.

sentences.zh: 采金匱之漏簡，訪玉山之遺文。

translations.literal: I gather leaking bamboo slips from the golden coffer and seek surviving texts from the jade mountain.
translations.idiomatic: I gather leaking bamboo slips from the golden coffer and seek surviving texts from the jade mountain.

sentences.zh: 敝精神於丘墳，盡心力於河漢。

translations.literal: I wear out spirit on the hill graves and exhaust mind on the Milky Way.
translations.idiomatic: I wear out spirit on the hill graves and exhaust mind on the Milky Way.

sentences.zh: 摛藻期之鞶繡，發議必在芬香。

translations.literal: When I weave ornament I expect brocade sashes; when I raise discourse it must be in fragrant words.
translations.idiomatic: When I weave ornament I expect brocade sashes; when I raise discourse it must be in fragrant words.

sentences.zh: 茲自美耳，吾無取焉。

translations.literal: This is beauty in itself—I have no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: That is beauty in itself—I have no part in it.

sentences.zh: 嘗試論之：夫崑峯積玉，光澤者前毀；

translations.literal: I once tried to discuss it: the Kunlun peak piles jade—the lustrous piece is destroyed first;
translations.idiomatic: I once tried to discuss it: the Kunlun peak piles jade—the lustrous piece is destroyed first;

sentences.zh: 瑤山叢桂，芳茂者先折。

translations.literal: the jade mountain clusters cassia—the fragrant and flourishing branch is broken first.
translations.idiomatic: the jade mountain clusters cassia—the fragrant flourishing branch is broken first.

sentences.zh: 是以東都有挂冕之臣，南國見捐情之士。

translations.literal: Therefore in the eastern capital there were ministers who hung up their caps; in the southern state there appeared gentlemen who cast away feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in the eastern capital there were ministers who hung up their caps; in the southern state there appeared gentlemen who cast away feeling.

sentences.zh: 斯豈惡粱錦，好蔬布哉？

translations.literal: Was this because they hated fine grain and brocade and loved coarse greens?
translations.idiomatic: Was that because they hated fine grain and brocade and loved coarse greens?

sentences.zh: 蓋欲保其七尺，終其百年耳。

translations.literal: They wished only to preserve their seven feet and complete their hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: They wished only to preserve their seven feet and complete their hundred years.

sentences.zh: 今弟官位旣達，聲華已遠，象由齒斃，膏用明煎，旣覽老氏谷神之談，應體留侯止足之逸。

translations.literal: Now younger brother, your office and rank are already advanced and your fame and splendor already far; the tusk is gone because the teeth perish, the fat is used because the lamp burns bright—you have already read Laozi's talk of the valley spirit and should embody Marquis Liu's rest in knowing when to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Now younger brother, your office and rank are already advanced and your fame and splendor already far; the tusk is gone because the teeth perish, the fat is used because the lamp burns bright—you have already read Laozi's talk of the valley spirit and should embody Marquis Liu's rest in knowing when to stop.

sentences.zh: 若能翻然清尚，解佩捐簪，則吾於茲山，莊可辦一。

translations.literal: If you can turn about to pure elevation, unfasten your girdle and cast aside your hairpin, then on this mountain of mine a lodge can be prepared at once.
translations.idiomatic: If you can turn about to pure elevation, unfasten your girdle and cast aside your hairpin, then on this mountain of mine a lodge can be prepared at once.

sentences.zh: 得把臂入林，掛巾垂枝，攜酒登巘，舒席平山，道素志，論舊款，訪丹法，語玄書，斯亦樂矣，何必富貴乎？

translations.literal: To link arms and enter the woods, hang the towel on drooping branches, carry wine and climb the height, spread mat on level mountain, speak plain resolve and discuss old friendship, inquire into cinnabar methods and converse on dark books—that too would be joy; why must one be rich and honored?
translations.idiomatic: To link arms and enter the woods, hang the towel on drooping branches, carry wine and climb the height, spread mat on level mountain, speak plain resolve and discuss old friendship, inquire into cinnabar methods and converse on dark books—that too would be joy; why must one be rich and honored?

sentences.zh: 去矣陽子，途乖趣別，緬尋此旨，杳若天漢。

translations.literal: Farewell, Master Yang—the road divides and our aims part; tracing this intent back, it is remote as the Milky Way.
translations.idiomatic: Farewell, Master Yang—the road divides and our aims part; tracing this intent back, it is remote as the Milky Way.

sentences.zh: 已矣哉，書不盡意。

translations.literal: It is over—writing cannot exhaust the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: It is over—writing cannot exhaust the meaning.

sentences.zh: 梁使將至，勑鴻勳對客。

translations.literal: When envoys from Liang were about to arrive, he was ordered to receive them as host.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys from Liang were due to arrive, the court ordered Hongxun to receive them.

sentences.zh: 高祖曾征至幷州，作《晉祠記》，好事者玩其文。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu had once campaigned as far as Bingzhou and composed the Record of the Jin Shrine; lovers of letters prized its prose.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu had once marched to Bingzhou and written the Record of the Jin Shrine, and men who cared for letters treasured its prose.

sentences.zh: 位至高陽太守，在官清素，妻子不免寒餒，時議高之。

translations.literal: He rose to Grand Administrator of Gaoyang. In office he was austere and pure; his wife and children could not escape cold and hunger, and opinion of the day held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Administrator of Gaoyang, where he served with austere integrity—so much so that his wife and children still knew cold and hunger—and contemporaries held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 天保初卒官。

translations.literal: At the opening of the Tianbao era he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era he died in office.

sentences.zh: 李廣，字弘基，范陽人也，其先自遼東徙焉。

translations.literal: Li Guang, styled Hongji, was a man of Fanyang; his ancestors had moved there from Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang, styled Hongji, was from Fanyang; his forebears had moved there from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 廣博涉群書，有才思文議之美，少與趙郡李謇齊名，為邢、魏之亞。

translations.literal: Guang read widely among the classics and possessed talent, reflection, and the beauty of literary discourse. In youth he shared fame with Li Jian of Zhao commandery, ranking just below Xing Shao and Wei Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Guang had read widely in the classics and possessed talent, reflection, and a gift for literary argument. In his youth he stood equal in reputation with Li Jian of Zhao commandery, second only to Xing Shao and Wei Shou.

sentences.zh: 而訥於言，敏於行。

translations.literal: Yet he was slow of speech and quick in action.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was slow of tongue and swift in deed.

sentences.zh: 魏安豐王延明鎮徐州，署廣長流參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince Anfeng of Wei Yuan Yanming guarded Xuzhou, he appointed Guang Senior Staff Officer for Current Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Anfeng of Wei, Yuan Yanming, held Xuzhou, he appointed Guang senior staff officer for current affairs.

sentences.zh: 釋褐蕩逆將軍。

translations.literal: At first appointment he was made Pacification General.
translations.idiomatic: On first entering service he was made Pacification General.

sentences.zh: 尒朱仲遠牒為大將軍記室，加諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhongyuan requisitioned him as Record Keeper to the Grand General with the additional title Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan summoned him as record keeper to the Grand General, with the additional title Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 荊州行臺辛纂上為行臺郎中，尋為車騎府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Xingzao of the Jingzhou frontier staff memorialized him up as Bureau Gentleman on the frontier staff; soon he was Recorder in the Office of the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzao of the Jingzhou frontier staff had him promoted to bureau gentleman on the staff; before long he was recorder in the Office of the Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 中尉崔暹精選御史，皆是世胄，廣獨以才學兼御史，修國史。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Cui Xuan rigorously selected censors—all were sons of noble houses; Guang alone, on learning and talent, was made censor while also editing the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Cui Xuan chose his censors with exacting care, and every appointee was a son of a noble house—Guang alone won the post on learning and talent, and while serving as censor he also edited the national history.

sentences.zh: 南臺文奏，多其辭也。

translations.literal: Most memorials from the Southern Terrace bore his phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the Southern Terrace's official documents carried his phrasing.

sentences.zh: 平陽公淹辟為中尉，轉侍御史。

translations.literal: Duke of Pingyang Yan appointed him vice censor; he was transferred to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Pingyang Yan appointed him vice censor, then transferred him to palace censor.

sentences.zh: 顯祖初嗣霸業，命掌書記。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xianzu's inheritance of the hegemony, Guang was ordered to keep the records.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu first took up the hegemony, Guang was ordered to keep the records.

sentences.zh: 天保初，欲以為中書郎，遇其病篤而止。

translations.literal: At the opening of Tianbao he was to be made Secretariat Gentleman, but the appointment stopped when his illness grew grave.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao he was to be made secretariat gentleman, but his illness turned grave and the appointment was set aside.

sentences.zh: 廣曾欲早朝，未明假寐，忽驚覺，謂其妻云：「吾向似睡，忽見一人出吾身中，語云：『君用心過苦，非精神所堪，今辭君去。

translations.literal: Once, going early to court before it was light, he dozed off and suddenly started awake, telling his wife: I seemed to be asleep when I saw a man come out of my body and say, Your mind works too hard—what the spirit cannot bear; I now take my leave of you.
translations.idiomatic: Once, on his way to early court while it was still dark, he dozed and suddenly started awake. He told his wife, "I seemed to sleep, then saw a man step out of my body and say, 'You tax your mind past what the spirit can bear—I now take my leave of you.'"

sentences.zh: 』」因而惚怳不樂，數日便遇疾，積年不起，資產屢空，藥石無繼。

translations.literal: From this he was confused and unhappy; within days he fell ill, and for years he could not rise. His assets were emptied again and again, and medicine ran out.
translations.idiomatic: After that he was dazed and low in spirit; within days he fell ill and for years could not rise. His household was emptied again and again, until there was no money left for medicine.

sentences.zh: 廣雅有鑒識，度量弘遠，坦平無私，為士流所愛，歲時共贍遺之，賴以自給。

translations.literal: Guang had fine discernment, broad magnanimity, and was level and unselfish; the gentry loved him, and each year they sent him gifts on which he relied to live.
translations.idiomatic: Guang had a keen eye, a wide measure, and a level hand without favor; men of standing loved him, and year by year they sent him gifts on which he managed to live.

sentences.zh: 竟以疾終。

translations.literal: In the end he died of his illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he died of his illness.

sentences.zh: 曾薦畢義雲於崔暹，廣卒後，義雲集其文筆十卷，托魏收為之敘。

translations.literal: He had once recommended Bi Yiyun to Cui Xuan. After Guang's death, Yiyun gathered ten juan of his writings and asked Wei Shou to write the preface.
translations.idiomatic: He had once recommended Bi Yiyun to Cui Xuan. After Guang's death, Yiyun gathered ten juan of his writings and entrusted Wei Shou to write the preface.

sentences.zh: 其族人子道亦有文章。

translations.literal: His clansman Zidao also had literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Zidao also wrote with distinction.

sentences.zh: 樊遜，字孝謙，河東北猗氏人也。

translations.literal: Fan Xun, styled Xiaoqian, was a man of Beiyi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xun, styled Xiaoqian, was from Beiyi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖琰，父衡，並無官宦。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan and his father Heng both held no office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan and his father Heng both held no office.

sentences.zh: 而衡性至孝，喪父，負土成墳，植柏方數十畝，朝夕號慕。

translations.literal: Heng was supremely filial. When his father died he carried earth to build the tomb mound and planted cypresses over several tens of mu, mourning morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was supremely filial. When his father died he carried earth to raise the mound and planted cypresses over several tens of mu, weeping morning and evening beside them.

sentences.zh: 遜少學，常為兄仲優饒。

translations.literal: Xun studied from youth, and his elder brother Zhong often provided for him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Xun studied from youth, and his elder brother Zhong often provided for him generously.

sentences.zh: 旣而自責曰：「名為人弟，獨受安逸，可不愧於心乎？

translations.literal: Then he blamed himself, saying: I am called a younger brother yet alone enjoy ease—can I not be ashamed before my own heart?
translations.idiomatic: Then he reproached himself: "I am called a younger brother, yet I alone enjoy ease—how can I not be ashamed before my own heart?"

sentences.zh: 」欲同勤事業。

translations.literal: He wished to share in the same toil and enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to share the same labor and ambition.

sentences.zh: 母馮氏謂之曰：「汝欲謹小行耶？

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Feng, said to him: Do you mean to keep only to petty circumspection?
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Feng, said to him, "Do you mean to keep only to petty circumspection?"

sentences.zh: 」遜感母言，遂專心典籍，恒書壁作「見賢思齊」四字，以自勸勉。

translations.literal: Moved by his mother's words, he devoted himself to the classics and constantly wrote on the wall the four characters see the worthy and think to emulate, to encourage himself.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his mother's words, he gave himself wholly to the classics and constantly wrote on the wall the four characters "see the worthy and think to emulate," to steel himself.

sentences.zh: 屬本州淪陷，寓居鄴中，為臨漳小史。

translations.literal: When his home commandery fell to the enemy he lodged in Ye and served as a minor clerk in Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When his home commandery fell to the enemy he lodged in Ye and served as a minor clerk in Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 縣令裴鑒蒞官清苦，致白雀等瑞，遜上《清德頌》十首。

translations.literal: Magistrate Pei Jian took office with austere integrity and brought forth omens such as the white sparrow; Xun submitted ten pieces of the Ode to Pure Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Pei Jian took office with austere integrity and drew forth omens such as the white sparrow; Xun submitted ten pieces of the Ode to Pure Virtue.

sentences.zh: 鑒大加賞重，擢為主簿，仍薦之於右僕射崔暹，與遼東李廣、渤海封孝琰等為暹賓客。

translations.literal: Jian greatly valued and promoted him to chief clerk, and still recommended him to Right Vice-Director Cui Xuan, together with Li Guang of Liaodong and Feng Xiaoyan of Bohai, as Xuan's literary guests.
translations.idiomatic: Jian prized him greatly, promoted him to chief clerk, and recommended him to Right Vice-Director Cui Xuan—together with Li Guang of Liaodong and Feng Xiaoyan of Bohai—as one of Xuan's literary guests.

sentences.zh: 人有譏其靖默不能趣時者。

translations.literal: Some mocked him for his quiet demeanor and failure to chase the times.
translations.idiomatic: Some mocked his quiet manner and his refusal to chase the fashion of the hour.

sentences.zh: 遜常服東方朔之言，陸沉世俗，避世金馬，何必深山蒿廬之下，遂借陸沉公子為主人，擬《客難》，制《客誨》以自廣。

translations.literal: Xun often took to heart Dongfang Shuo's words about lying low in the world and avoiding the world at the Golden Horse Gate—why must one be beneath deep mountains and thatched huts? He therefore borrowed the name Lord Lying Low as host, modeled on the Guest's Difficulty, and composed the Guest's Reproach to enlarge his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Xun often took to heart Dongfang Shuo's counsel about lying low in the world and keeping to the Golden Horse Gate to avoid the age—why must one hide only in deep mountains and thatched huts? He therefore borrowed the name Lord Lying Low as his host, modeled on the Guest's Difficulty, and wrote the Guest's Reproach to give his meaning room.

sentences.zh: 後崔暹大會賓客，大司馬、襄城王元旭時亦在坐，論欲命府僚。

translations.literal: Later, when Cui Xuan held a great gathering of guests, the Grand Marshal, Prince of Xiangcheng Yuan Xu, was also present, and they discussed whom to appoint to the prince's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Cui Xuan held a great gathering of guests, Grand Marshal Prince of Xiangcheng Yuan Xu was also seated there, and they discussed whom to appoint to the prince's staff.

sentences.zh: 暹指遜曰：「此人學富才高，兼之佳行，可為王參軍也。

translations.literal: Xuan pointed at Xun and said: This man's learning is rich and his talent high; add his fine conduct—he can serve as the prince's army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan pointed at Xun and said, "This man's learning is deep and his talent high, and his conduct is fine besides—he can serve as the prince's army adviser."

sentences.zh: 」旭目之曰：「豈能就耶？

translations.literal: Xu looked at him and said: Could he really take the post?
translations.idiomatic: Xu looked him over and said, "Could he really take such a post?"

sentences.zh: 」遜曰：「家無蔭第，不敢當此。

translations.literal: Xun said: My house has no hereditary stipend; I dare not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: Xun said, "My house has no hereditary stipend—I dare not accept this."

sentences.zh: 」武定七年，世宗崩，暹徙於邊裔，賓客咸散，遜遂往陳留而居之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wuding the Emperor passed away; Xuan was moved to the frontier marches and his guests all scattered, and Xun went to live in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Wuding the Emperor passed away; Xuan was sent to the frontier marches and his guests scattered, and Xun went to settle in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史劉殺鬼以遜兼錄事參軍，仍舉秀才。

translations.literal: Liu Shagui, governor of Liangzhou, made Xun concurrent recorder and also nominated him as xiucai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shagui, governor of Liangzhou, made Xun concurrent recorder and also nominated him as xiucai.

sentences.zh: 尚書案舊令，下州三載一舉秀才，為五年已貢開封人鄭祖獻，計至此年未合，兼別駕王聰抗議，右丞陽斐不能卻。

translations.literal: The old rule of the Secretariat held that each lower province presented xiucai once every three years; it had been five years since Kaifeng man Zheng Zuxian was sent up, and by the count this year did not qualify. Vice Governor Wang Cong protested, and Right Assistant Director Yang Fei could not refute him.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat's old rule held that each lower province presented xiucai once every three years; five years had already passed since Kaifeng man Zheng Zuxian was sent up, and by the count this year did not qualify. Vice Governor Wang Cong protested, and Right Assistant Director Yang Fei could not set his protest aside.

sentences.zh: 尚書令高隆之曰：「雖遜才學優異，待明年仕非遠。

translations.literal: Shangshu Ling Gao Longzhi said: Though Xun's learning and talent are outstanding, to wait until next year for office is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: Shangshu Ling Gao Longzhi said, "Though Xun's learning and talent are outstanding, to wait until next year for office is not far."

sentences.zh: 」遜竟還本州。

translations.literal: Xun in the end returned to his home province.
translations.idiomatic: Xun in the end returned to his home province.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉兼長史，從軍南討。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to concurrent chief clerk and followed the army on the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to concurrent chief clerk and followed the army on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 軍還，殺鬼移任潁川，又引遜兼潁州長史。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Shagui was moved to Yingchuan and again drew Xun as concurrent chief clerk of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Shagui was moved to Yingchuan and again drew Xun as concurrent chief clerk of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 天保元年，本州復召舉秀才。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao his home province again summoned him as xiucai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao his home province again summoned him as xiucai.

sentences.zh: 二年春，會朝堂對策罷，中書郎張子融奏入。

translations.literal: In the second year, spring, after the palace examination and policy response ended, Secretariat Gentleman Zhang Zirong memorialized his entry.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, in spring, after the palace examination and policy response had ended, Secretariat Gentleman Zhang Zirong memorialized his entry.

sentences.zh: 至四年五月，遜與定州秀才李子宣等以對策三年不調，被付外，上書請從聞罷，詔不報。

translations.literal: By the fourth year, fifth month, Xun and Dingzhou xiucai Li Zixuan and others, because three years had passed since the policy response without appointment, were sent outside the ranks; they memorialized asking that their cases be heard and dismissed, but the edict gave no reply.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth year, in the fifth month, Xun and Dingzhou xiucai Li Zixuan and others—because three years had passed since the policy response without appointment—were sent outside the ranks. They memorialized asking that their cases be heard and dismissed, but the edict gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 梁州重表舉遜為秀才。

translations.literal: Liangzhou again memorialized Xun as xiucai.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou again memorialized Xun as xiucai.

sentences.zh: 五年正月制詔問升中紀號，遜對曰：

translations.literal: In the fifth year, first month, an imperial edict questioned the title for ascending the central peak; Xun answered:
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, in the first month, an imperial edict questioned the title for ascending the central peak; Xun answered:

sentences.zh: 臣聞巡嶽之禮，勒在《虞書》，省方之義，著於《易象》。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the rite of touring the sacred peaks is engraved in the Document of Yu, and the meaning of surveying the regions is set forth in the Images of the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that the rite of touring the sacred peaks is cut into the Document of Yu, and the meaning of surveying the regions is set forth in the Images of the Changes.

sentences.zh: 往帝前王，匪唯一姓，封金刊玉，億有餘人。

translations.literal: Former emperors and early kings were not of a single surname; those who sealed gold and carved jade number more than a hundred million.
translations.idiomatic: Former emperors and early kings were not of a single surname; those who sealed gold and carved jade number beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 仲尼之觀梁甫，不能盡識；

translations.literal: When Zhongni viewed Liangfu he could not know them all;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongni viewed Liangfu he could not know them all;

sentences.zh: 夷吾之對齊桓，所存未幾。

translations.literal: what Guan Zhong answered Duke Huan of Qi preserved was only a few.
translations.idiomatic: what Guan Zhong answered Duke Huan of Qi preserved was only a few.

sentences.zh: 然盛德之事，必待太平，茍非其人，更貽靈譴。

translations.literal: Yet the deed of greatest virtue must await great peace; if it is not the right man, it only invites spiritual punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the deed of greatest virtue must await great peace; if it is not the right man, it only invites spiritual punishment.

sentences.zh: 秦皇無道，致雨風之災；

translations.literal: Qin Huang was without the Way and brought the disaster of rain and wind;
translations.idiomatic: Qin Huang was without the Way and brought the disaster of rain and wind;

sentences.zh: 漢武奢淫，有奉車之害。

translations.literal: Han Wu was extravagant and licentious and suffered the harm of the carriage that bore his coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wu was extravagant and licentious and suffered the harm of the carriage that bore his coffin.

sentences.zh: 及文叔受命，炎精更輝，四海安流，天下輯睦，劍賜騎士，馬駕鼓車，乃用張純之文，始從伯陽之說。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wendi received the Mandate the flame of Han shone anew; the four seas flowed in peace and the realm was united. Swords were bestowed on knights and horses yoked to the drum carriage—only then did he use Zhang Chun's text and begin to follow Boyang's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wendi received the Mandate the flame of Han shone anew; the four seas flowed in peace and the realm was united. Swords were bestowed on knights and horses yoked to the drum carriage—only then did he use Zhang Chun's text and begin to follow Boyang's teaching.

sentences.zh: 至於魏、晉，雖各有君，量德而處，莫能擬議。

translations.literal: As for Wei and Jin, though each had its ruler, they measured virtue and took their place and none could be compared in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: As for Wei and Jin, though each had its ruler, they measured virtue and took their place, and none could be compared in such deliberation.

sentences.zh: 蔣濟上言於前，徒穢紙墨；

translations.literal: Jiang Ji memorialized before and only soiled paper and ink;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji's memorial came before and only soiled paper and ink;

sentences.zh: 袁準發論於後，終未施行。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhun issued his treatise after and in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhun's treatise came after and in the end was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 世歷三朝，年將十祀，啟聖之期，茲為昌會。

translations.literal: The age has passed through three courts and the years approach ten reign-periods; the season of opening sagehood is now this splendid assembly.
translations.idiomatic: The age has passed through three courts and the years approach ten reign-periods; the season of opening sagehood is now this splendid assembly.

sentences.zh: 然自水德不競，函谷封途，天馬息歌，苞茅絕貢。

translations.literal: Yet since the power of water ceased to contend, the passes of Hangu were sealed; the heavenly horse ceased its song and the tribute of thatched bundles was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since the power of water ceased to contend, the passes of Hangu were sealed; the heavenly horse ceased its song and the tribute of thatched bundles was cut off.

sentences.zh: 我太祖收寶雞之瑞，握鳳皇之書，體一德以匡朝，屈三分而事主，蕩此妖寇，易如沃雪。

translations.literal: Our Grand Ancestor gathered the omen of the treasure cock and grasped the book of the phoenix, with one virtue to set the court aright and bowing to three parts to serve his lord, scattering these demon bands as easily as pouring boiling water on snow.
translations.idiomatic: Our Grand Ancestor gathered the omen of the treasure cock and grasped the book of the phoenix, with one virtue to set the court aright and bowing to three parts to serve his lord, scattering these demon bands as easily as pouring boiling water on snow.

sentences.zh: 但昌旣受命，發乃行誅，雖太白出高，中國宜戰，置之度外，望其遷善。

translations.literal: But when Chang received the Mandate, Fa then carried out punishment; though the Great White rose high and the Central Land ought to fight, he set it outside his measure and looked for them to turn to goodness.
translations.idiomatic: But when Chang received the Mandate, Fa then carried out punishment; though the Great White rose high and the Central Land ought to fight, he set it outside his measure and looked for them to turn to goodness.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下以神武之姿，天然之略，馬多冀北，將異山西，涼風至，白露下，北上太行，東臨碣石，方欲吞巴蜀而掃崤函，苑長洲而池江漢。

translations.literal: I bow before Your Majesty's divine martial bearing and heaven-given strategy—horses many as in Jibei, generals unlike those of Shanxi; when the cool wind comes and white dew falls, you will march north to the Taihang and east to Jieshi, about to swallow Ba-Shu and sweep Xiao-Han, to park Long Isle and pool the Jiang-Han.
translations.idiomatic: I bow before Your Majesty's divine martial bearing and heaven-given strategy—horses many as in Jibei, generals unlike those of Shanxi; when the cool wind comes and white dew falls, you will march north to the Taihang and east to Jieshi, about to swallow Ba-Shu and sweep Xiao-Han, to park Long Isle and pool the Jiang-Han.

sentences.zh: 復恐迎風縱火，芝艾共焚，按此六軍，未申九伐。

translations.literal: Yet I fear that if we meet the wind and set the fire, wormwood and mugwort will burn together; if we press these six armies, the nine punishments will not be declared.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I fear that if we meet the wind and set the fire, wormwood and mugwort will burn together; if we press these six armies, the nine punishments will not be declared.

sentences.zh: 夫周發牙璋，漢馳竹使，義在濟民，非聞好戰。

translations.literal: When Zhou Fa sent the jade tally and Han dispatched the bamboo envoy, the meaning lay in succoring the people, not in love of war.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Fa sent the jade tally and Han dispatched the bamboo envoy, the meaning lay in succoring the people, not in love of war.

sentences.zh: 至如投鼠忌器之說，蓋是常談；

translations.literal: As for the saying about casting at a rat and fearing the vessel, that is common talk;
translations.idiomatic: As for the saying about casting at a rat and fearing the vessel, that is common talk;

sentences.zh: 文德懷遠之言，豈識權道。

translations.literal: the words about civil virtue embracing the distant do not know expedient policy.
translations.idiomatic: the words about civil virtue embracing the distant do not know expedient policy.

sentences.zh: 今三臺令子，六郡良家，蓄銳須時，裹糧待詔。

translations.literal: Now the sons of the Three Terraces and the good families of the six commanderies store their edge and wait for the hour, wrap their grain and await the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sons of the Three Terraces and the good families of the six commanderies store their edge and wait for the hour, wrap their grain and await the edict.

sentences.zh: 未若龍駕虎服，先收隴右之民，電轉雷驚，因取荊南之地。

translations.literal: Better to drive the dragon carriage in tiger garb, first gather the people of Longyou, turn like lightning and startle like thunder, and then take the lands of southern Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Better to drive the dragon carriage in tiger garb, first gather the people of Longyou, turn like lightning and startle like thunder, and then take the lands of southern Jing.

sentences.zh: 昔秦舉長平，金精食昴，楚攻鉅鹿，枉矢霄流，況我威靈，能無協贊。

translations.literal: In old times Qin raised Changping and the metal essence devoured Mao; Chu attacked Julu and the crooked arrow streamed across the sky—how much more, with our majesty and spirit, can there be no concerted aid?
translations.idiomatic: In old times Qin raised Changping and the metal essence devoured Mao; Chu attacked Julu and the crooked arrow streamed across the sky—how much more, with our majesty and spirit, can there be no concerted aid?

sentences.zh: 但使彼之百姓，一睹六軍，似見周王，若逢司隸。

translations.literal: Only let their common people once behold the six armies—they will seem to see the King of Zhou, or to meet the Minister of Correction.
translations.idiomatic: Only let their common people once behold the six armies—they will seem to see the King of Zhou, or to meet the Minister of Correction.

sentences.zh: 然後除其苛令，與其約法，振旅而還，止戈為武，標金南海，勒石東山，紀天地之奇功，被風聲於千載。

translations.literal: Then remove their harsh orders and give them your compact laws, shake the ranks and return, halt the weapons and make martial virtue a name only, plant the golden marker on the southern sea and carve stone on the eastern mountain, recording heaven and earth's strange achievement and spreading your wind-sound for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Then remove their harsh orders and give them your compact laws, shake the ranks and return, halt the weapons and make martial virtue a name only, plant the golden marker on the southern sea and carve stone on the eastern mountain, recording heaven and earth's strange achievement and spreading your renown for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 若令馬皃不死，子陽尚在，便欲案明堂之圖，草射牛之禮，比德論功，多慚往列，升中告禪，臣用有疑。

translations.literal: If Ma Huang were not dead and Ziyang still stood, you would then consult the diagram of the Bright Hall and draft the rite of shooting the ox, comparing virtue and discussing merit—you would be shamed beside the men of old. To ascend the central peak and announce fengshan—your servant has doubts.
translations.idiomatic: If Ma Huang were not dead and Ziyang still stood, you would then consult the diagram of the Bright Hall and draft the rite of shooting the ox, comparing virtue and discussing merit—you would be shamed beside the men of old. To ascend the central peak and announce fengshan—your servant has doubts.

sentences.zh: 又問求才審官，遜對曰：

translations.literal: He was again questioned on seeking talent and examining office; Xun answered:
translations.idiomatic: He was again questioned on seeking talent and examining office; Xun answered:

sentences.zh: 臣聞雕獸畫龍，徒有風雲之勢；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that carved beasts and painted dragons have only the air of wind and clouds;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that carved beasts and painted dragons have only the air of wind and clouds;

sentences.zh: 金舟玉馬，終無水陸之功。

translations.literal: golden boats and jade horses in the end have no achievement on water or land.
translations.idiomatic: golden boats and jade horses in the end have no achievement on water or land.

sentences.zh: 三駕禮賢，將收實用，一毛不拔，復何足取。

translations.literal: Three times to drive the carriage and honor the worthy is to gather what is truly useful; one hair not plucked—what is there to take?
translations.idiomatic: Three times to drive the carriage and honor the worthy is to gather what is truly useful; one hair not plucked—what is there to take?

sentences.zh: 是以堯作虞賓，遂全箕山之操；

translations.literal: Therefore Yao made Yu guest and thereby preserved the conduct of Mount Ji;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Yao made Yu guest and thereby preserved the conduct of Mount Ji;

sentences.zh: 周移商鼎，不納孤竹之言。

translations.literal: Zhou moved the tripod of Shang and did not admit the words of the lone bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou moved the tripod of Shang and did not admit the words of the lone bamboo.

sentences.zh: 但處土盜名，雖云久矣；

translations.literal: Yet recluses who steal a name have long been so;
translations.idiomatic: Yet recluses who steal a name have long been so;

sentences.zh: 朝臣竊位，蓋亦實多。

translations.literal: court ministers who usurp place are also truly many.
translations.idiomatic: court ministers who usurp place are also truly many.

sentences.zh: 漢拜丞相，便有鐘鼓之妖；

translations.literal: When Han invested the chief minister, there was at once the omen of bells and drums;
translations.idiomatic: When Han invested the chief minister, there was at once the omen of bells and drums;

sentences.zh: 魏用三公，乃致孫權之笑。

translations.literal: when Wei used the Three Dukes, it brought Sun Quan's laughter.
translations.idiomatic: when Wei used the Three Dukes, it brought Sun Quan's laughter.

sentences.zh: 故山林之與朝廷，得容非毀；

translations.literal: Thus mountain forest and court can each tolerate blame and praise;
translations.idiomatic: Thus mountain forest and court can each tolerate blame and praise;

sentences.zh: 肥遁之與賓王，翻有優劣。

translations.literal: fat reclusion and honored guest in turn have their better and worse.
translations.idiomatic: fat reclusion and honored guest in turn have their better and worse.

sentences.zh: 至於時非蹈海，而曰羞作秦民；

translations.literal: As for times that were not crossing the sea yet saying it shames one to be a subject of Qin;
translations.idiomatic: As for times that were not crossing the sea yet saying it shames one to be a subject of Qin;

sentences.zh: 事異出關，而言恥從衛亂。

translations.literal: affairs unlike leaving the passes yet speaking of shame at following Wei's disorder.
translations.idiomatic: affairs unlike leaving the passes yet speaking of shame at following Wei's disorder.

sentences.zh: 雖復星干帝座，不易高尚之心；

translations.literal: Though the stars trespass on the Emperor's seat, they do not alter a heart set on loftiness;
translations.idiomatic: Though the stars trespass on the Emperor's seat, they do not alter a heart set on loftiness;

sentences.zh: 月犯少微，終存耿介之志。

translations.literal: though the moon offends the Lesser Apex, they still keep a straight and unyielding will.
translations.idiomatic: though the moon offends the Lesser Apex, they still keep a straight and unyielding will.

sentences.zh: 自我太嶽之後，克廣洪業，禹至神宗，舜格文祖。

translations.literal: Since our Grand Ancestor, we have broadened the great enterprise—from Yu reaching the Divine Ancestor, from Shun matching the Literary Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Since our Grand Ancestor, we have broadened the great enterprise—from Yu reaching the Divine Ancestor, from Shun matching the Literary Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 陛下受天之明命，光華日月，爰自納麓，乃格文祖，儀天地以設官，象星辰而布職。

translations.literal: Your Majesty received heaven's bright mandate, your glory eclipsing sun and moon; from accepting the regency you matched the Literary Ancestor, taking heaven and earth as model to set offices and stars as image to spread duties.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty received heaven's bright mandate, your glory eclipsing sun and moon; from accepting the regency you matched the Literary Ancestor, taking heaven and earth as model to set offices and stars as image to spread duties.

sentences.zh: 漢家神鳳，慚用紀年；

translations.literal: Han of the Divine Phoenix was shamed to use it only for chronology;
translations.idiomatic: Han of the Divine Phoenix was shamed to use it only for chronology;

sentences.zh: 魏氏青龍，羞將改號。

translations.literal: Wei of the Blue Dragon was ashamed to change the reign title.
translations.idiomatic: Wei of the Blue Dragon was ashamed to change the reign title.

sentences.zh: 上膺列宿，咸是異人；

translations.literal: Above you answer to the arrayed stars—all are uncommon men;
translations.idiomatic: Above you answer to the arrayed stars—all are uncommon men;

sentences.zh: 下法山川，莫非奇士。

translations.literal: below you take mountains and rivers as law—none are not strange knights.
translations.idiomatic: below you take mountains and rivers as law—none are not strange knights.

sentences.zh: 所以畫堂甲觀，修德日新，廟鼎歌鐘，王勳歲委。

translations.literal: Therefore in the painted hall and armored watchtower virtue is renewed day by day; in the temple cauldrons and singing bells royal merit is entrusted year by year.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in the painted hall and armored watchtower virtue is renewed day by day; in the temple cauldrons and singing bells royal merit is entrusted year by year.

sentences.zh: 循名責實，選衆舉能，朝無銅臭之公，世絕《錢神》之論。

translations.literal: Match names to realities, choose from the multitude and raise the able; let the court have no grandees who reek of copper, and the age be rid of discourse on the Money God.
translations.idiomatic: Match titles to what men truly are; choose widely and promote talent, until no grandee at court smells of coin and the age has done with talk of the Money God.

sentences.zh: 昔百里相秦，名存《雀籙》；

translations.literal: In old times Baili Xi served Qin, and his name survives in the Sparrow Register;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Baili Xi became minister of Qin, and his name still lives in the Sparrow Register;

sentences.zh: 蕭、張輔沛，姓在《河書》。

translations.literal: Xiao He and Zhang Liang aided Pei, and their surnames stand in the River Chart.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He and Zhang Liang helped found Han at Pei, and their houses are written in the River Chart.

sentences.zh: 今日公卿，抑亦天授，與之為治，何欲不從。

translations.literal: Today's ministers and grandees are likewise heaven's gift; to govern with them, what wish would not be followed?
translations.idiomatic: The high ministers of today are heaven's gift as well; rule beside them, and what desire would go unmet?

sentences.zh: 未必稽首天師，方聞牧馬之術；

translations.literal: One need not kowtow to the Celestial Master to hear the art of tending horses;
translations.idiomatic: You need not kowtow to a Celestial Master before you may hear how to tend horses;

sentences.zh: 膝行山上，始得治身之道。

translations.literal: nor crawl on one's knees up a mountain to obtain the way of ordering the self.
translations.idiomatic: nor crawl on your knees up a mountain before you learn how to order your own life.

sentences.zh: 但使帝德休明，自強不息，甲夜觀書，支日通奏。

translations.literal: Only let the emperor's virtue be radiant and unceasing in self-strengthening, reading at the first watch of night and passing memorials through the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: Let the emperor's virtue shine clear and his resolve never slacken—books open at the first watch of night, memorials flowing the whole day through.

sentences.zh: 周昌桀、紂之論，欣然開納；

translations.literal: Zhou Chang's argument likening the ruler to Jie and Zhou—gladly accept it;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Chang compares the throne to Jie and Zhou, welcome the words gladly;

sentences.zh: 劉毅桓、靈之比，終自含弘。

translations.literal: Liu Yi's comparison to Huan and Ling—in the end bear it with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: when Liu Yi compares you to Huan and Ling, in the end swallow the sting and show forbearance.

sentences.zh: 高懸王爵，唯能是與，管庫靡遺，漁鹽畢錄。

translations.literal: Hang high the royal ranks and give them only to the able; let no storehouse clerk be passed over, nor any salt-gatherer or fisherman left unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: Hang the royal ranks high and grant them only to the capable; leave no clerk of the granaries overlooked, no fisherman or salt-worker unlisted.

sentences.zh: 無令桓譚非讖，官止於郡丞；

translations.literal: Do not let Huan Tan, for rejecting prophecy, stop at county aide;
translations.idiomatic: Do not let a Huan Tan, punished for rejecting prophecy, die a county aide;

sentences.zh: 趙壹負才，位終於計掾。

translations.literal: nor Zhao Yi, for bearing talent, end as a clerical recorder.
translations.idiomatic: nor a Zhao Yi, rich in talent, end his days as a petty recorder.

sentences.zh: 則天下宅心，幽明知感，歲精仕漢，風伯朝周，真人去而復歸，臺星坼而還斂，《詩》稱多士，《易》載群龍，從此而言，可以無愧。

translations.literal: Then all under Heaven will turn their hearts, dark and bright will know and respond, the year-spirit will serve Han and the wind-lord attend Zhou, the true man will depart and return, the terrace star split and gather again; the Odes praise many officers, the Changes records a host of dragons—from this, one may be without shame.
translations.idiomatic: Then the realm will give you its heart, spirits dark and bright will answer, omens will align as in Han and Zhou of old, sage and star will return to their courses, the Odes will again praise a multitude of men, the Changes a throng of dragons—and on that score, Your Majesty, you need not blush.

sentences.zh: 又問釋道兩教，遜對曰：

translations.literal: He was again asked about the two teachings, Buddhism and Daoism; Xun replied:
translations.idiomatic: He was questioned next on the two teachings, Buddhism and Daoism. Xun answered:

sentences.zh: 臣聞天道性命，聖人所不言，蓋以理絕涉求，難為稱謂，伯陽道德之論，莊周逍遙之旨，遺言取意，猶有可尋。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the Way of Heaven and fate-nature are what sages do not speak of, because the principle cuts off involvement and is hard to name; yet in Laozi's discourse on the Way and in Zhuangzi's doctrine of free wandering, if one takes the drift of what was left behind, something may still be sought.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the Way of Heaven and the matter of fate are what the sages leave unspoken—the principle lies beyond grasp, hard to put into words.
