Still, in Laozi's talk of the Way and Zhuangzi's teaching of free wandering, if one reads for the meaning behind the words, something can be found.

sentences.zh: 至若玉簡金書，神經秘錄，三尺九轉之奇，絳雪玄霜之異，淮南成道，犬吠雲中，子喬得仙，劍飛天上，皆是憑虛之說。

translations.literal: As for jade slips and golden books, secret scriptures and hidden records, the marvel of the nine-turn rod three feet long, the wonder of crimson snow and dark frost—when Huainan achieved the Way, dogs barked in the clouds; when Prince Qiao gained immortality, swords flew in the sky—all are tales that lean on emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: But jade slips and golden books, secret canon and hidden lore—the three-foot rod turned nine times, elixirs of crimson snow and dark frost—when the King of Huainan 'attained the Way,' dogs were said to bark in the clouds; when Prince Qiao 'became immortal,' swords were said to fly in the sky. These are stories that lean on thin air.

sentences.zh: 海棗之談，求之如係風，學之如捕影。

translations.literal: Talk of sea dates and such—seek it like tying the wind, study it like catching a shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Talk of sea-dates and the like is like trying to tie down the wind, or study it like chasing a shadow.

sentences.zh: 而燕君、齊後，秦皇、漢帝，信彼方士，冀遇其真。

translations.literal: Yet the lords of Yan and Qi, the First Emperor of Qin and the Han emperors trusted those masters of the methods and hoped to meet the true.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rulers of Yan and Qi, the First Emperor of Qin, and the Han emperors trusted such masters and hoped to meet the Real.

sentences.zh: 徐福去而不歸，欒大往而無獲。

translations.literal: Xu Fu went away and did not return; Luan Da went and obtained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu sailed away and never came back; Luan Da went forth and brought back nothing.

sentences.zh: 猶謂升遐倒影，抵掌可期；

translations.literal: Still they believed that ascending in the far reflection and clapping hands could be expected soon;
translations.idiomatic: Still they believed that to rise in the far reflection and clap their hands was something they could expect any day;

sentences.zh: 祭鬼求神，庶或不死。

translations.literal: that sacrificing to ghosts and seeking spirits might perhaps grant no death.
translations.idiomatic: that if they sacrificed to ghosts and besought the spirits, they might somehow escape death.

sentences.zh: 江璧旣返，還入驪山之墓；

translations.literal: When the river jewel was returned, it entered the tomb on Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: When the river jewel was 'returned,' it only entered the tomb on Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 龍媒已至，終下茂陵之墳。

translations.literal: when the dragon steed arrived, it ended beneath the mound at Maoling.
translations.idiomatic: when the dragon steed 'arrived,' it ended beneath the mound at Maoling.

sentences.zh: 方知劉向之信洪寶，沒有餘責；

translations.literal: Then one knows that Liu Xiang's faith in the great treasure left him no surplus of blame;
translations.idiomatic: Then one sees that Liu Xiang, who believed in the great treasure, was left with no surplus of excuse;

sentences.zh: 王充之非黃帝，比為不相。

translations.literal: and Wang Chong's rejection of the Yellow Emperor was, by comparison, not far off.
translations.idiomatic: and that Wang Chong, who rejected the Yellow Emperor legend, was not so far wrong.

sentences.zh: 又末葉已來，大存佛教，寫經西土，畫像南宮。

translations.literal: Moreover, in recent generations Buddhism has greatly flourished: scriptures copied in the western lands, images painted in the southern palace.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages, moreover, Buddhism has grown vast—scriptures copied from the western lands, images painted in the southern palace.

sentences.zh: 昆池地黑，以為燒劫之灰；

translations.literal: The Kunming pool's black earth was taken as ash of the burnt kalpa;
translations.idiomatic: The black earth of the Kunming Pool was taken for the ash of a cosmic burn;

sentences.zh: 春秋夜明，謂是降神之日。

translations.literal: a bright night in spring and autumn was called the day spirits descended.
translations.idiomatic: a night in spring or autumn when the sky stayed bright was called the day the gods came down.

sentences.zh: 法王自在，變化無窮，置世界於微塵，納須彌於黍米。

translations.literal: The Dharma-king is free and changes without end, setting the world in a mote of dust and fitting Mount Sumeru in a grain of millet.
translations.idiomatic: The Dharma-king is sovereign and without limit, setting the whole world in a speck of dust and packing Mount Sumeru into a grain of millet.

sentences.zh: 蓋理本虛無，示諸方便，而妖妄之輩，茍求出家，藥王燔軀，波論灑血，假未能然，猶當克命。

translations.literal: The principle is in essence empty; these are shown as expedients—yet the deluded, grasping at them, beg to leave the household; the Medicine King burned his body, Bo Lun sprinkled his blood—if they could not do even that, they should at least yield their lives.
translations.idiomatic: The root teaching is emptiness; the rest is skillful means shown to the crowd. Yet the deluded clutch at it and beg to leave the world; the Medicine King burned his body, Bodhidharma shed his blood—if they cannot do even that, they should at least be ready to give their lives.

sentences.zh: 寧有改形易貌，有異生人，恣意放情，還同俗物。

translations.literal: How much less should they change form and appearance to differ from other men, indulge every whim, and in the end be no different from vulgar folk.
translations.idiomatic: How much less should they change their form and face until they hardly seem human, indulge every appetite, and in the end be no better than the common run.

sentences.zh: 龍宮餘論，鹿野前言，此而得容，道風前墜。

translations.literal: If the leftover doctrines of the dragon palace and the earlier words of the deer park are tolerated, the wind of the Way falls before us.
translations.idiomatic: If the leftover talk of the dragon palace and the old words of the deer park are indulged, the wind of the true Way will fall before it ever rises.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下受天明命，屈己濟民，山鬼效靈，海神率職。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to consider that Your Majesty, receiving Heaven's bright mandate, has humbled himself to succor the people; mountain ghosts show their spirit, the sea god leads his office.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to think that Your Majesty, having received Heaven's bright mandate, has humbled himself to rescue the people; mountain ghosts show their power, the sea god does his duty.

sentences.zh: 湘中石燕，沐時雨而群飛；

translations.literal: The stone swallows of Xiangzhong, when the season's rain bathes them, fly in flocks;
translations.idiomatic: The stone swallows of Xiangzhong, when the timely rain washes them, rise in flocks;

sentences.zh: 臺上銅烏，訴和風而杓轉。

translations.literal: the bronze raven on the terrace, complaining of the harmonious wind, turns its ladle.
translations.idiomatic: the bronze raven on the terrace, feeling the fair wind, turns its ladle.

sentences.zh: 以周都洛邑，治在鎬京，漢宅咸陽，魂歸豐、沛，汾、晉之地，王跡維始，眷言巡幸，且勞經略。

translations.literal: When Zhou made Luoyang its capital, government still lay at Haojing; when Han made its home at Xianyang, its soul returned to Feng and Pei—the lands of Fen and Jin, where royal traces first began: to speak of touring them is already to weary strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou built Luoyang, rule still lay at Haojing; when Han dwelt at Xianyang, its soul looked back to Feng and Pei. The lands of Fen and Jin, where the royal trace first began—to speak of touring them is already to tax your strategy.

sentences.zh: 猶復降情文苑，斟酌百家，想執玉於瑤池，念求珠於赤水。

translations.literal: Yet you still lower your mind to the Literary Garden and weigh the hundred schools, thinking to hold jade at Jasper Pool and to seek pearls at Red Water.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you still bend your mind to the Literary Garden and sift the hundred schools, as though to hold jade at Jasper Pool or seek pearls at Red Water.

sentences.zh: 竊以王母獻環，由感周德；

translations.literal: Your servant considers that when the Queen Mother offered her ring, it was from feeling Zhou's virtue;
translations.idiomatic: I take it that when the Queen Mother of the West offered her ring, she was answering Zhou's virtue;

sentences.zh: 上天錫佩，實報禹功。

translations.literal: when Heaven bestowed the girdle-pendant, it was in true reward for Yu's merit.
translations.idiomatic: when Heaven bestowed the girdle-gem, it was true payment for Yu's service.

sentences.zh: 二班勒史，兩馬制書，未見三世之辭，無聞一乘之旨。

translations.literal: The two Bans compiled histories, the two Simas made books—none saw the language of the third age, none heard the doctrine of the one vehicle.
translations.idiomatic: The two Bans wrote history, the two Simas wrote prose—none of them knew the phrasing of the third age, none heard the teaching of the one vehicle.

sentences.zh: 帝樂王禮，尚有時而沿革；

translations.literal: Imperial music and royal rites still changed with the times;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial music and royal rites still shifted with the times;

sentences.zh: 左道怪民，亦何疑於沙汰。

translations.literal: why doubt winnowing out the left-hand ways and strange folk?
translations.idiomatic: why should you hesitate to winnow out left-hand ways and strange folk?

sentences.zh: 又問刑罰寬猛，遜對曰：

translations.literal: He was again asked about whether punishments should be lenient or severe; Xun replied:
translations.idiomatic: He was questioned next on whether punishments should be lenient or severe. Xun answered:

sentences.zh: 臣聞惟王建國，刑以助禮，猶寒暑之贊陰陽，山川之通天地。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when a king establishes a state, punishments assist ritual—as cold and heat assist yin and yang, as mountains and rivers thread through heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when a true king founds a state, punishments help ritual along—as cold and heat help yin and yang, as mountains and rivers thread through heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 爰自末葉，法令稍滋，秦篆無以窮書，楚竹不能盡載。

translations.literal: From the late age onward, statutes have gradually multiplied; Qin bamboo could not exhaust what was written, Chu slips could not hold it all.
translations.idiomatic: From the late age on, laws have crept wider; Qin could not write them all on bamboo, Chu could not load them on slips.

sentences.zh: 有司因此，開以二門，高下在心，寒熱隨意。

translations.literal: The clerks, on this basis, opened two gates; high and low lay in their hearts, cold and heat at their whim.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis the clerks opened two gates—high or low at their whim, harsh or mild as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 《周官》三典，棄之若吹毛；

translations.literal: The three codes of the Offices of Zhou they tossed aside like blowing fur;
translations.idiomatic: The three codes of the Zhou Offices they tossed aside like blowing fur;

sentences.zh: 漢律九章，違之如覆手。

translations.literal: the nine chapters of Han law they broke as easily as turning the hand.
translations.idiomatic: the nine chapters of Han law they broke as easily as turning the hand over.

sentences.zh: 遂使長平獄氣，得酒而後消；

translations.literal: Thus the miasma of the Longping prison only faded after wine was granted;
translations.idiomatic: So the foul air of the Longping prison only lifted after wine was granted;

sentences.zh: 東海孝婦，因災而方雪。

translations.literal: the filial woman of Donghai was only whitened by disaster.
translations.idiomatic: the filial woman of Donghai was only cleared when Heaven sent disaster.

sentences.zh: 詔書掛壁，有善而莫遵；

translations.literal: Edicts hung on the wall, yet when there was good no one followed it;
translations.idiomatic: Edicts hung on the wall, yet when they commanded good, no one obeyed;

sentences.zh: 姦吏到門，無求而不可。

translations.literal: when the corrupt clerk came to the door, nothing was sought that could not be had.
translations.idiomatic: when a corrupt clerk came to the door, nothing was asked that could not be bought.

sentences.zh: 皆由上失其道，民不見德。

translations.literal: All because above, the Way was lost; below, the people saw no virtue.
translations.idiomatic: All because above, the Way was lost; below, the people saw no virtue.

sentences.zh: 而議者守迷，不尋其本。

translations.literal: Yet those who debate cling to delusion and do not seek the root.
translations.idiomatic: Yet debaters cling to their delusions and never look for the root.

sentences.zh: 鐘繇、王朗追怨張蒼，祖訥、梅陶共尤文帝。

translations.literal: Zhong Yao and Wang Lang pursued grievance against Zhang Cang; Zu Na and Mei Tao together praised Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao and Wang Lang nursed old grievance against Zhang Cang; Zu Na and Mei Tao together praised Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 便謂化屍起偃，在復肉刑；

translations.literal: They then said that to raise the dead and still the corpse lay in restoring corporal punishment;
translations.idiomatic: From that they said that to raise the dead and still the corpse meant bringing back corporal punishment;

sentences.zh: 致治興邦，無關周禮。

translations.literal: that to order the state and exalt the realm had nothing to do with the rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: that to order the realm and exalt the state had nothing to do with the Zhou rites.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下，昧旦坐朝，留心政術，明罰以糾諸侯，申恩以孩百姓。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to consider that Your Majesty, rising before dawn to sit in court, keeps his mind on government and uses clear punishments to correct the feudal lords and extends grace to cherish the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to think that Your Majesty, rising before dawn to hold court, keeps his mind on government, uses clear punishments to correct the feudal lords, and extends grace to cherish the hundred surnames.

sentences.zh: 黃旗紫蓋，已絕東南；

translations.literal: The yellow banner and purple canopy have already left the southeast;
translations.idiomatic: The yellow banner and purple canopy have already quit the southeast;

sentences.zh: 白馬素車，將降軹道。

translations.literal: the white horse and plain carriage are about to descend on Zhi Road.
translations.idiomatic: the white horse and plain carriage are about to come down Zhi Road.

sentences.zh: 若復峻典深文，臣實未悟。

translations.literal: If you again make the code stern and the text deep, your servant truly does not understand.
translations.idiomatic: If you now make the code stern again and the text deep, I truly do not understand.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 人肖天地，俱稟陰陽，安則願存，擾則圖死。

translations.literal: Men resemble heaven and earth and alike receive yin and yang; at peace they wish to live, when disturbed they plot death.
translations.idiomatic: Men mirror heaven and earth and share in yin and yang; when at peace they wish to live, when harried they plot death.

sentences.zh: 故王者之治，務先禮樂，如有未從，刑書乃用，寬猛兼設，水火俱陳，未有專任商、韓而能長久。

translations.literal: Therefore the king's governance must first attend to ritual and music; if there are those who do not follow, then the penal writings are used; lenience and severity are both set, water and fire both displayed—never has one relied only on Shang Yang and Han Fei and endured long.
translations.idiomatic: So the king's rule must put ritual and music first; only when some still will not follow does the penal code come out. Leniency and severity stand together, water and fire both in view—never yet has a realm leaned only on Shang Yang and Han Fei and lasted.

sentences.zh: 昔秦歸士會，晉盜來奔；

translations.literal: In old times Qin returned Shi Hui and Jin's thief came to flee;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Qin sent back Shi Hui and Jin's thief fled to them;

sentences.zh: 舜舉臯陶，不仁自遠。

translations.literal: Shun raised Gao Yao and the unkind put themselves far away.
translations.idiomatic: Shun raised Gao Yao and the unkind kept their distance of themselves.

sentences.zh: 但令釋之、定國迭作理官，龔遂、文翁繼為郡守，科間律令，一此憲章，欣聞汲黯之言，泣斷昭平之罪。

translations.literal: Only let Zhang Shizhi and Yu Dingguo take turns as judges, Gong Sui and Wen Weng succeed one another as prefects, make the statutes one with the fundamental code, rejoice to hear Ji An's words, weep and break off Lord Shao's sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Only let Zhang Shizhi and Yu Dingguo serve in turn as judges, Gong Sui and Wen Weng follow one another as prefects, knit the statutes to a single code, rejoice to hear Ji An speak, weep and set aside the sentence on Lord Shao.

sentences.zh: 則天下自治，大道公行，乳獸含牙，蒼鷹垂翅，楚王錢府，不復須封，漢獄冤囚，自然蒙理。

translations.literal: Then all under Heaven will govern itself, the great Way will walk abroad, suckling beasts will bear their tusks, the dark kite will fold its wings, the Chu king's money vault will need no more sealing, and Han's wronged prisoners will naturally receive justice.
translations.idiomatic: Then the realm will order itself, the great Way will walk abroad, suckling beasts will sheathe their tusks, the dark kite will fold its wings, the Chu king's treasury will need no further seal, and Han's wronged prisoners will naturally find justice.

sentences.zh: 後服之徒，旣承風而慕化；

translations.literal: Those beyond the borders, having received the wind, will admire and be transformed;
translations.idiomatic: Those beyond the borders, having caught the wind, will admire and change;

sentences.zh: 有截之內，皆蹈德而詠仁。

translations.literal: within the trimmed realm all will tread virtue and sing of benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: within the four seas all will tread in virtue and sing of benevolence.

sentences.zh: 號以成康，何難之有？

translations.literal: To be hailed as the age of Cheng and Kang—what difficulty is there?
translations.idiomatic: To be hailed as another age of Cheng and Kang—what could be hard about that?

sentences.zh: 又問禍福報應，遜對曰：

translations.literal: He was again asked about fortune, misfortune, and retribution; Xun replied:
translations.idiomatic: He was questioned next on fortune, misfortune, and retribution. Xun answered:

sentences.zh: 臣聞五方易辨，尚待指南；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the five directions are easy to distinguish, yet one still waits for the south-pointing chariot;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the five directions are easy to tell apart, yet one still waits for the south-pointing chariot;

sentences.zh: 百世可知，猶須吹律。

translations.literal: a hundred generations may be known, yet one still needs to blow the pitch-pipes.
translations.idiomatic: a hundred generations may be foreknown, yet one still must blow the pitch-pipes.

sentences.zh: 況復天道秘遠，神跡難源，不有通靈，孰能盡悟。

translations.literal: How much more the secret remoteness of Heaven's Way and the hard-to-trace tracks of the spirit—without communion with them, who can fully comprehend?
translations.idiomatic: How much more the secret remoteness of Heaven's Way and the hard-to-trace tracks of the spirits—without communion, who can grasp them whole?

sentences.zh: 乘查至於河漢，唯睹牽牛；

translations.literal: When the raft reached the River of Heaven, one only saw the Cowherd;
translations.idiomatic: When the raft reached the River of Heaven, one only saw the Cowherd Star;

sentences.zh: 假寐遊於上玄，止逢翟犬。

translations.literal: in a feigned sleep one wandered in the upper mystery and only met the Di Dog.
translations.idiomatic: in a feigned sleep one wandered the upper mystery and only met the Di Dog.

sentences.zh: 造化之理，旣寂寞而無傳；

translations.literal: The principle of creation and transformation is already silent and without transmission;
translations.idiomatic: The principle of creation and change is already silent and untransmitted;

sentences.zh: 報應之來，固難得而妄說。

translations.literal: the coming of retribution is inherently hard to speak of rashly.
translations.idiomatic: the coming of retribution is, by nature, not something to speak of rashly.

sentences.zh: 但秦穆有道，勾芒錫祥；

translations.literal: Yet Duke Mu of Qin had the Way and Goumang bestowed auspice;
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Duke Mu of Qin held the Way, Goumang granted good omens;

sentences.zh: 虢公涼德，蓐收降禍。

translations.literal: Duke Guo had a cold virtue and Rusou sent down calamity.
translations.idiomatic: when Duke Guo had a cold virtue, Rusou sent calamity down.

sentences.zh: 高明在上，定自有知，不可謂神冥昧難信。

translations.literal: What is lofty above surely has its knowing—one cannot say the spirits are dark and hard to trust.
translations.idiomatic: What is high above surely knows—one cannot say the spirits are dark and untrustworthy.

sentences.zh: 若夫仲尼厄於陳、蔡，孟軻困於齊、梁，自是不遇其時，寧關性命之理。

translations.literal: As for Confucius beset at Chen and Cai, Mencius trapped at Qi and Liang—that was simply not meeting the time; how could it concern the principle of fate-nature?
translations.idiomatic: As for Confucius trapped at Chen and Cai, Mencius hard pressed in Qi and Liang—that was simply not meeting the time; what has that to do with the principle of fate?

sentences.zh: 子胥無君，馬遷附下，受誅取辱，何可尤人。

translations.literal: Wu Zixu without a lord, Sima Qian attached below—receiving execution and taking disgrace: how can one blame others?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zixu without a lord, Sima Qian clinging to a low post—taking execution and shame: how can one blame others for that?

sentences.zh: 至如協律見親，櫂船得幸，從此而言，更不足怪。

translations.literal: As for the music harmonizer who found kinship, the oar-man who gained favor—from this, one should be less surprised.
translations.idiomatic: As for the pitch-pipe officer who found favor, the boatman who gained luck—from that angle, there is less to marvel at.

sentences.zh: 周王漂杵，致天之罰；

translations.literal: King Wu's floating pestle was Heaven's punishment;
translations.idiomatic: King Wu's floating pestle was Heaven's punishment;

sentences.zh: 白起誅降，行己之意。

translations.literal: Bai Qi's slaughter of the surrendered was his own intent.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Qi's slaughter of the surrendered was his own intent.

sentences.zh: 是以七百之祚，仍加姬氏；

translations.literal: Thus the seven-hundred-year span was still added to the house of Ji;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the seven-hundred-year span was still added to the house of Ji;

sentences.zh: 杜郵之戮，還屬武安。

translations.literal: the execution at Duyou still fell on Lord Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: the execution at Duyou still fell on Lord Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 昔漢問上計，不過日蝕；

translations.literal: In old times Han questioned the upper accounts and went no further than eclipses of the sun;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Han questioned the upper accounts and went no further than solar eclipses;

sentences.zh: 晉策秀才，止於寒火。

translations.literal: Jin tested the cultivated talent and stopped at cold fire.
translations.idiomatic: Jin tested the cultivated talent and stopped at cold fire.

sentences.zh: 前賢往士，咸用為難；

translations.literal: Former worthies and past gentlemen all took this as hard;
translations.idiomatic: Former worthies and past gentlemen all took this as hard;

sentences.zh: 推古比今，臣見其易。

translations.literal: weighing antiquity against today, your servant sees it as easy.
translations.idiomatic: weighing antiquity against today, I see it as easy.

sentences.zh: 然草萊百姓，過荷恩私，三折寒膠，再遊金馬。

translations.literal: Yet this humble commoner has overborne your grace; thrice broken, cold glue, twice visiting the Golden Horse Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this humble commoner has overborne your grace—lacquer thrice broken, twice admitted at the Golden Horse Gate.

sentences.zh: 王言昭賁，思若有神，占對失圖，伏深悚懼。

translations.literal: The king's words were bright and splendid; his thought seemed inspired—yet in matching answers he lost the chart and bows deep in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Your words were bright and splendid; my thought seemed touched by the spirits—yet in answering I missed the mark, and I bow deep in fear.

sentences.zh: 尚書擢第，以遜為當時第一。

translations.literal: The Secretariat ranked the candidates and made Xun first of his time.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat ranked the candidates and placed Xun first in the land.

sentences.zh: 十二月，清河王岳為大行臺，率衆南討，以遜從軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Prince of Qinghe Yue became Grand Commissioner-in-Chief, led troops south to attack, and Xun followed the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Prince of Qinghe Yue became Grand Commissioner-in-Chief, led troops south on campaign, and Xun went with the army.

sentences.zh: 明年，顯祖納貞陰侯為梁主，岳假遜大行臺郎中，使於南，與蕭脩、侯瑱和解。

translations.literal: The next year, the Manifest Ancestor installed the Marquis of Zhenyin as lord of Liang; Yue made Xun acting director of the Grand Commissioner's office and sent him south as envoy to treat for peace with Xiao Xiu and Hou Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Manifest Ancestor set up the Marquis of Zhenyin as lord of Liang. Yue made Xun acting director of the Grand Commissioner's office and sent him south to treat for peace with Xiao Xiu and Hou Zhen.

sentences.zh: 遜往來五日，得脩等報書，岳因與脩盟于江上。

translations.literal: In five days of going and coming he obtained the reply letters of Xiu and the others; Yue then allied with Xiu on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Within five days going and returning he had the reply letters from Xiu and the others; Yue then allied with Xiu on the river.

sentences.zh: 大軍還鄴，遜仍被都官尚書崔昂舉薦。

translations.literal: When the great army returned to Ye, Xun was again recommended by Director of the Ministry of Justice Cui Ang.
translations.idiomatic: When the great army returned to Ye, Xun was again recommended by Cui Ang, Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 詔付尚書，考為清平勤幹，送吏部。

translations.literal: An edict entrusted him to the Ministry of State Affairs; on examination he was rated clear, fair, diligent, and capable, and was forwarded to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: An edict placed him in the hands of the Ministry of State Affairs; when they examined his record they found him clear, fair, diligent, and capable, and sent him on to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔令校定群書，供皇太子。

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict ordered the collation of the collected classics to supply the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year an edict ordered the collation of the collected classics for the Crown Prince's use.

sentences.zh: 遜與冀州秀才高乾和、瀛州秀才馬敬德、許散愁、韓同寶、洛州秀才傅懷德、懷州秀才古道子、廣平郡孝廉李漢子、渤海郡孝廉鮑長暄、陽平郡孝廉景孫、前梁州府主簿王九元、前開府水曹參軍周子深等十一人同被尚書召共刊定。

translations.literal: Xun, together with eleven others—the Jizhou licentiate Gao Qianhe, the Yingzhou licentiate Ma Jingde, Xu San'chou, Han Tongbao, the Luozhou licentiate Fu Huai'de, the Huaizhou licentiate Gu Daozi, the Guangping commandery filial exemplar Li Hanzi, the Bohai commandery filial exemplar Bao Changxuan, the Yangping commandery filial exemplar Jing Sun, the former Liangzhou establishment chief clerk Wang Jiuyuan, and the former establishment water-bureau section chief Zhou Zishen—were alike summoned by the Ministry to collate together.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and eleven others—the Jizhou licentiate Gao Qianhe, the Yingzhou licentiate Ma Jingde, Xu San'chou, Han Tongbao, the Luozhou licentiate Fu Huai'de, the Huaizhou licentiate Gu Daozi, the Guangping filial exemplar Li Hanzi, the Bohai filial exemplar Bao Changxuan, the Yangping filial exemplar Jing Sun, the former Liangzhou establishment chief clerk Wang Jiuyuan, and the former establishment water-bureau section chief Zhou Zishen—were summoned by the Ministry to collate as one body.

sentences.zh: 時秘府書籍紕繆者多，遜乃議曰：「按漢中壘校尉劉向受詔校書，每一書竟，表上，輒言：臣向書、長水校尉臣參書，太史公、太常博士書、中外書合若干本以相比校，然後殺青。

translations.literal: At that time many books in the secret repository were corrupt; Xun then proposed: "According to the precedent of Liu Xiang, Director of the Fortress at Hanzhong, who received an imperial charge to collate books—whenever he finished a single work he would memorialize the throne, always stating: 'Your servant Xiang's copy, Director of the Long Water Gate Your servant Can's copy, the Grand Historian's copy, the Grand Director of Ceremonies doctor's copy, inner and outer office copies—so many fascicles in all were compared and collated, and only then was the final text fixed in ink.'"
translations.idiomatic: Many volumes in the secret repository were corrupt at the time, and Xun proposed: "We should follow Liu Xiang, Director of the Fortress at Hanzhong, who received an imperial charge to collate the classics. Whenever he finished a book he would memorialize the throne, always reporting: 'Your servant Xiang's copy, Director of the Long Water Gate Your servant Can's copy, the Grand Historian's copy, the Grand Director of Ceremonies doctor's copy, and inner and outer office copies—so many fascicles in all were compared and collated, and only then was the text fixed in ink for publication.'"

sentences.zh: 今所讎校，供擬極重，出自蘭臺，御諸甲館。

translations.literal: The collations now under review were intended for the weightiest use, issued from the Orchid Terrace and kept in the First-Rank Archives.
translations.idiomatic: The texts we are collating now are meant for the gravest purposes, issued from the Orchid Terrace and housed in the First-Rank Archives.

sentences.zh: 向之故事，見存府閤，即欲刊定，必藉衆本。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang's precedent survives in the office archives; to collate and fix texts now, one must rely on many copies.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's procedure still survives in the office archives; if we mean to collate and fix the texts now, we must lean on many copies.

sentences.zh: 太常卿邢子才、太子少傅魏收、吏部尚書辛術、司農少卿穆子容、前黃門郎司馬子瑞、故國子祭酒李業興並是多書之家，請牒借本參校得失。

translations.literal: Grand Director of Ceremonies Xing Zicai, Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince Wei Shou, Minister of Personnel Xin Shu, Vice Minister of Revenue Mu Zirong, former Yellow Gate Gentleman Sima Zirui, and the late Director of the Imperial University Li Yexing were all houses rich in books; he asked that lists be sent to borrow their copies for collating gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Director of Ceremonies Xing Zicai, Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince Wei Shou, Minister of Personnel Xin Shu, Vice Minister of Revenue Mu Zirong, former Yellow Gate Gentleman Sima Zirui, and the late Director of the Imperial University Li Yexing all kept great libraries; he asked that lists be sent so their copies might be borrowed to collate against our texts.

sentences.zh: 」秘書監尉瑾移尚書都坐，凡得別本三千餘卷，《五經》諸史，殆無遺闕。

translations.literal: Secretariat Supervisor Wei Jin forwarded the matter to the chief seat of the Ministry; in all they obtained more than three thousand juan of alternate copies, and among the Five Classics and the various histories scarcely anything was left out.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Supervisor Wei Jin forwarded the request to the Ministry's chief seat; in all they obtained more than three thousand juan of alternate copies, and among the Five Classics and the various histories scarcely a title was missing.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔尚書開東西二省官選，所司策問，遜為當時第一。

translations.literal: In the eighth year an edict opened selection for officials of the Eastern and Western Provinces at the Ministry; in the policy questions set by the office, Xun ranked first in his day.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year an edict opened selection for officials of the Eastern and Western Provinces at the Ministry; in the policy questions set by the office, Xun took first place in his generation.

sentences.zh: 左僕射楊愔辟遜為其府佐。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Yang Yin recruited Xun as a staff officer in his establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Yang Yin recruited Xun as a staff officer in his establishment.

sentences.zh: 遜辭曰：「門族寒陋，訪第必不成，乞補員外司馬督。

translations.literal: Xun declined, saying: "My clan is poor and mean; if I seek a ranked post I am sure to fail. I beg to be appointed an irregular aide who supervises the establishment's military affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Xun declined, saying, "My house is poor and low; if I seek a ranked post I am sure to fail. I beg instead for an irregular aide who supervises the establishment's military affairs."

sentences.zh: 」愔曰：「才高不依常例。

translations.literal: Yin said: "When talent is high, one does not follow the usual rule."
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "When talent runs high, one does not follow the usual rule."

sentences.zh: 」特奏用之。

translations.literal: He memorialized specially to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized specially to employ him.

sentences.zh: 九年，有詔超除員外將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year an edict promoted him by exception to irregular general.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year an edict promoted him by exception to irregular general.

sentences.zh: 後世祖鎮鄴，召入司徒府管書記。

translations.literal: Later, when Shizu was stationed at Ye, he was summoned into the Secretariat to manage documents.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Shizu was stationed at Ye, he was summoned into the Secretariat to manage documents.

sentences.zh: 及登祚，轉授主書，遷員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, he was transferred and made chief secretary, then promoted to irregular attendant of the cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu ascended the throne, he was transferred and made chief secretary, then promoted to irregular attendant of the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 天統初，病卒。

translations.literal: At the start of Tiantong he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tiantong he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 劉逖，字子長，彭城叢亭裏人也。

translations.literal: Liu Ti, styled Zichang, was a man of Congting Lane in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ti, styled Zichang, came from Congting Lane in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 祖芳，魏太常卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fang was Grand Director of Ceremonies of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fang had been Grand Director of Ceremonies of Wei.

sentences.zh: 父戫，金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His father Yi was a Grand Master of Splendid Virtue with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi held the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Virtue with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 逖少而聰敏，好弋獵騎射，以行樂為事，愛交遊，善戲謔。

translations.literal: Ti was clever from youth, fond of hunting and archery on horseback, taking pleasure in travel as his business, loving company, and skilled at jest.
translations.idiomatic: Ti was clever from youth, fond of hunting and archery on horseback; he made pleasure and travel his trade, loved company, and was skilled at jest.

sentences.zh: 郡辟功曹，州命主簿。

translations.literal: The commandery recruited him as merit officer; the province appointed him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery recruited him as merit officer; the province appointed him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 魏末徵詣霸府，世宗以為永安公浚開府行參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei he was summoned to the hegemon's office; Shizong made him a traveling aide in the establishment of Prince of Yong'an Jun.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wei he was summoned to the hegemon's office; Shizong made him a traveling aide in the establishment of Prince of Yong'an Jun.

sentences.zh: 逖遠離鄉家，倦於羈旅，發憤自勵，專精讀書。

translations.literal: Far from his home district and weary of life on the road, he roused himself in anger and applied himself solely to reading.
translations.idiomatic: Far from home and weary of life on the road, he roused himself and bent all his force to reading.

sentences.zh: 晉陽都會之所，霸朝人士攸集，咸務於宴集。

translations.literal: Jinyang was the gathering place of the hegemon's court; men of the ruling house flocked there, all bent on feasting.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyang was the gathering place of the hegemon's court; men of the ruling house flocked there, all bent on feasting.

sentences.zh: 逖在遊宴之中，卷不離手，值有文籍所未見者，則終日諷誦，或通夜不歸，其好學如此。

translations.literal: Even amid these revels Ti never let his scroll leave his hand; whenever he came upon a text he had not seen before, he would chant it through the day, sometimes not returning home all night—such was his love of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Even amid these revels Ti never let his scroll leave his hand; whenever he came upon a text he had not seen before, he would chant it through the day, sometimes not returning home all night—such was his hunger for learning.

sentences.zh: 亦留心文藻，頗工詩詠。

translations.literal: He also turned his mind to belles-lettres and was quite skilled at verse.
translations.idiomatic: He also turned his mind to belles-lettres and was quite skilled at verse.

sentences.zh: 天保初，行定陶縣令，坐姦事免，十餘年不得調。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianbao he served as acting magistrate of Dingtao county and was dismissed on a charge of misconduct; for more than ten years he received no new appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao he served as acting magistrate of Dingtao county and was dismissed on a charge of misconduct; for more than ten years he received no new appointment.

sentences.zh: 乾明年，兼員外散騎常侍，使於梁主蕭莊，還，兼三公郎中。

translations.literal: In the Qianming era he was concurrently irregular attendant of the cavalry and sent as envoy to Liang's ruler Xiao Zhuang; on his return he was concurrently a gentleman of the Three Excellencies Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianming era he was concurrently irregular attendant of the cavalry and sent as envoy to Liang's ruler Xiao Zhuang; on his return he was concurrently a gentleman of the Three Excellencies Bureau.

sentences.zh: 皇建元年，除太子洗馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangjian he was made mentor of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangjian he was made mentor of the heir.

sentences.zh: 肅宗崩，從世祖赴晉陽，除散騎侍郎，兼儀曹郎中。

translations.literal: When Suzong died, he followed Shizu to Jinyang, was made irregular attendant of the cavalry, and concurrently a gentleman of the Ceremonies Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong died, he followed Shizu to Jinyang, was made irregular attendant of the cavalry, and concurrently a gentleman of the Ceremonies Bureau.

sentences.zh: 久之，兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: After a long while he was concurrently a gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was concurrently a gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 和士開寵要，逖附之，正授中書侍郎，入典機密，兼散騎常侍，聘陳使主。

translations.literal: He Shikai held favor and power; Ti attached himself to him, was formally appointed gentleman of the Secretariat, entered to manage secrets, was concurrently irregular attendant of the cavalry, and served as chief envoy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai held favor and power; Ti attached himself to him, was formally appointed gentleman of the Secretariat, entered to manage secrets, was concurrently irregular attendant of the cavalry, and served as chief envoy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 還，除通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: On his return he was made attendant of direct communication and irregular cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made attendant of direct communication and irregular cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋遷給事黃門侍郎，修國史，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to attendant who presents matters to the Yellow Gate, edited the national history, and was given concurrent irregular attendant of the cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to attendant who presents matters to the Yellow Gate, edited the national history, and was given concurrent irregular attendant of the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 又除假儀同三司，聘周使副。

translations.literal: He was further made acting insignia equal to the Three Excellencies and deputy chief envoy to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made acting insignia equal to the Three Excellencies and deputy chief envoy to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 二國始通，禮儀未定，逖與周朝議論往復，斟酌古今，事多合禮，兼文辭可觀，甚得名譽。

translations.literal: When the two states first opened relations, ritual had not yet been fixed; Ti debated back and forth with the Zhou court, weighing past and present, and in most matters matched ritual; his literary phrasing was also admirable, and he won great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: When the two states first opened relations, ritual had not yet been fixed; Ti debated back and forth with the Zhou court, weighing past and present, and in most matters matched ritual; his literary phrasing was also admirable, and he won great reputation.

sentences.zh: 使還，拜儀同三司。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was given insignia equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When the mission returned, he was given insignia equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，出為江州刺史。

translations.literal: When Shizu died, he went out as inspector of Jiang province.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu died, he went out as inspector of Jiang province.

sentences.zh: 祖珽執政，徙為仁州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zu Ting held power, he was moved to inspector of Ren province.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Ting held power, he was moved to inspector of Ren province.

sentences.zh: 祖珽旣出，徵還，待詔文林館，重除散騎常侍，奏門下事。

translations.literal: After Zu Ting was removed, Ti was recalled, kept on call at the Forest of Literature Hall, and again made irregular attendant of the cavalry to present matters at the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After Zu Ting was removed, Ti was recalled, kept on call at the Forest of Literature Hall, and again made irregular attendant of the cavalry to present matters at the Gate.

sentences.zh: 未幾，與崔季舒等同時被戮，時年四十九。

translations.literal: Before long he was executed together with Cui Jishu and others at the same time, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was executed together with Cui Jishu and others at the same time, aged forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 初，逖與珽以文義相得，結雷、陳之契，又為弟俊聘珽之女。

translations.literal: Earlier Ti and Zu Ting had found each other through literary affinity and made a bond like Lei and Chen; he also had his younger brother Jun take Ting's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ti and Zu Ting had found each other through literary affinity and made a bond like Lei and Chen; he also had his younger brother Jun take Ting's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 珽之將免趙彥深等也，先以告逖，仍付密啟，令其奏聞。

translations.literal: When Ting was about to remove Zhao Yanshen and the others, he first told Ti and even handed him a secret memorial, ordering him to report it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting was about to remove Zhao Yanshen and the others, he first told Ti and even handed him a secret memorial, ordering him to report it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 彥深等頗知之，先自申理，珽由此疑逖告其所為。

translations.literal: Yanshen and the others learned of it somewhat in advance and pleaded their own case first; because of this Ting suspected Ti had informed on what he had done.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen and the others learned of it somewhat in advance and pleaded their own case first; because of this Ting suspected Ti had informed on what he had done.

sentences.zh: 及珽被出，逖遂遣弟離婚，其輕交易絕如此。

translations.literal: When Ting was removed, Ti at once sent his brother to divorce her—so lightly did he break ties and cut relations.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting was removed, Ti at once sent his brother to divorce her—so lightly did he break ties and cut relations.

sentences.zh: 所制詩賦及雜文文筆三十卷。

translations.literal: The poetry, rhapsodies, and miscellaneous prose he composed came to thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: The poetry, rhapsodies, and miscellaneous prose he composed came to thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 子逸民，開府行參軍。

translations.literal: His son Yimin was a traveling aide in an establishment office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yimin was a traveling aide in an establishment office.

sentences.zh: 逖弟詧，少聰明，好文學。

translations.literal: Ti's younger brother Cha was clever from youth and loved literature.
translations.idiomatic: Ti's younger brother Cha was clever from youth and loved literature.

sentences.zh: 天統、武平之間，歷殿中侍御史，兼散騎侍郎，迎勞陳使，轉尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: Between Tiantong and Wuping he served in turn as attendant censor within the palace, concurrently irregular attendant of the cavalry, welcomed and entertained the Chen envoy, and was transferred to a gentleman of the Ceremonies Bureau in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Between Tiantong and Wuping he served in turn as attendant censor within the palace, concurrently irregular attendant of the cavalry, welcomed and entertained the Chen envoy, and was transferred to a gentleman of the Ceremonies Bureau in the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 周大象末，卒於黎州治中。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhou era of Great Elephant he died as administrator of Li province.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhou era of Great Elephant he died as administrator of Li province.

sentences.zh: 子玄道，有人品識用，定州騎兵參軍。

translations.literal: His son Xuandao had character and judgment and served as cavalry section chief of Ding province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuandao had character and judgment and served as cavalry section chief of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 逖從子顗，字君卿。

translations.literal: Ti's nephew Yan, styled Junqing.
translations.idiomatic: Ti's nephew Yan, styled Junqing.

sentences.zh: 祖廞，魏尚書，為高祖所殺。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yin was a minister of Wei and was killed by Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yin had been a minister of Wei and was killed by Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 顗父濟及濟弟峻俱奔江南。

translations.literal: Yan's father Ji and Ji's younger brother Jun both fled south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's father Ji and Ji's younger brother Jun both fled south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 顗出後。

translations.literal: Yan was given out in adoption.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was given out in adoption.

sentences.zh: 武定中從峻還北。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he followed Jun back north.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he followed Jun back north.

sentences.zh: 摐賜爵臨潁子，大寧中卒於司徒司馬。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Marquis of Linying and died in the Daning era as a secretary in the Grand Marshal's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the title Marquis of Linying and died in the Daning era as a secretary in the Grand Marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 顗好文學，工草書，風儀甚美。

translations.literal: Yan loved literature, was skilled at cursive script, and his bearing was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: Yan loved literature, was skilled at cursive script, and his bearing was very fine.

sentences.zh: 歷瀛州外兵參軍、司空功曹，待詔文林館，除大理司直。

translations.literal: He served in turn as outer military section chief of Ying province and merit officer in the Ministry of Works, was kept on call at the Forest of Literature Hall, and was made direct judge in the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as outer military section chief of Ying province and merit officer in the Ministry of Works, was kept on call at the Forest of Literature Hall, and was made direct judge in the Court of Review.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中鄜州司馬，卒。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was a secretary of Zheng province and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was a secretary of Zheng province and died.

sentences.zh: 顏之推，字介，瑯邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Yan Zhitui, styled Jie, was a man of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhitui, styled Jie, came from Linyi in Langye.

sentences.zh: 九世祖含，從晉元東渡，官至侍中、右光祿、西平侯。

translations.literal: His ninth-generation ancestor Han, following Emperor Yuan of Jin east across the river, reached the post of attendant, Right Grand Master of Splendid Virtue, and Marquis of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: His ninth-generation ancestor Han, following Emperor Yuan of Jin east across the river, reached the post of attendant, Right Grand Master of Splendid Virtue, and Marquis of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 父勰，梁湘東王繹鎮西府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His father Xie was a consulting officer in the western establishment staff of Xiao Yi, Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xie was a consulting officer in the western establishment staff of Xiao Yi, Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 世善《周官》、《左氏》，之推早傳家業。

translations.literal: The family had long excelled in the Offices of Zhou and the Zuo Tradition; Zhitui received the household learning early.
translations.idiomatic: The family had long excelled in the Offices of Zhou and the Zuo Tradition; Zhitui received the household learning early.

sentences.zh: 年十二，值繹自講《莊》、《老》，便預門徒。

translations.literal: At twelve, when Yi was himself lecturing on the Zhuangzi and Laozi, he was admitted among the disciples.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve, when Yi was himself lecturing on the Zhuangzi and Laozi, he was admitted among the disciples.

sentences.zh: 虛談非其所好，還習《禮》、《傳》，博覽群書，無不該洽，詞情典麗，甚為西府所稱。

translations.literal: Empty talk was not to his taste; he returned to the study of the Rites and the Commentaries, ranged widely through books, and was thorough in all he touched; his phrasing was classical and beautiful, and the western establishment praised him highly.
translations.idiomatic: Empty talk was not to his taste; he returned to the study of the Rites and the Commentaries, ranged widely through books, and was thorough in all he touched; his phrasing was classical and beautiful, and the western establishment praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 繹以為其國左常侍，加鎮西墨曹參軍。

translations.literal: Yi made him regular attendant of the state on the left and added him as ink-and-brush section chief of the western establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yi made him regular attendant of the state on the left and added him as ink-and-brush section chief of the western establishment.

sentences.zh: 好飲酒，多任縱，不修邊幅，時論以此少之。

translations.literal: He loved wine, was much given to license, and did not keep his dress in order; opinion at the time therefore thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine, was much given to license, and did not keep his dress in order; opinion at the time therefore thought less of him.

sentences.zh: 繹遣世子方諸出鎮郢州，以之推掌管記。

translations.literal: Yi sent the heir Fangzhu out to garrison Yingzhou and put Zhitui in charge of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent the heir Fangzhu out to garrison Yingzhou and put Zhitui in charge of documents.

sentences.zh: 值侯景陷郢州，頻欲殺之，賴其行臺郎中王則以獲免。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing took Yingzhou he repeatedly wished to kill him; he was spared thanks to Wang Ze, a gentleman in Jing's traveling office.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing took Yingzhou he repeatedly wished to kill him; he was spared thanks to Wang Ze, a gentleman in Jing's traveling office.

sentences.zh: 被囚送建業。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned and sent to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned and sent to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 景平，還江陵。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, he returned to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was pacified, he returned to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 時繹已自立，以之推為散騎侍郎，奏舍人事。

translations.literal: By then Yi had declared himself ruler; he made Zhitui irregular attendant of the cavalry and a gentleman who presents matters in the heir's household.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yi had declared himself ruler; he made Zhitui irregular attendant of the cavalry and a gentleman who presents matters in the heir's household.

sentences.zh: 後為周軍所破。

translations.literal: Later he was defeated by the Zhou army.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was defeated by the Zhou army.

sentences.zh: 大將軍李顯慶重之，薦往弘農，令掌其兄陽平公遠書翰。

translations.literal: Grand General Li Xianqing valued him, recommended him to Hongnong, and had him manage the correspondence of his elder brother, the Duke of Yangping, Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Li Xianqing valued him, recommended him to Hongnong, and had him manage the correspondence of his elder brother, the Duke of Yangping, Yuan.

sentences.zh: 值河水暴長，具船將妻子來奔，經砥柱之險，時人稱其勇決。

translations.literal: When the river rose in sudden flood, he prepared a boat and came fleeing with wife and children; he passed the peril of the Rapids, and men of the time praised his courage and resolve.
translations.idiomatic: When the river rose in sudden flood, he prepared a boat and came fleeing with wife and children; he passed the peril of the Rapids, and men of the time praised his courage and resolve.

sentences.zh: 顯祖見而悅之，即除奉朝請，引於內館中，侍從左右，頗被顧眄。

translations.literal: Xianzu saw him and was pleased, at once made him a court gentleman for attendance, brought him into the inner lodge to attend left and right, and favored him with frequent glances.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu saw him and was pleased, at once made him a court gentleman for attendance, brought him into the inner lodge to attend left and right, and favored him with frequent glances.

sentences.zh: 天保末，從至天池，以為中書舍人，令中書郎段孝信將勑書出示之推。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he followed the ruler to Heavenly Pool; he was made a secretary in the Secretariat and ordered that Secretariat Gentleman Duan Xiaoxin bring out the edict documents and show them to Zhitui.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao he followed the ruler to Heavenly Pool; he was made a secretary in the Secretariat and ordered that Secretariat Gentleman Duan Xiaoxin bring out the edict documents and show them to Zhitui.

sentences.zh: 之推營外飲酒，孝信還以狀言，顯祖乃曰：「且停」。

translations.literal: Zhitui was drinking outside the camp; when Xiaoxin returned and reported the matter, Xianzu said: "Let it wait."
translations.idiomatic: Zhitui was drinking outside the camp; when Xiaoxin returned and reported the matter, Xianzu said, "Let it wait."

sentences.zh: 由是遂寢。

translations.literal: Because of this the appointment was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 河清末，被舉為趙州功曹參軍，尋待詔文林館，除司徒錄事參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Heqing era he was recommended as merit officer in Zhao province, soon kept on call at the Forest of Literature Hall, and made recording officer in the Grand Marshal's office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Heqing era he was recommended as merit officer in Zhao province, soon kept on call at the Forest of Literature Hall, and made recording officer in the Grand Marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 之推聰穎機悟，博識有才辯，工尺牘，應對閑明，大為祖珽所重，令掌知館事，判署文書。

translations.literal: Zhitui was clever, quick-witted, broadly learned, talented in debate, skilled at documents, and easy in reply; Zu Ting valued him greatly, put him in charge of the hall's affairs, and had him sign and judge papers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhitui was clever, quick-witted, broadly learned, talented in debate, skilled at documents, and easy in reply; Zu Ting valued him greatly, put him in charge of the hall's affairs, and had him sign and judge papers.

sentences.zh: 尋遷通直散騎常侍，俄領中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to attendant of direct communication and irregular cavalry, and shortly led the secretariat as secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to attendant of direct communication and irregular cavalry, and shortly led the secretariat as secretary.

sentences.zh: 帝時有取索，恒令中使傳旨，之推稟承宣告，館中皆受進止。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor had a request, he always sent a palace messenger to transmit the order; Zhitui received and announced it, and everyone in the hall took their cue from him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor had a request, he always sent a palace messenger to transmit the order; Zhitui received and announced it, and everyone in the hall took their cue from him.

sentences.zh: 所進文章，皆是其封署，於進賢門奏之，待報方出。

translations.literal: Every document submitted was sealed by him; he presented them at the Gate of Advancement to the Worthy and waited for a reply before they went out.
translations.idiomatic: Every document submitted was sealed by him; he presented them at the Gate of Advancement to the Worthy and waited for a reply before they went out.

sentences.zh: 兼善於文字，監校繕寫，處事勤敏，號為稱職。

translations.literal: He was also skilled at writing, supervised collation and copying, handled affairs diligently and swiftly, and was called competent in his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled at writing, supervised collation and copying, handled affairs diligently and swiftly, and was called competent in his post.

sentences.zh: 帝甚加恩接，顧遇逾厚，為勳要者所嫉，常欲害之。

translations.literal: The emperor showed him great favor and regard beyond the usual; men of merit and power envied him and often wished to harm him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed him great favor and regard beyond the usual; men of merit and power envied him and often wished to harm him.

sentences.zh: 崔季舒等將諫也，之推取急還宅，故不連署。

translations.literal: When Cui Jishu and the others were about to remonstrate, Zhitui took urgent leave and returned home, and therefore did not join in the collective signature.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Jishu and the others were about to remonstrate, Zhitui took urgent leave and returned home, and therefore did not join in the collective signature.

sentences.zh: 及召集諫人，之推亦被喚入，勘無其名，方得免禍。

translations.literal: When the remonstrators were summoned, Zhitui was called in as well; on investigation his name was not among them, and only then did he escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When the remonstrators were summoned, Zhitui was called in as well; on investigation his name was not among them, and only then did he escape disaster.

sentences.zh: 尋除黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was made gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 及周兵陷晉陽，帝輕騎還鄴，窘急計無所從，之推因宦者侍中鄧長颙進奔陳之策，仍勸募吳士千餘人以為左右，取青、徐路共投陳國。

translations.literal: When the Zhou army took Jinyang, the emperor rode back to Ye in light armor; in desperate straits he had no plan to follow; Zhitui, through the eunuch attendant Deng Changyong, advanced a plan to flee to Chen, and urged recruiting more than a thousand Wu men as a personal guard, taking the Qing and Xu route together to throw themselves on Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou army took Jinyang, the emperor rode back to Ye in light armor; in desperate straits he had no plan to follow; Zhitui, through the eunuch attendant Deng Changyong, advanced a plan to flee to Chen, and urged recruiting more than a thousand Wu men as a personal guard, taking the Qing and Xu route together to throw themselves on Chen.

sentences.zh: 帝甚納之，以告丞相高阿那肱等。

translations.literal: The emperor was much inclined to accept it and told the chief minister Gao Anagong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was much inclined to accept it and told the chief minister Gao Anagong and the others.

sentences.zh: 阿那肱不願入陳，乃云吳士難信，不須募之。

translations.literal: Anagong did not wish to enter Chen and said the Wu men were hard to trust and need not be recruited.
translations.idiomatic: Anagong did not wish to enter Chen and said the Wu men were hard to trust and need not be recruited.

sentences.zh: 勸帝送珍寶累重向青州，且守三齊之地，若不可保，徐浮海南渡。

translations.literal: He urged the emperor to send heavy treasures to Qing province and for the time being hold the land of the Three Qi; if it could not be kept, then cross the sea south to escape.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the emperor to send heavy treasures to Qing province and for the time being hold the land of the Three Qi; if it could not be kept, then cross the sea south to escape.

sentences.zh: 雖不從之推計策，然猶以為平原太守，令守河津。

translations.literal: Though they did not follow Zhitui's plan, they still made him governor of Pingyuan and ordered him to guard the river crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Though they did not follow Zhitui's plan, they still made him governor of Pingyuan and ordered him to guard the river crossing.

sentences.zh: 齊亡入周，大象末為御史上士。

translations.literal: When Qi fell he entered Zhou and, at the end of the Great Elephant era, was a senior scholar in the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he entered Zhou and, at the end of the Great Elephant era, was a senior scholar in the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，太子召為學士，甚見禮重。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui the heir summoned him as an academician and treated him with great ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui the heir summoned him as academician and treated him with great ceremony and weight.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾終。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 有文三十卷，撰《家訓》二十篇，並行於世。

translations.literal: He left thirty juan of writings and compiled twenty chapters of Family Instructions, both of which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left thirty juan of writings and compiled twenty chapters of Family Instructions, both of which circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 曾撰《觀我生賦》，文致清遠，其詞曰：

translations.literal: He once composed the rhapsody "Observing My Life," its writing clear and far-reaching; its words say:
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote the rhapsody Observing My Life, its language clear and far-reaching; it begins:

sentences.zh: 仰浮清之藐藐，俯沈奧之茫茫。

translations.literal: Looking up at the distant clarity floating above, looking down at the deep mystery sinking below.
translations.idiomatic: I lift my gaze to the far floating clarity above; I bend my eyes to the deep, sunken mystery below.

sentences.zh: 已生民而立教，乃司牧以分疆。

translations.literal: Having raised the people, he established teaching; thus stewards divided the realms.
translations.idiomatic: Once the people were raised, teaching was set; stewards of the land were appointed to divide the realms.

sentences.zh: 內諸夏而外夷狄，驟五帝而馳三王。

translations.literal: Within were the various Xia, without were the barbarians; swiftly they passed through the Five Emperors and raced the Three Kings.
translations.idiomatic: Within lay the myriad Xia; without, the barbarian tribes—racing through the Five Emperors, galloping past the Three Kings.

sentences.zh: 大道寢而日隱，《小雅》摧以云亡。

translations.literal: The Great Way withdrew and the sun hid, "Minor Odes" was shattered and thus perished.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Way withdrew and the sun went into hiding; the Minor Odes were shattered, and so it perished.

sentences.zh: 哀趙武之作孽，怪漢靈之不祥。

translations.literal: Mourning the crimes of Zhao Wu, marveling at the ill fortune of Han Ling.
translations.idiomatic: I mourn the crimes of Zhao Wu; I marvel at the ill fortune of Han Ling.

sentences.zh: 旄頭玩其金鼎，典午失其珠囊。

translations.literal: The Bushel star toyed with the golden tripod, the Hall of Wu lost its pearl pouch.
translations.idiomatic: The Bushel star played with the golden tripod; the Hall of Wu lost its pearl pouch.

sentences.zh: 瀍澗鞠成沙漠，神華泯為龍荒。

translations.literal: Chan and Jian waters curled into desert, Sacred Splendor extinguished into dragon wilderness.
translations.idiomatic: The Chan and Jian streams curled into desert; Sacred Splendor was extinguished into dragon wilderness.

sentences.zh: 吾王所以東運，我祖於是南翔。

translations.literal: Thus our king moved east; thus our ancestor flew south.
translations.idiomatic: Thus our king moved east; thus our ancestor flew south.

sentences.zh: （晉中宗以瑯邪王南渡，之推瑯邪人，故稱吾王。）

translations.literal: (Jin Central Banner as Langye prince crossed south; Zhitui was a Langye man, hence "our king.")
translations.idiomatic: (The Jin Central Banner, as Prince of Langye, crossed south; Zhitui was a man of Langye, hence "our king.")

sentences.zh: 去琅邪之遷越，宅金陵之舊章。

translations.literal: Leaving Langye's migration to Yue, dwelling in Jinling's old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: We left Langye's flight to Yue and made our home in Jinling's old statutes.

sentences.zh: 作羽儀於新邑，樹杞梓於水鄉。

translations.literal: Making feathered standards in the new capital, planting catalpa and nan in the water country.
translations.idiomatic: We raised feathered standards in the new capital and planted catalpa and nan in the water country.

sentences.zh: 傳清白而勿替，守法度而不忘。

translations.literal: Transmitting purity without decline, holding to law without forgetting.
translations.idiomatic: We transmitted purity without decline and held to law without forgetting.

sentences.zh: 逮微躬之九葉，頹世濟之聲芳。

translations.literal: Reaching my slight self's ninth generation, the declining age's accumulated fragrance of merit.
translations.idiomatic: It reached my slight self in the ninth generation—the declining age's accumulated fragrance of merit.

sentences.zh: 問我良之安在，鐘厭惡於有梁。

translations.literal: I asked where my good days had gone; the bell had grown weary of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: I asked where my good days had gone; the bell had grown weary of Liang.

sentences.zh: 養傅翼之飛獸，

translations.literal: Raising Fu Yi's flying beast,
translations.idiomatic: They raised Fu Yi's flying beast,

sentences.zh: （梁武帝納亡人侯景，授其命，遂為反叛之基。）

translations.literal: (Emperor Wu of Liang took in the fugitive Hou Jing and entrusted him with command; thus the foundation of rebellion was laid.)
translations.idiomatic: (Emperor Wu of Liang took in the fugitive Hou Jing and gave him command—thus the foundation of rebellion was laid.)

sentences.zh: 子貪心之野狼。

translations.literal: and the son, a wolf of greedy heart.
translations.idiomatic: and the son—a wolf of greedy heart.

sentences.zh: （武帝初養臨川王子正德為嗣，生昭明後，正德還本，特封臨賀王。

translations.literal: (At first Emperor Wu raised Linchuan prince Zhengde as heir; after Zhaoming was born, Zhengde was returned to his original status and specially enfeoffed as Prince of Linhe.)
translations.idiomatic: (At first Emperor Wu raised Linchuan prince Zhengde as heir; after Zhaoming was born, Zhengde was returned to his original status and specially enfeoffed as Prince of Linhe.)

sentences.zh: 猶懷怨恨。

translations.literal: He still harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He still harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 徑叛入北而還，積財養士，每有異志也。）

translations.literal: He fled straight north and returned, amassed wealth and nurtured soldiers, and always harbored strange designs.
translations.idiomatic: He fled straight to the north and returned, amassed wealth and nurtured soldiers, and always harbored strange designs.

sentences.zh: 初召禍於絕域，重發釁於蕭墻。

translations.literal: At first he summoned disaster from the outer marches; again he raised strife within the palace walls.
translations.idiomatic: At first he summoned disaster from the outer marches; again he raised strife within the palace walls.

sentences.zh: （正德求征侯景，至新林，叛投景，景立為主，以攻臺城。）

translations.literal: (Zhengde requested to campaign against Hou Jing; reaching Xinlin, he rebelled and threw himself on Jing, who set him up as ruler to attack the Terrace City.)
translations.idiomatic: (Zhengde requested to campaign against Hou Jing; reaching Xinlin, he rebelled and threw himself on Jing, who set him up as ruler to attack the Terrace City.)

sentences.zh: 雖萬里而作限，聊一葦而可航。

translations.literal: Though ten thousand li made a barrier, a single reed could still be sailed.
translations.idiomatic: Though ten thousand li made a barrier, a single reed could still be sailed.

sentences.zh: 指金闕以長鎩，向王路而蹶張。

translations.literal: They pointed their long spears at the golden towers and turned their bows toward the royal road.
translations.idiomatic: They pointed their long spears at the golden towers and turned their bows toward the royal road.

sentences.zh: 勤王逾於十萬，曾不解其扼吭。

translations.literal: Those who came to rescue the throne exceeded a hundred thousand, yet not one knew how to seize the throat.
translations.idiomatic: Those who came to rescue the throne exceeded a hundred thousand, yet not one knew how to seize the throat.

sentences.zh: 嗟將相之骨鯁，皆屈體於犬羊。

translations.literal: Alas—the backbones of generals and ministers all bent their bodies before dogs and goats.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—the backbones of generals and ministers all bent their bodies before dogs and goats.

sentences.zh: 臺城陷，援軍並問訊二宮，致敬於侯景也。

translations.literal: When the Terrace City fell, the relief armies alike inquired after the Two Palaces and paid homage to Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Terrace City fell, the relief armies alike inquired after the Two Palaces and paid homage to Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 武皇忽以厭世，白日黯而無光。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor suddenly grew weary of the world; the white sun dimmed and lost its light.
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Emperor suddenly grew weary of the world; the white sun dimmed and lost its light.

sentences.zh: 旣饗國而五十，何克終之弗康。

translations.literal: Having enjoyed the state for fifty years, how could its end not be unpeaceful?
translations.idiomatic: Having enjoyed the state for fifty years, how could its end not be unpeaceful?

sentences.zh: 嗣君聽於巨猾，每凜然而負芒。

translations.literal: The heir listened to the great villain; each day he shivered, bearing thorns on his back.
translations.idiomatic: The heir listened to the great villain; each day he shivered, bearing thorns on his back.

sentences.zh: 自東晉之違難，寓禮樂於江湘。

translations.literal: Since Eastern Jin's flight from calamity, rites and music have lodged by the Yangzi and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Since Eastern Jin's flight from calamity, rites and music have lodged by the Yangzi and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 迄此幾於三百，左衽浹於四方。

translations.literal: Nearly three hundred years have passed since; left lapels have soaked the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly three hundred years have passed since; left lapels have soaked the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 詠苦胡而永嘆，吟微管而增傷。

translations.literal: I chant the bitter barbarian and sigh without end; I intone the faint pipes and my grief grows.
translations.idiomatic: I chant the bitter barbarian and sigh without end; I intone the faint pipes and my grief grows.

sentences.zh: 世祖赫其斯怒，奮大義於沮漳。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor blazed in his wrath and roused great righteousness at Juzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor blazed in his wrath and roused great righteousness at Juzhang.

sentences.zh: （孝元帝時為荊州刺史。）

translations.literal: (At the time he was Jingzhou inspector.)
translations.idiomatic: (At the time he was Jingzhou inspector.)

sentences.zh: 授犀函與鶴膝，建飛雲及艅艎。

translations.literal: He handed out rhinoceros cases and crane-knee bows, built Flying Cloud and Warship vessels.
translations.idiomatic: He handed out rhinoceros cases and crane-knee bows, built Flying Cloud and Warship vessels.

sentences.zh: 北征兵於漢曲，南發餫於衡陽。

translations.literal: North he raised troops at Han's bend; south he sent grain from Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: North he raised troops at Han's bend; south he sent grain from Hengyang.

sentences.zh: （湘州刺史河東王譽、雍州刺史嶽陽王察並隸荊州都督府。）

translations.literal: (Xiangzhou inspector Prince of Hedong Yu and Yongzhou inspector Prince of Yueyang Cha both fell under the Jingzhou commandery.)
translations.idiomatic: (Xiangzhou inspector Prince of Hedong Yu and Yongzhou inspector Prince of Yueyang Cha both fell under the Jingzhou commandery.)

sentences.zh: 昔承華之賓帝，實兄亡而弟及。

translations.literal: Long ago the heir of Chenghua attended the emperor; in truth the elder brother died and the younger succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the heir of Chenghua attended the emperor; in truth the elder brother died and the younger succeeded.

sentences.zh: （昭明太子薨，乃立晉安王為太子。）

translations.literal: (When Crown Prince Zhaoming died, the Jin'an king was then made crown prince.)
translations.idiomatic: (When Crown Prince Zhaoming died, the Jin'an king was then made crown prince.)

sentences.zh: 逮皇孫之失寵，嘆扶車之不立。

translations.literal: When the legitimate grandson lost favor, I sighed that the heir's carriage could not be set upright.
translations.idiomatic: When the legitimate grandson lost favor, I sighed that the heir's carriage could not be set upright.

sentences.zh: （嫡皇孫驩出封豫章王而薨。）

translations.literal: (The legitimate grandson Huan was enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang and died.)
translations.idiomatic: (The legitimate grandson Huan was enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang and died.)

sentences.zh: 間王道之多難，各私求於京邑。

translations.literal: The royal way knew many hardships; each sought his private gain in the capital districts.
translations.idiomatic: The royal way knew many hardships; each sought his private gain in the capital districts.

sentences.zh: 襄陽阻其銅符，長沙閉其玉粒。

translations.literal: Xiangyang blocked its bronze tally; Changsha shut its jade grain.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang blocked its bronze tally; Changsha shut its jade grain.

sentences.zh: （河東、嶽陽皆昭明子。）

translations.literal: (Hedong and Yueyang were both sons of Zhaoming.)
translations.idiomatic: (Hedong and Yueyang were both sons of Zhaoming.)

sentences.zh: 遽自戰於其地，豈大勛之暇集。

translations.literal: They hastened to fight on their own ground; how could great merit find leisure to gather?
translations.idiomatic: They hastened to fight on their own ground; how could great merit find leisure to gather?

sentences.zh: 子旣殞而侄攻，昆亦圍而叔襲。

translations.literal: The son had fallen and the nephew attacked; the elder brother was besieged and the uncle struck.
translations.idiomatic: The son had fallen and the nephew attacked; the elder brother was besieged and the uncle struck.

sentences.zh: 褚乘城而宵下，杜倒戈而夜入。

translations.literal: Chu descended the walls by night; Du turned his spears and entered by night.
translations.idiomatic: Chu descended the walls by night; Du turned his spears and entered by night.

sentences.zh: （孝元以河東不供船艎，乃遣世子方等為刺史。

translations.literal: (Emperor Yuan, because Hedong would not supply ships, sent the heir Fangdeng out as inspector.)
translations.idiomatic: (Emperor Yuan, because Hedong would not supply ships, sent the heir Fangdeng out as inspector.)

sentences.zh: 大軍掩至，河東不暇遣拒。

translations.literal: The great army came suddenly; Hedong had no time to send resistance.
translations.idiomatic: The great army came suddenly; Hedong had no time to send resistance.

sentences.zh: 世子信用群小，貪其子女玉帛，遂欲攻之，故河東急而逆戰，世子為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: The heir trusted petty men, coveted their daughters, jade, and silks, and thus wished to attack them; so Hedong was pressed and fought in rebellion, and the heir was killed by mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: The heir trusted petty men, coveted their daughters, jade, and silks, and thus wished to attack them; so Hedong was pressed and fought in rebellion, and the heir was killed by mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 孝元發怒，又使鮑泉圍河東。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan grew angry and again sent Bao Quan to besiege Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan grew angry and again sent Bao Quan to besiege Hedong.

sentences.zh: 而岳陽宣言大獵，即擁衆襲荊州求解湘州之圍。

translations.literal: Yueyang proclaimed a great hunt and at once led his host to strike Jingzhou, seeking to lift the siege of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yueyang proclaimed a great hunt and at once led his host to strike Jingzhou, seeking to lift the siege of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時襄陽杜岸兄弟怨其見劫，不以實告，又不義此行，率兵八千夜降，岳陽於是遁走。

translations.literal: At the time the Xiangyang brothers Du An and Du Mu resented being seized and did not report the truth; they also thought the campaign unjust, and led eight thousand men to surrender by night—Yueyang therefore fled.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Xiangyang brothers Du An and Du Mu resented being seized and did not report the truth; they also thought the campaign unjust, and led eight thousand men to surrender by night—Yueyang therefore fled.

sentences.zh: 河東府褚顯族據投岳陽。

translations.literal: Chu Xianzu of the Hedong establishment surrendered to Yueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Xianzu of the Hedong establishment surrendered to Yueyang.

sentences.zh: 所以湘州見陷也。）

translations.literal: Thus Xiangzhou was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Xiangzhou was taken.

sentences.zh: 行路彎弓而含笑，骨肉相誅而涕泣。

translations.literal: Travelers bent their bows and smiled; flesh and bone slew one another and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers bent their bows and smiled; flesh and bone slew one another and wept.

sentences.zh: 周旦其猶病諸，孝武悔而焉及。

translations.literal: Would even the Duke of Zhou still be ill at this? Emperor Wu of Han repented—yet how could he reach it?
translations.idiomatic: Would even the Duke of Zhou still be ill at this? Emperor Wu of Han repented—yet how could he reach it?

sentences.zh: 方幕府之事殷，謬見擇於人群。

translations.literal: When the headquarters' affairs were pressing, I was wrongly chosen from the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: When the headquarters' affairs were pressing, I was wrongly chosen from the crowd.

sentences.zh: 未成冠而登仕，財解履以從軍。

translations.literal: Before the cap was complete I entered office; barely untying my shoes I followed the army.
translations.idiomatic: Before the cap was complete I entered office; barely untying my shoes I followed the army.

sentences.zh: （時年十九，釋褐湘東國右常侍，以軍功加鎮西墨曹參軍。）

translations.literal: (At the time he was nineteen; he doffed the hemp and became right regular attendant of the Xiangdong state, and for military merit was added as ink-collar aide of the army pacifying the west.)
translations.idiomatic: (At the time he was nineteen; he doffed the hemp and became right regular attendant of the Xiangdong state, and for military merit was added as ink-collar aide of the army pacifying the west.)

sentences.zh: 非社稷之能衛。

translations.literal: Not able to guard the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Not able to guard the altars of state.

sentences.zh: （童汪綺）

translations.literal: (Tong Wangqi)
translations.idiomatic: (Tong Wangqi)

sentences.zh: 闕僅書記於階闥，罕羽翼於風雲。

translations.literal: I lacked only secretarial duties at the inner gate; I rarely had wingbeats in wind and clouds.
translations.idiomatic: I lacked only secretarial duties at the inner gate; I rarely had wingbeats in wind and clouds.

sentences.zh: 及荊王之定霸，始讎恥而圖雪。

translations.literal: When the King of Jing fixed his hegemony, I at last turned shame into a plan for vengeance.
translations.idiomatic: When the King of Jing fixed his hegemony, I at last turned shame into a plan for vengeance.

sentences.zh: 舟師次乎武昌，撫軍鎮於夏汭。

translations.literal: The fleet anchored at Wuchang; the pacifying army garrisoned at Xia'er.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet anchored at Wuchang; the pacifying army garrisoned at Xia'er.

sentences.zh: （時遣徐州刺史徐文盛領二萬人屯武昌蘆州拒侯景將任約，又第二子綏寧度方諸為世子，拜中撫軍將軍、郢州刺史，以盛聲勢。）

translations.literal: (At the time he sent Xuzhou inspector Xu Wensheng with twenty thousand men to camp at Wuchang's Luzhou to resist Hou Jing's general Ren Yue; his second son Suining duke Fangzhu was made heir, appointed Central Pacifying Army general and Yingzhou inspector, to swell the momentum.)
translations.idiomatic: (At the time he sent Xuzhou inspector Xu Wensheng with twenty thousand men to camp at Wuchang's Luzhou to resist Hou Jing's general Ren Yue; his second son Suining duke Fangzhu was made heir, appointed Central Pacifying Army general and Yingzhou inspector, to swell the momentum.)

sentences.zh: 濫充選於多士，在參戎之盛列。

translations.literal: I was rashly placed among the many talents in the ranks of those joining the army.
translations.idiomatic: I was rashly placed among the many talents in the ranks of those joining the army.

sentences.zh: 慚四白之調護，廁六友之談說。

translations.literal: Ashamed to tune and nurse the four whites, I stood in the corner of the six friends' talk.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed to tune and nurse the four whites, I stood in the corner of the six friends' talk.

sentences.zh: （時遷中撫軍外兵參軍，掌管記，與文拚、劉民英等與世子遊處。）

translations.literal: (At the time he was transferred to Central Pacifying Army outer-troops aide, in charge of records, and with Wen Pin, Liu Minying, and others kept company with the heir.)
translations.idiomatic: (At the time he was transferred to Central Pacifying Army outer-troops aide, in charge of records, and with Wen Pin, Liu Minying, and others kept company with the heir.)

sentences.zh: 雖形就而心和，匪余懷之所說。

translations.literal: Though the form drew near and the heart was harmonious, it was not what my breast delighted in.
translations.idiomatic: Though the form drew near and the heart was harmonious, it was not what my breast delighted in.

sentences.zh: 繄深宮之生貴，矧垂堂與倚衡。

translations.literal: Alas—the noble born in the deep palace; how much more those who lean on the hall and the scale!
