translations.idiomatic: Alas—the noble born in the deep palace; how much more those who lean on the hall and the scale!

sentences.zh: 欲推心以厲物，樹幼齒以先聲。

translations.literal: He wished to lay bare his heart to stiffen others and set the young teeth ahead to sound first.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to lay bare his heart to stiffen others and set the young teeth ahead to sound first.

sentences.zh: （中撫軍時年十五。）

translations.literal: (The Central Pacifying Army was then fifteen sui.)
translations.idiomatic: (The Central Pacifying Army was then fifteen sui.)

sentences.zh: 愾敷求之不器，乃畫地而取名。

translations.literal: Indignant that his wide search found no fit vessel, he drew on the ground to take a name.
translations.idiomatic: Indignant that his wide search found no fit vessel, he drew on the ground to take a name.

sentences.zh: 仗禦武於文吏，

translations.literal: He relied on martial defense in a literary officer,
translations.idiomatic: He relied on martial defense in a literary officer,

sentences.zh: （以虞預為郢州司馬，領城防事。）

translations.literal: (making Yu Yu Yingzhou marshal, in charge of city defense.)
translations.idiomatic: (making Yu Yu Yingzhou marshal, in charge of city defense.)

sentences.zh: 委軍政於儒生。

translations.literal: and entrusted military affairs to a Confucian scholar.
translations.idiomatic: and entrusted military affairs to a Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: （以鮑泉為郢州行事，總攝州府也。）

translations.literal: (He made Bao Quan acting Yingzhou administrator, in overall charge of the prefecture.)
translations.idiomatic: (He made Bao Quan acting Yingzhou administrator, in overall charge of the prefecture.)

sentences.zh: 值白波之猝駭，逢赤舌之燒城。

translations.literal: I met the white wave's sudden terror and encountered the red tongue burning the city.
translations.idiomatic: I met the white wave's sudden terror and encountered the red tongue burning the city.

sentences.zh: 王凝坐而對寇，向詡拱以臨兵。

translations.literal: Wang Ning sat facing the foe; Xiang Xu folded his hands before the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ning sat facing the foe; Xiang Xu folded his hands before the troops.

sentences.zh: （任約為文盛所困，侯景自上救之，舟艦弊漏，軍饑卒疲，數戰失利。

translations.literal: (Ren Yue was pressed by Wensheng; Hou Jing came up himself to rescue him. The ships leaked and were worn; the army was hungry and the soldiers weary; battle after battle was lost.)
translations.idiomatic: (Ren Yue was pressed by Wensheng; Hou Jing came up himself to rescue him. The ships leaked and were worn; the army was hungry and the soldiers weary; battle after battle was lost.)

sentences.zh: 乃令宋子仙、任約步道偷郢州城，預無備，故陷賊。）

translations.literal: He then ordered Song Zixian and Ren Yue to march by land and steal into Yingzhou city; there was no preparation, and so it fell to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Song Zixian and Ren Yue to march by land and steal into Yingzhou city; there was no preparation, and so it fell to the bandits.

sentences.zh: 莫不變蝯而化鵠，皆自取首以破腦。

translations.literal: None failed to change from gibbon to swan and each took his own head to break his skull.
translations.idiomatic: None failed to change from gibbon to swan and each took his own head to break his skull.

sentences.zh: 將睥睨於渚宮，先憑陵於他道。

translations.literal: They were about to look down on the Palace of Isles; first they overran the other road.
translations.idiomatic: They were about to look down on the Palace of Isles; first they overran the other road.

sentences.zh: （景欲攻荊州，路由巴陵。）

translations.literal: (Jing wished to attack Jingzhou; the route passed through Baling.)
translations.idiomatic: (Jing wished to attack Jingzhou; the route passed through Baling.)

sentences.zh: 懿永寧之龍蟠，

translations.literal: Yi of Yongning coiled like a dragon;
translations.idiomatic: Yi of Yongning coiled like a dragon;

sentences.zh: （永寧公王僧辯據巴陵城，善於守禦，景不能進。）

translations.literal: (Duke of Yongning Wang Sengbian held Baling city, skilled in defense; Jing could not advance.)
translations.idiomatic: (Duke of Yongning Wang Sengbian held Baling city, skilled in defense; Jing could not advance.)

sentences.zh: 奇護軍之電掃。

translations.literal: the odd Protector of the Army swept like lightning.
translations.idiomatic: the odd Protector of the Army swept like lightning.

sentences.zh: （護軍將軍陸法和破任約於赤亭湖，景退走，大潰。）

translations.literal: (Protector of the Army Lu Fahe broke Ren Yue at Chiting Lake; Jing retreated and was utterly routed.)
translations.idiomatic: (Protector of the Army Lu Fahe broke Ren Yue at Chiting Lake; Jing retreated and was utterly routed.)

sentences.zh: 奔虜快其餘毒，縲囚膏乎野草。

translations.literal: Fleeing captives rejoiced in their remaining poison; bound prisoners were greased on the wild grass.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing captives rejoiced in their remaining poison; bound prisoners were greased on the wild grass.

sentences.zh: 幸先生之無勸，賴滕公之我保。

translations.literal: I was spared thanks to the Master's not urging; I was preserved thanks to Duke Teng's regard for me.
translations.idiomatic: I was spared thanks to the Master's not urging; I was preserved thanks to Duke Teng's regard for me.

sentences.zh: （之推執在景軍，例當見殺。

translations.literal: (Zhitui was held in Jing's army and by rule should have been killed.)
translations.idiomatic: (Zhitui was held in Jing's army and by rule should have been killed.)

sentences.zh: 景行臺郎中王則初無舊識，再三救護，獲免，囚以還都。）

translations.literal: Jing's traveling-office gentleman Wang Ze had at first no old acquaintance with him, yet again and again protected him; he was spared and imprisoned and sent back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's traveling-office gentleman Wang Ze had at first no old acquaintance with him, yet again and again protected him; he was spared and imprisoned and sent back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 剟鬼錄於岱宗，招歸魂於蒼昊。

translations.literal: I struck the ghost record at Mount Dai and summoned the returning soul to the azure heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I struck the ghost record at Mount Dai and summoned the returning soul to the azure heaven.

sentences.zh: 時解衣訖而獲全。

translations.literal: At the time, once I had stripped my clothes I was wholly spared.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, once I had stripped my clothes I was wholly spared.

sentences.zh: 荷性命之重賜，銜若人以終老。

translations.literal: I bore the heavy gift of life; I cherished such a man to my old age.
translations.idiomatic: I bore the heavy gift of life; I cherished such a man to my old age.

sentences.zh: 賊棄甲而來復，肆觜距之雕鳶。

translations.literal: The bandits cast off their armor and came again, baring beak and talon like carved kites.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits cast off their armor and came again, baring beak and talon like carved kites.

sentences.zh: 積假履而弒帝，憑衣霧以上天。

translations.literal: He piled up leave-slips in straw sandals to murder the emperor, and rode mist-veiled robes toward heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Piling up leave-slips in straw sandals, he murdered the emperor; riding robe-mist, he claimed heaven.

sentences.zh: 用速災於四月，奚聞道之十年。

translations.literal: He brought swift disaster in the fourth month—how could one hear of the Way's ten years?
translations.idiomatic: Swift disaster in the fourth month—what of the Way's ten-year promise?

sentences.zh: （臺城陷後，梁武曾獨坐嘆曰：「侯景於文為小人百日天子。

translations.literal: (After Terrace City fell, Emperor Wu of Liang once sat alone and sighed: "In wen Hou Jing is a petty man's hundred-day Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: (After Terrace City fell, Emperor Wu of Liang sat alone and sighed: "In wen, Hou Jing is a petty man's hundred-day Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」及景以大寶二年十一月十九日僭位，至明年三月十九日棄城逃竄，是一百二十日，掞天道紀大數，故文為百日。

translations.literal: " When Jing illegally took the throne on the nineteenth day of the eleventh month in the second year of Dabao, until the nineteenth day of the third month the next year he abandoned the city and fled—a hundred and twenty days; by the Way of Heaven's reckoning of great numbers, in wen it is "a hundred days."
translations.idiomatic: " When Jing usurped the throne on the nineteenth of the eleventh month, year two of Dabao, and on the nineteenth of the third month the next year abandoned the city and fled, it was a hundred and twenty days; by Heaven's great reckoning, in wen that reads as a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 」言與公孫述俱稟十二，而旬歲不同。）

translations.literal: " The words, like Gongsun Shu's, both receive twelve—yet ten-day years differ.)
translations.idiomatic: " The phrase, like Gongsun Shu's, shares twelve—yet the ten-day count differs.)

sentences.zh: 就狄俘於舊壤，陷戎俗於來旋。

translations.literal: Taken captive by Di barbarians on the old soil, sunk in barbarian ways on the homeward turn.
translations.idiomatic: Taken captive by Di on native soil, sunk in barbarian custom on the road home.

sentences.zh: 慨黍離於清廟，愴麥秀於空廛。

translations.literal: Grieving "Pleasant Valley" in the clear temple, mourning "Wheat in Ear" in empty market stalls.
translations.idiomatic: He grieved "Pleasant Valley" in the clear temple, mourned "Wheat in Ear" in empty stalls.

sentences.zh: 鼗鼓臥而不考，景鐘毀而莫懸。

translations.literal: Toy drums lie unstruck; the great bell is shattered and no longer hung.
translations.idiomatic: Toy drums lie unplayed; the great bell lies broken, unhung.

sentences.zh: 野蕭條以橫骨，邑闃寂而無煙。

translations.literal: Wilds desolate with bones strewn across them; towns silent, without smoke.
translations.idiomatic: The wilds were desolate, bones strewn across them; towns stood silent, without smoke.

sentences.zh: 疇百家之或在，

translations.literal: Of the hundred clans, perhaps some still exist,
translations.idiomatic: Of the hundred clans, perhaps some still survived,

sentences.zh: （中原冠帶隨晉渡江者百家，故江東有《百譜》，至是在都者覆滅略盡。）

translations.literal: (A hundred families of Central Plains gentry who crossed the Yangzi with the Jin—hence Jiangdong had the Hundred Genealogies; those in the capital were almost entirely destroyed.)
translations.idiomatic: (A hundred families of Central Plains gentry who crossed the Yangzi with Jin—hence Jiangdong kept the Hundred Genealogies; those still in the capital were nearly all destroyed.)

sentences.zh: 覆五宗而翦焉。

translations.literal: five generations overthrown and cut down.
translations.idiomatic: five generations were overthrown and cut down.

sentences.zh: 獨昭君之哀奏，唯翁主之悲弦。

translations.literal: Only Princess Zhaojun's lament was played; only Princess Wengzhu's mournful strings.
translations.idiomatic: Only Princess Zhaojun's lament sounded; only Princess Wengzhu's grieving strings.

sentences.zh: （公主子女見辱見讎。）

translations.literal: (The princesses' sons and daughters were shamed and killed.)
translations.idiomatic: (The princesses' sons and daughters were shamed and slain.)

sentences.zh: 經長干以掩抑，

translations.literal: Passing Changgan in suppressed grief,
translations.idiomatic: He passed Changgan in suppressed grief,

sentences.zh: （長干舊顏家巷。）

translations.literal: (Changgan was the old Yan family lane.)
translations.idiomatic: (Changgan was the old lane of the Yan house.)

sentences.zh: 展白下以流連。

translations.literal: unfolding through Baixia in lingering sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: and lingered through Baixia in sorrow that would not leave.

sentences.zh: （靖侯以下七世墳塋皆在白下。）

translations.literal: (Seven generations of tombs from Jing Marquis downward all lay at Baixia.)
translations.idiomatic: (Seven generations of tombs from Jing Marquis down all lay at Baixia.)

sentences.zh: 深燕雀之餘思，感桑梓之遺虔。

translations.literal: Deeply feeling what swallows and sparrows recall, moved by native earth's old devotion.
translations.idiomatic: He felt deeply what swallows and sparrows remember, and was moved by the old devotion of native earth.

sentences.zh: 得此心於尼甫，信茲言乎仲宣。

translations.literal: He found this heart in Confucius; he trusted these words of Wang Can.
translations.idiomatic: In Confucius he found this heart; in Wang Can he trusted these words.

sentences.zh: 逷西土之有衆，資方叔以薄伐。

translations.literal: From afar the western lands had multitudes; he relied on Fang Shu for the light campaign.
translations.idiomatic: From afar the western lands had hosts; he leaned on Fang Shu for a light punitive strike.

sentences.zh: （永寧公以司徒為大都督。）

translations.literal: (The Duke of Yongning, as Minister over the Masses, was Grand Commander.)
translations.idiomatic: (The Duke of Yongning served as Minister over the Masses and Grand Commander.)

sentences.zh: 撫鳴劍而雷咤，振雄旗而雲窣。

translations.literal: He stroked ringing swords with thunder's roar and shook heroic banners like scudding clouds.
translations.idiomatic: He stroked ringing swords till thunder roared, shook heroic banners till clouds scudded.

sentences.zh: 千里追其飛走，三載窮於巢窟。

translations.literal: A thousand li he chased their flight; three years he exhausted their nests and dens.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand li he chased their flight; three years he wore out their nests and dens.

sentences.zh: 屠蚩尤於東郡，掛郅支於北闕。

translations.literal: He slew Chiyou in the eastern commandery and hung Zhizhi's head on the northern gate.
translations.idiomatic: He slew Chiyou in the eastern commandery and hung Zhizhi's head on the northern gate.

sentences.zh: （旣斬侯景，烹尸於建業市，百姓食之，至於肉盡齕骨，傳首荊州，懸於都街。

translations.literal: (After beheading Hou Jing, they boiled the corpse in the Jiankang market; the people ate until the flesh was gone and gnawed the bones; the head was sent to Jingzhou and hung on the capital street.
translations.idiomatic: (After Hou Jing was beheaded, his corpse was boiled in the Jiankang market; commoners ate until the flesh was gone and gnawed the bones; the head was sent to Jingzhou and hung on the capital street.

sentences.zh: 弔幽魂之冤枉，掃園陵之蕪沒。

translations.literal: He mourned wronged souls in the dark, swept overgrown imperial mounds.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned wronged shades, swept imperial mounds choked with weeds.

sentences.zh: 殷道是以再興，夏祀於焉不忽。

translations.literal: Thus the Yin way was revived; Xia sacrifices were not neglected thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Yin way rose again; Xia sacrifices were not neglected.

sentences.zh: 但遺恨於炎崑，火延宮而累月。

translations.literal: But regret remained for Flame-Kun: fire spread through the palace for months on end.
translations.idiomatic: But regret lingered for Flame-Kun—fire ran through the palace for months.

sentences.zh: （侯景旣走，義師採櫓失火，燒宮殿蕩盡也。）

translations.literal: (After Hou Jing fled, the loyalist army, gathering rudders, accidentally set fire and burned the palaces utterly.)
translations.idiomatic: (After Hou Jing fled, the loyalist army, gathering rudders, lost control of fire and burned the palaces to nothing.)

sentences.zh: 指余櫂於兩東，侍升壇之五讓。

translations.literal: I pointed my oars toward the two easts and attended the five deferrals on the ascending altar.
translations.idiomatic: I pointed my oars toward the two easts and attended the five deferrals at the ascending altar.

sentences.zh: 欽漢官之復覩，赴楚民之有望。

translations.literal: I rejoiced to see Han officials again and answered the Chu people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: I rejoiced to see Han officials again and answered what the Chu people had hoped for.

sentences.zh: 攝絳衣以奏言，忝黃散於官謗。

translations.literal: Wearing crimson robes I presented memorials, humbly holding Yellow Gate duties amid office slander.
translations.idiomatic: In crimson robes I presented memorials, humbly bearing Yellow Gate office amid slander.

sentences.zh: （時為散騎侍郎，奏舍人事也。）

translations.literal: (At the time he was Irregular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, presenting affairs of the lodge.)
translations.idiomatic: (At the time he was irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry, presenting lodge affairs.)

sentences.zh: 或校石渠之文，

translations.literal: Sometimes he collated Stone Canal texts,
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he collated Stone Canal texts,

sentences.zh: （王司徒表送秘閤舊事八萬卷，乃詔比校，部分為正禦、副御、重雜三本。

translations.literal: (Minister Wang memorialized sending eighty thousand juan of secret-repository old records; an edict ordered comparison and collation, divided into principal, secondary, and miscellaneous sets.
translations.idiomatic: (Minister Wang memorialized sending eighty thousand juan of secret-repository records; an edict ordered collation into principal, secondary, and miscellaneous sets.

sentences.zh: 左民尚書周弘正、黃門郎彭僧朗、直省學士王珪、戴陵校經部，左僕射王褒、吏部尚書宗懷正、員外郎顏之推、直學士劉仁英校史部，廷尉卿殷不害、御史中丞王孝紀、中書郎鄧藎、金部郎中徐報校子部，右衛將軍庾信、中書郎王固、晉安王文學宗善業、直省學士周確校集部也。）

translations.literal: Zhou Hongzheng, Minister of the Left for the People, Peng Senglang, gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Wang Gui and Dai Ling, direct-province scholars, collated the Classics section; Wang Bao, Left Vice Director, Zong Huaizheng, Minister of Personnel, Yan Zhitui, irregular gentleman, Liu Renying, direct scholar, collated History; Yin Buhai, Director of Justice, Wang Xiaoji, censor-in-chief, Deng Shen, secretariat gentleman, Xu Bao, director of the Gold Bureau, collated Masters; Yu Xin, General of the Right Guard, Wang Gu, literary aide to Prince of Jin'an, Zong Shanye, Zhou Que, direct scholars, collated Collectanea.)
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Hongzheng of the Left for the People, Peng Senglang of the Yellow Gate, Wang Gui and Dai Ling of the direct province collated Classics; Wang Bao, Left Vice Director, Zong Huaizheng of Personnel, Yan Zhitui as irregular gentleman, Liu Renying as direct scholar collated History; Yin Buhai of Justice, censor-in-chief Wang Xiaoji, Deng Shen of the Secretariat, Xu Bao of the Gold Bureau collated Masters; Yu Xin of the Right Guard, Wang Gu, Zong Shanye of Jin'an, Zhou Que collated Collectanea.)

sentences.zh: 時參柏梁之唱。

translations.literal: at times joining the Bo Liang hymns.
translations.idiomatic: at times joining the Bo Liang hymns.

sentences.zh: 顧甂甌之不算，濯波濤而無量。

translations.literal: He regarded jars and caldrons as beyond counting and washed in waves without measure.
translations.idiomatic: He looked on jars and caldrons as beyond count and bathed in waves without measure.

sentences.zh: 屬瀟湘之負罪，

translations.literal: When Xiangyang bore guilt,
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangyang bore guilt,

sentences.zh: （陸納。）

translations.literal: (Lu Na.)
translations.idiomatic: (Lu Na.)

sentences.zh: 兼岷峨之自王。

translations.literal: and Min-Emei proclaimed itself king,
translations.idiomatic: and Min-Emei made itself king,

sentences.zh: （武陵王。）

translations.literal: (the Prince of Wuling.)
translations.idiomatic: (the Prince of Wuling.)

sentences.zh: 竚旣定以鳴鸞，修東都之大壯。

translations.literal: he waited till things were settled to ring the phoenix carriage and restore the Eastern Capital's great magnificence.
translations.idiomatic: he waited till order returned to ring the phoenix carriage and rebuild the Eastern Capital's grandeur.

sentences.zh: （詔司農卿黃文超營殿。）

translations.literal: (An edict ordered Minister of Agriculture Huang Chao to build the halls.)
translations.idiomatic: (An edict ordered Minister of Agriculture Huang Chao to build the halls.)

sentences.zh: 驚北風之復起，慘南歌之不暢。

translations.literal: Startled that the north wind rose again, grieved that southern songs would not flow.
translations.idiomatic: He was startled when the north wind rose again, grieved when southern songs would not flow.

sentences.zh: （秦兵繼來。）

translations.literal: (Qin troops came in succession.)
translations.idiomatic: (Qin troops came again and again.)

sentences.zh: 守金城之湯池，轉絳宮之玉帳。

translations.literal: He held the golden city's boiling moat and turned the crimson palace's jade canopy.
translations.idiomatic: He held the golden city's boiling moat and turned the crimson palace's jade canopy.

sentences.zh: （孝元自曉陰陽兵法，初聞賊來，頗為厭勝，被圍之後，每嘆息，知必敗。）

translations.literal: (Emperor Xiaoyuan understood yin-yang and military arts; when he first heard rebels were coming he used much exorcism; after the siege, he sighed repeatedly, knowing defeat was certain.)
translations.idiomatic: (Emperor Xiaoyuan knew yin-yang and military arts; when rebels first came he relied on exorcism; under siege he sighed again and again, knowing he must fall.)

sentences.zh: 徒有道而師直，翻無名之不抗。

translations.literal: He had the Way and his army was upright—yet reversed, without a righteous name he could not resist.
translations.idiomatic: He had the Way and a straight army—yet without a righteous name he could not hold out.

sentences.zh: （孝元與宇文丞相斷金結和，無何見滅，是師出無名。）

translations.literal: (Xiaoyuan and Chancellor Yuwen pledged like severed metal; soon he was destroyed—an army without righteous name.)
translations.idiomatic: (Xiaoyuan and Chancellor Yuwen pledged like severed metal; soon he was destroyed—the campaign had no righteous name.)

sentences.zh: 民百萬而囚虜，書千兩而煙煬。

translations.literal: A million people became captives; a thousand cartloads of books went up in smoke and ash.
translations.idiomatic: A million people were taken captive; a thousand cartloads of books burned to ash.

sentences.zh: 溥天之下，斯文盡喪。

translations.literal: Under the broad heaven, all culture perished.
translations.idiomatic: Under broad heaven, all culture perished.

sentences.zh: （北於墳籍少於江東三分之一，梁氏剝亂，散逸湮亡。

translations.literal: (In the north, tomb records were less than a third of Jiangdong's; Liang's stripping and chaos scattered and drowned them.
translations.idiomatic: (In the north, tomb records were less than a third of Jiangdong's; Liang's stripping and chaos scattered and drowned them.

sentences.zh: 唯孝元鳩合，通重十餘萬，史籍以來，未之有也。

translations.literal: Only Xiaoyuan gathered them, more than a hundred thousand in all—unprecedented in historical records.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xiaoyuan gathered them—more than a hundred thousand in all—unprecedented in the records.

sentences.zh: 兵敗悉焚之，海內無復書府。）

translations.literal: Defeat burned them all; within the seas there were no book houses again.)
translations.idiomatic: Defeat burned them all; within the seas there were no book houses again.)

sentences.zh: 憐嬰孺之何辜，矜老疾之無狀。

translations.literal: He pitied infants and children—what was their crime? He grieved for the old and sick—without proper form.
translations.idiomatic: He pitied infants—what crime had they? He grieved for the old and sick left without proper burial.

sentences.zh: 奪諸懷而棄草，踣於途而受掠。

translations.literal: Seized from arms and abandoned to the grass, they stumbled on the roads and suffered plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Torn from arms and cast on the grass, they fell on the roads and were plundered.

sentences.zh: 冤乘輿之殘酷，軫人神之無狀。

translations.literal: He resented cruelty to the imperial carriage and grieved the lawless state of man and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: He resented cruelty to the imperial carriage and grieved that man and spirits had lost all law.

sentences.zh: 載下車以黜喪，揜藳桐棺之藳葬。

translations.literal: He mounted the cart of dismissal for mourning and covered the rush-and-tung coffin's sparse burial.
translations.idiomatic: He rode the cart of dismissal in mourning and covered the rush-and-tung coffin's sparse burial.

sentences.zh: 雲無心以容與，風懷憤而憀悢。

translations.literal: Clouds without heart drifted along; wind harbored rage and restlessness.
translations.idiomatic: Clouds drifted without heart; wind nursed rage and would not rest.

sentences.zh: 井伯飲牛於秦中，子卿牧羊於海上。

translations.literal: Jing Bo drank ox in the Qin region; Ziqing herded sheep by the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Bo drank with his ox in Qin; Ziqing herded sheep by the sea.

sentences.zh: 留釧之妻，人銜其斷絕；

translations.literal: The sword-belt wife—people mourned her severance;
translations.idiomatic: The sword-belt wife—people mourned her severance;

sentences.zh: 擊磬之子，家纏其悲愴。

translations.literal: the stone-chime player's son—families wound themselves in grief.
translations.idiomatic: the stone-chime player's son—households wrapped themselves in grief.

sentences.zh: 小臣恥其獨死，實有愧於胡顏，牽屙疻而就路，

translations.literal: This petty minister shamed to die alone, truly ashamed before barbarian faces, leading lame foot toward the road,
translations.idiomatic: This petty minister shamed to die alone, ashamed before barbarian faces, dragging lame foot toward the road,

sentences.zh: （時患腳氣。）

translations.literal: (at the time suffering from foot qi.)
translations.idiomatic: (at the time he suffered from foot qi.)

sentences.zh: 策駑蹇以入關。

translations.literal: driving a lame nag into the pass.
translations.idiomatic: driving a lame nag into the pass.

sentences.zh: （官疲驢瘦馬。）

translations.literal: (Post horses exhausted, donkeys and horses thin.)
translations.idiomatic: (Post horses were exhausted; donkeys and horses were thin.)

sentences.zh: 下無景而屬蹈，上有尋而亟搴。

translations.literal: Below, no shadow yet he must tread; above, a span yet he must climb quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Below there was no shadow yet he had to tread on; above, a span yet he had to climb fast.

sentences.zh: 嗟飛蓬之日永，恨流梗之無還。

translations.literal: Alas—the flying tumbleweed's days are long; hatred—the drifting stem never returns.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—the flying tumbleweed's days stretch on; hatred—the drifting stem never comes home.

sentences.zh: 若乃玄牛之旌，九龍之路，土圭測影，璇璣審度。

translations.literal: As for black-ox banners, nine-dragon roads, earth gui measuring shadow, armillary sphere verifying degrees—
translations.idiomatic: As for black-ox banners, nine-dragon roads, the earth gui measuring shadow, the armillary sphere fixing degrees—

sentences.zh: 或先聖之規模，乍前王之典故。

translations.literal: sometimes former sages' models, sometimes former kings' statutes.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes a former sage's model, sometimes a former king's statute.

sentences.zh: 與神鼎而偕沒，切仙宮之永慕。

translations.literal: They perished together with the divine tripod; one cuts off the immortal palace forever missed.
translations.idiomatic: They sank with the divine tripod; the immortal palace was cut off forever, only missed.

sentences.zh: 爾其十六國之風教，七十代之州壤，接耳目而不通，詠圖書而可想。

translations.literal: Then the sixteen kingdoms' customs, seventy generations' commanderies—heard and seen but unreachable; sung in maps and books, only imaginable.
translations.idiomatic: The sixteen kingdoms' customs, seventy generations' commanderies—heard and seen but unreachable; sung in maps and books, only imaginable.

sentences.zh: 何黎氓之匪昔，徒山川之猶曩。

translations.literal: Why are the black-haired folk not as of old? Only mountains and rivers remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Why are the people not as they were? Only mountains and rivers stay as before.

sentences.zh: 每結思於江湖，將取弊於羅網。

translations.literal: Each time he knotted thoughts on rivers and lakes, about to take harm from nets.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he knotted his thoughts on rivers and lakes, about to be taken in nets.

sentences.zh: 聆代竹之哀怨，聽出塞之嘹朗。

translations.literal: He heard bamboo of another age's grief and listened to the frontier song's clear cry.
translations.idiomatic: He heard another age's bamboo grief and listened to the frontier song's clear cry.

sentences.zh: 對皓月以增愁，臨芳樽而無賞。

translations.literal: Facing the bright moon, sorrow grew; before the fragrant cup, no delight.
translations.idiomatic: Facing the bright moon, sorrow grew; before the fragrant cup, there was no delight.

sentences.zh: 自太清之內釁，彼天齊而外侵。

translations.literal: From strife within Great Clarity, they from Heavenly Qi invaded from without.
translations.idiomatic: From strife within Great Clarity, Heavenly Qi invaded from without.

sentences.zh: 始蹙國於淮滸，遂壓境於江潯。

translations.literal: First they cramped the state at the Huai shore; then pressed the border at the Yangzi bank.
translations.idiomatic: First they cramped the state at the Huai shore; then pressed the border at the Yangzi bank.

sentences.zh: （侯景之亂，齊氏深斥梁家土宇，江北、淮北唯餘廬江、晉熙、高唐、新蔡、西陽、齊昌數郡。

translations.literal: (In Hou Jing's rebellion, Qi deeply stripped Liang's territory; north and south of the Huai only Lujiang, Jinxi, Gaotang, Xincai, Xiyang, and Qichang commanderies remained.
translations.idiomatic: (In Hou Jing's rebellion, Qi deeply stripped Liang's territory; north and south of the Huai only Lujiang, Jinxi, Gaotang, Xincai, Xiyang, and Qichang remained.

sentences.zh: 至孝元之敗，於是盡矣，以江為界也。）

translations.literal: At Xiaoyuan's defeat, then all was gone—the Yangzi became the border.)
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaoyuan's defeat, all was gone—the Yangzi became the border.)

sentences.zh: 獲仁厚之麟角，剋儁秀之南金。

translations.literal: They gained benevolent and thick horn of qilin and overcame outstanding southern gold.
translations.idiomatic: They gained the qilin's benevolent horn and overcame outstanding southern gold.

sentences.zh: 爰衆旅而納主，車五百以敻臨，

translations.literal: They gathered hosts and installed a ruler; five hundred chariots came from afar,
translations.idiomatic: They gathered hosts and installed a ruler; five hundred chariots came from afar,

sentences.zh: （齊遣上黨王渙率兵數萬納梁貞陽侯明為主。）

translations.literal: (Qi sent Prince of Shangdang Huan leading tens of thousands to install Liang's Marquis of Zhenyang Ming as ruler.)
translations.idiomatic: (Qi sent Prince of Shangdang Huan with tens of thousands to install Liang's Marquis of Zhenyang Ming as ruler.)

sentences.zh: 返季子之觀樂，釋鍾儀之鼓琴。

translations.literal: They returned Jizi's viewing of music and released Zhong Yi's drum and zither.
translations.idiomatic: They returned Jizi to his music and released Zhong Yi from drum and zither.

sentences.zh: （梁武聘使謝挺、徐陵始得還南，凡厥梁臣，皆以禮遣。）

translations.literal: (Liang's envoys Xie Ting and Xu Ling at last could return south; all Liang subjects were sent off with ceremony.)
translations.idiomatic: (Liang's envoys Xie Ting and Xu Ling at last returned south; all Liang subjects were sent off with ceremony.)

sentences.zh: 竊聞風而清耳，傾見日之歸心。

translations.literal: Secretly hearing the wind, ears grew clear; leaning toward the seen sun, hearts turned homeward.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the wind in secret, ears grew clear; leaning toward the seen sun, hearts turned homeward.

sentences.zh: 試拂蓍以貞筮，遇交泰之吉林。

translations.literal: He tried brushing the yarrow for a true divination and met Mount Tai's auspicious fortune in the hexagram.
translations.idiomatic: He brushed the yarrow for a true divination and met auspicious fortune in the hexagram of Tai.

sentences.zh: （之推聞梁人返國，故有奔齊之心。

translations.literal: (Zhitui heard Liang people were returning to the state and therefore had a mind to flee to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: (Zhitui heard Liang people were returning home and therefore meant to flee to Qi.

sentences.zh: 以丙子歲旦筮東行吉不，遇《泰》之《坎》，乃喜曰：「天地交泰而更習，坎重險，行而不失其信，此吉卦也，但恨小往大來耳。

translations.literal: On New Year's day of the bingzi year he divined whether going east was auspicious and met Tai changing to Kan; he rejoiced and said: "Heaven and earth join in Tai and turn to practice; Kan doubles peril, yet going without losing faith—this is an auspicious hexagram, only I regret small going and great coming."
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's day of the bingzi year he divined whether going east was auspicious and met Tai changing to Kan; he rejoiced and said, "Heaven and earth join in Tai and turn to practice; Kan doubles peril, yet the journey keeps faith—an auspicious hexagram, only I regret small going and great coming."

sentences.zh: 」後遂吉也。）

translations.literal: " Later it indeed proved auspicious.)
translations.idiomatic: " Later it indeed proved auspicious.)

sentences.zh: 譬欲秦而更楚，假南路於東尋。

translations.literal: It was like wishing for Qin yet changing to Chu, borrowing the southern road toward eastern Xun.
translations.idiomatic: It was like wishing for Qin yet changing to Chu, borrowing the southern road toward eastern Xun.

sentences.zh: 乘龍門之一曲，歷砥柱之雙岑。

translations.literal: He rode one bend of Dragon Gate and passed the twin peaks of Dizhu.
translations.idiomatic: He rode one bend of Dragon Gate and passed the twin peaks of Dizhu.

sentences.zh: 冰夷風薄而雷呴，陽侯山載而谷沈。

translations.literal: Ice Spirit thinned the wind and thunder roared; Yang Lord bore mountains and valleys sank.
translations.idiomatic: Ice Spirit thinned the wind and thunder roared; Yang Lord bore mountains and valleys sank.

sentences.zh: 侔挈龜以憑濬，類斬蛟而赴深。

translations.literal: He matched one who carried the turtle to ford the deep and was like one who slew the flood dragon and plunged into the depths.
translations.idiomatic: He matched one who carried the turtle to ford the deep and was like one who slew the flood dragon and plunged into the depths.

sentences.zh: 昏揚舲於分陜，曙結纜於河陰。

translations.literal: At dusk he raised sails at Fen-Shan; at dawn he moored at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he raised sails at Fen-Shan; at dawn he moored at Heyin.

sentences.zh: （水路七百里一夜而至）

translations.literal: (Seven hundred li by water—they arrived in one night.)
translations.idiomatic: (Seven hundred li by water—they arrived in one night.)

sentences.zh: 追風飈之逸氣，從忠信以行吟。

translations.literal: He chased the swift wind's fleeing breath and followed loyalty and faith in his traveling song.
translations.idiomatic: He chased the swift wind's fleeing breath and followed loyalty and faith in his traveling song.

sentences.zh: 遭厄命而事旋，舊國從於采芑。

translations.literal: Met hostile fate, yet affairs turned round; the old realm followed the ode Gathering Calamus.
translations.idiomatic: Fate turned hostile, yet affairs wheeled about—and the old realm went the way of Gathering Calamus.

sentences.zh: 先廢君而誅相，訖變朝而易市。

translations.literal: First the ruler was deposed and the chancellor executed; at last the court changed and the market shifted.
translations.idiomatic: First they deposed the ruler and killed the chancellor; in the end the court changed hands and the market changed with it.

sentences.zh: （至鄴，便值陳興而梁滅，故不得還南。）

translations.literal: (Upon reaching Ye he happened on Chen's rise and Liang's fall, and so could not return south.)
translations.idiomatic: (When he reached Ye, Chen was rising and Liang was falling, and he could not go home to the south.)

sentences.zh: 遂留滯於漳濱，私自憐其何已。

translations.literal: Thus he lingered on the Zhang's banks, privately lamenting how it would ever end.
translations.idiomatic: So he stayed stranded on the Zhang's shore, privately asking when the waiting would ever end.

sentences.zh: 謝黃鵠之迴集，恧翠鳳之高峙。

translations.literal: He declined the yellow swan's wheeling return; he felt shamed before the azure phoenix towering high.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the yellow swan's wheeling homeward flight and felt small before the azure phoenix on its height.

sentences.zh: 曾微令思之對，空竊彥先之仕，纂書盛化之旁，待詔崇文之裏。

translations.literal: Never had he Wei Lingsi's gift for reply; in vain he stole Yan Xianzhi's post—compiling books beside the Hall where Culture Flourishes, awaiting edict in the quarter honored for letters.
translations.idiomatic: He never had Wei Lingsi's wit in debate, only borrowed Yan Xianzhi's post in name—compiling books by the Flourishing Culture Hall, awaiting edict in the quarter where letters were honored.

sentences.zh: （齊武平中，署文林館待詔者僕射陽休之、祖孝徵以下三十餘人，之推專掌，其撰《修文殿御覽》、《續文章流別》等皆詣進賢門奏之。）

translations.literal: (In Wuping of Qi more than thirty gentlemen awaiting edict at the Forest of Literature were appointed, including Vice Director Yang Xiuzhi, Zu Xiaozheng, and others; Zhitui had sole charge, and works such as the Repair the Culture Hall Imperial Overview and the Continuation of Literary Genres Classification were all presented at the Gate of Advancing Worthies.)
translations.idiomatic: (In Qi's Wuping era over thirty awaiting-edict gentlemen of the Forest of Literature were appointed, from Vice Director Yang Xiuzhi and Zu Xiaozheng downward; Zhitui held sole charge, and works such as the Repair the Culture Hall Imperial Overview and the Continuation of Literary Genres Classification were all submitted at the Gate of Advancing Worthies.)

sentences.zh: 珥貂蟬而就列，執麾蓋以入齒。

translations.literal: Wearing marten tail and cicada badge he took his place in rank; bearing canopy and halberd he entered the sequence.
translations.idiomatic: He pinned marten tail and cicada badge and took his place in the ranks; he bore canopy and halberd and entered the court sequence.

sentences.zh: （時以通直散騎常侍遷黃門郎也。）

translations.literal: (At the time he was transferred from unhampered attendant of scattered cavalry to gentleman of the Yellow Gate.)
translations.idiomatic: (At the time he was promoted from unhampered attendant of scattered cavalry to gentleman of the Yellow Gate.)

sentences.zh: 款一相之故人，

translations.literal: He called on an old friend who had been chancellor alone—
translations.idiomatic: He paid a visit to an old friend, the chancellor who stood alone—

sentences.zh: （故人祖僕射掌機密，吐納帝令也。）

translations.literal: (The old friend, Vice Director Zu, managed secrets, issuing and receiving the emperor's commands.)
translations.idiomatic: (That friend was Vice Director Zu, who held the secrets of state and shaped what the emperor sent out and took in.)

sentences.zh: 賀萬乘之知己。

translations.literal: and congratulated himself on a sovereign's intimate trust.
translations.idiomatic: and counted himself blessed with a sovereign's intimate trust.

sentences.zh: 秪夜語之見忌，寧懷璧之足恃。

translations.literal: Only night talk drew suspicion; could clutching a jade disk really suffice?
translations.idiomatic: Even whispered talk after dark drew suspicion; could clutching a jade disk really keep one safe?

sentences.zh: 諫譖言之矛戟，惕險情之山水。

translations.literal: He guarded against remonstrance and slander's spears and shields; he was wary of perilous hearts like mountain rivers.
translations.idiomatic: He braced against remonstrance and slander, spear and shield alike, and watched hearts treacherous as mountain rivers.

sentences.zh: 由重裘以寒勝，用去薪而沸止。

translations.literal: Through heavy furs cold was overcome; by removing fuel boiling ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy furs could beat back the cold; take away the fuel and the boil stops.

sentences.zh: （時武職疾文人，之推蒙禮遇，每構創痏。

translations.literal: (At the time the military despised literati; Zhitui enjoyed imperial favor and was wounded at every turn.)
translations.idiomatic: (The military class then despised men of letters; Zhitui, though favored, was cut at every turn.)

sentences.zh: 故侍中崔季舒等六人以諫誅，之推爾日鄰禍。

translations.literal: (Hence Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Jishu and six others were put to death for remonstrance; that day Zhitui barely escaped the neighboring disaster.)
translations.idiomatic: (When Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Jishu and six others were executed for remonstrance, Zhitui that day barely escaped the disaster next door.)

sentences.zh: 而儕流或有毀之推於祖僕射者，僕射察之無實，所知如舊不忘。）

translations.literal: (Yet some of his peers slandered Zhitui to Vice Director Zu; the Vice Director investigated and found no substance, and treated him as before without forgetting.)
translations.idiomatic: (Some peers still slandered Zhitui to Vice Director Zu; Zu investigated, found nothing, and kept his regard unchanged.)

sentences.zh: 予武成之燕翼，遵春坊而原始。

translations.literal: I traced Martial Completion's soaring wings, following the Spring Quarters back to origins.
translations.idiomatic: I followed Martial Completion's soaring wings and traced the Spring Quarters back to their source.

sentences.zh: 唯驕奢之是修，亦佞臣之云使。

translations.literal: Only extravagance was cultivated; sycophant ministers were likewise deployed.
translations.idiomatic: Only extravagance was tended; sycophant ministers were put to use as well.

sentences.zh: （武成奢侈，後宮御者數百人，食於水陸貢獻珍異，至乃厭飽，棄於廁中。

translations.literal: (Wucheng was extravagant; the inner palace had several hundred attendants, fed from land and water with rare tribute until they were sated and the surplus was cast into the privy.
translations.idiomatic: (Wucheng was extravagant: several hundred women of the inner palace were fed from land and sea with rare tribute until they were glutted and the surplus was thrown into the privy.)

sentences.zh: 褌衣悉羅纈錦繡珍玉，織成五百一段。

translations.literal: Undergarments were all brocade and embroidery with pearls and jade, woven in sections of five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Even their undergarments were brocade and embroidery studded with pearl and jade, woven in lengths of five hundred.

sentences.zh: 爾後宮掖遂為舊事。

translations.literal: Afterward the inner palace took this as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After that the inner palace kept the custom.

sentences.zh: 後主之在宮，乃使駱提婆母陸氏為之，又胡人何洪珍等為左右，後皆預政亂國焉。）

translations.literal: When the Later Sovereign was in the palace, he had Luotuopa's mother Lady Lu attend him, and Hu men such as He Hongzhen at his side; later they all took part in government and ruined the state.)
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Sovereign was still in the palace, Luotuopa's mother Lady Lu and Hu favorites such as He Hongzhen stood at his side—and in time they all meddled in rule and wrecked the realm.)

sentences.zh: 惜染絲之良質，惰琢玉之遺祉。

translations.literal: He prized dyed silk's fine quality yet was idle toward jade-carving's lasting blessing.
translations.idiomatic: He prized the good fiber of dyed silk yet was slack toward the lasting blessing of carved jade.

sentences.zh: 用夷吾而治臻，昵狄牙而亂起。

translations.literal: Employ Guan Zhong and rule reached perfection; dote on Duke Huan's favorite and disorder rose.
translations.idiomatic: Use a Guan Zhong and order comes; dote on a Duke Huan's favorite and chaos rises.

sentences.zh: （祖孝徵用事，則朝野翕然，政刑有綱紀矣。

translations.literal: (When Zu Xiaozheng held power, court and countryside drew together and government and punishment had their thread.)
translations.idiomatic: (When Zu Xiaozheng held power, court and countryside moved as one and law and policy had a thread to follow.)

sentences.zh: 駱提婆等苦孝徵以法繩己，譖而出之。

translations.literal: Luotuopa and the rest hated Xiaozheng for binding them by law and slandered him until he was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Luotuopa and his circle hated Xiaozheng for binding them with law and slandered him out of office.

sentences.zh: 於是教令昏僻，至于滅亡。

translations.literal: Then edicts grew benighted and perverse, down to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts then grew benighted and perverse, all the way to extinction.

sentences.zh: 誠怠荒於度政，惋驅除之神速。

translations.literal: Truly slack and negligent in measuring government; he grieved how swiftly the divine banishment came.
translations.idiomatic: He was slack and negligent in measuring government, and grieved how swiftly heaven's banishment came.

sentences.zh: 肇平陽之爛魚，次太原之破竹。

translations.literal: First the rotting fish at Pingyang; next bamboo splitting at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: First the rotting fish at Pingyang, then bamboo splitting at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 晉州小失利，便棄軍還幷，又不守幷州，奔走向鄴。

translations.literal: A small setback at Jin province and he abandoned the army back to Bing; he would not hold Bing either, fleeing toward Ye.
translations.idiomatic: A small reverse at Jin province and he abandoned the army for Bing; he would not hold Bing either, but fled toward Ye.

sentences.zh: 寔未改於弦望，遂□□□□□，及都□而升降，懷墳墓之淪覆。

translations.literal: Indeed the new and full moons had not altered; then □□□□□□□; when the capital □ rose and fell, he bore thoughts of ancestral tombs submerged.
translations.idiomatic: The moon's phases had barely shifted when [text missing]; when the capital [text missing] rose and fell he nursed the fear that his family's graves had been drowned.

sentences.zh: 迷識主而狀人，競己棲而擇木。

translations.literal: Lost sight of the ruler to judge men; all rushed to roost and pick their tree.
translations.idiomatic: Men forgot the ruler and judged only people; each hurried to roost and choose his tree.

sentences.zh: 六馬紛其顛沛，千官散於犇逐。

translations.literal: Six horses in turmoil, a thousand officials scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Six horses thrashed in chaos; a thousand officials scattered in the rout.

sentences.zh: 無寒瓜以療饑，靡秋螢而照宿。

translations.literal: No winter melon to cure hunger, no autumn fireflies to light the night.
translations.idiomatic: There was no winter melon to ease hunger, no autumn firefly to light the night.

sentences.zh: （時在季冬，故無此物。）

translations.literal: (It was deep winter, hence no such things.)
translations.idiomatic: (It was deep winter, so such things did not exist.)

sentences.zh: 讎敵起於舟中，胡、越生於輦轂。

translations.literal: Vengeance rose within the boat; Hu and Yue were born at the chariot hub.
translations.idiomatic: Enemies rose within the boat; Hu and Yue sprang from the chariot's hub.

sentences.zh: 壯安德之一戰，邀文武之餘福。

translations.literal: Prince Ande's one battle invited the civil and military remnant's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ande's single battle drew what blessing civil and military remnants could offer.

sentences.zh: 屍狼藉其如莽，血玄黃以成谷。

translations.literal: Corpses strewn thick as wild grass; blood black-yellow piled into valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Corpses lay thick as wild grass; blood black and yellow heaped into valleys.

sentences.zh: （後主犇後，安德王延宗收合餘燼，於幷州夜戰，殺數千人。

translations.literal: (After the Later Sovereign fled, Prince Ande Yan Zong gathered the embers and fought at Bing by night, killing several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: (After the Later Sovereign fled, Prince Ande Yan Zong gathered the embers, fought at Bing by night, and killed several thousand.)

sentences.zh: 周主欲退，齊將之降周者告以虛實，故留至明而安德敗也。）

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler wished to withdraw; Qi generals who had surrendered to Zhou told him the truth, so he stayed until dawn and Ande was defeated.)
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou ruler meant to pull back, but Qi generals who had surrendered to Zhou told him the true situation, so he held on until dawn and Ande was defeated.)

sentences.zh: 天命縱不可再來，猶賢死廟而慟哭。

translations.literal: Though heaven's mandate could not come twice, still he deemed dying at the temple and weeping the nobler act.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate might not come twice, yet he still thought it nobler to die at the ancestral temple and weep.

sentences.zh: 乃詔余以典郡，據要路而問津。

translations.literal: Then he was charged with governing a commandery, holding a key road and asking the ford.
translations.idiomatic: Then they charged him with governing a commandery, holding a key road and asking after the crossing.

sentences.zh: （除之推為平原郡，據河津，以為犇陳之計。）

translations.literal: (He was made governor of Pingyuan, holding the river ford, as part of the plan to flee to Chen.)
translations.idiomatic: (Zhitui was made governor of Pingyuan, holding the river crossing, as part of the plan to flee to Chen.)

sentences.zh: 斯呼航而濟水，郊鄉導於善鄰。

translations.literal: Like calling out to ferry and cross water; countryside guided them to a good neighbor.
translations.idiomatic: It was like shouting for a ferry to cross the waters; the countryside would guide them to a friendly neighbor.

sentences.zh: （約以鄴下一戰不剋，當與之推入陳。）

translations.literal: (They agreed that if the battle below Ye did not succeed, he would enter Chen with Zhitui.)
translations.idiomatic: (They agreed that if the fight below Ye failed, the sovereign would enter Chen with Zhitui.)

sentences.zh: 不羞寄公之禮，願為式微之賓。

translations.literal: Not ashamed of lodging with a lord's kindness; willing to be a guest in Decaying Splendour.
translations.idiomatic: He was not ashamed to accept a lord's sheltering kindness and was willing to be a guest in Decaying Splendour.

sentences.zh: 忽成言而中悔，矯陰疏而陽親。

translations.literal: Suddenly after agreement he repented midway; he disguised estrangement in private while showing kinship in public.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly, after words were given, he repented halfway; private coldness wore the mask of public warmth.

sentences.zh: 信諂謀於公主，競受陷於姦臣。

translations.literal: Trusted flattery's plots from the princess; competed to fall into treacherous ministers' traps.
translations.idiomatic: He trusted the princess's flattery and plots, and all raced to fall into treacherous ministers' snares.

sentences.zh: （丞相高阿那肱等不願入南，又懼失齊主則得罪於周朝，故疏間之推。

translations.literal: (Chief Minister Gao Anagong and the rest did not wish to go south, and feared that losing the Qi ruler would mean guilt before Zhou, so they estranged Zhitui.
translations.idiomatic: (Chief Minister Gao Anagong and the rest did not wish to flee south and feared that if they lost the Qi ruler Zhou would blame them, so they drove a wedge between sovereign and Zhitui.)

sentences.zh: 所以齊主留之推守平原城，而索船渡濟向青州。

translations.literal: Therefore the Qi ruler left Zhitui to hold Pingyuan city while he demanded boats to cross the Ji toward Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: So the Qi ruler left Zhitui to hold Pingyuan while he demanded boats to cross the Ji toward Qing province.

sentences.zh: 阿那肱求自鎮濟州，乃啟報應齊主云：「無賊，勿怱怱。

translations.literal: Anagong asked to garrison Jizhou himself and then reported to the Qi ruler, "No bandits—do not hurry."
translations.idiomatic: Anagong asked to garrison Jizhou himself, then sent word to the Qi ruler: "There are no bandits—do not hurry."

sentences.zh: 」遂道周軍追齊主而及之。）

translations.literal: Thus he guided the Zhou army to pursue the Qi ruler and overtake him.)
translations.idiomatic: So he guided the Zhou army in pursuit until they overtook the Qi ruler.)

sentences.zh: 曩九圍以制命，今八尺而由人。

translations.literal: Once nine domains answered to command; now eight feet are subject to others.
translations.idiomatic: Once the nine domains answered to his command; now even eight feet of body belong to another.

sentences.zh: 四七之期必盡，百六之數溘屯。

translations.literal: The twenty-eight-year term must run out; the hundred-six count suddenly heaps up.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-eight-year span had to end; the hundred-six calamity number suddenly piled up.

sentences.zh: （趙郡李穆叔調妙占天文算術，齊初踐祚計止於二十八年。

translations.literal: (Li Muchu of Zhao commandery was skilled in astronomy and calculation; at Qi's founding he calculated that rule would end in twenty-eight years.
translations.idiomatic: (Li Muchu of Zhao commandery was skilled in astronomy and reckoning; at Qi's founding he calculated that the dynasty would end in twenty-eight years.)

sentences.zh: 至是如期而滅。）

translations.literal: When the time came it perished as foretold.)
translations.idiomatic: When the term came it fell exactly as he had said.)

sentences.zh: 予一生而三化，備荼苦而蓼辛。

translations.literal: One life, three transformations; he tasted bitterness of tea and pungency of smartweed.
translations.idiomatic: In one life he knew three transformations and tasted tea's bitterness and smartweed's bite.

sentences.zh: （在揚都值侯景殺簡文而篡位，於江陵逢孝元覆滅，至此而三為亡國之人。）

translations.literal: (At Yangdu he met Hou Jing's killing of Emperor Jianwen and usurpation; at Jiangling he met Emperor Xiaoyuan's ruin; here he became a man of a fallen state for the third time.)
translations.idiomatic: (At Yangdu he lived through Hou Jing's murder of Emperor Jianwen and seizure of the throne; at Jiangling through Emperor Xiaoyuan's destruction; here he was a man of a ruined state for the third time.)

sentences.zh: 鳥焚林而鎩翮，魚奪水而暴鱗。

translations.literal: Birds burned the forest and broke pinions; fish lost water and exposed scales.
translations.idiomatic: Birds burned the forest and broke their pinions; fish lost the water and bared their scales.

sentences.zh: 嗟宇宙之遼曠，愧無所而容身。

translations.literal: Alas the universe's vast emptiness; ashamed that nowhere could hold his person.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—the universe's vast emptiness; he was ashamed that nowhere could hold his body.

sentences.zh: 夫有過而自訟，始發矇於天真。

translations.literal: When one faults oneself in lawsuit, only then does enlightenment break through native truth.
translations.idiomatic: Only when a man accuses himself does the veil lift from inborn truth.

sentences.zh: 遠絕聖而棄智，妄鎖義以羈仁。

translations.literal: Far rejecting sagehood and abandoning wisdom, vainly locking duty to bind benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: He had rejected the sages from afar and cast wisdom aside, vainly locking duty to chain benevolence.

sentences.zh: 舉世溺而欲拯，王道鬱以求申。

translations.literal: All the world drowned and he wished to save it; the kingly way was choked and he sought to clear it.
translations.idiomatic: The whole world was drowning and he wished to save it; the kingly way was choked and he sought to open it.

sentences.zh: 旣銜石以填海，終荷戟入秦。

translations.literal: First he carried stone to fill the sea; in the end he shouldered spear to enter Qin.
translations.idiomatic: First he carried stone to fill the sea; in the end he bore a spear toward Qin.

sentences.zh: 亡壽陵之故步，臨大行以逡巡。

translations.literal: Lost Shouling's old pace; facing the great road he hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: He lost Shouling's old stride and halted on the great road, unable to go forward.

sentences.zh: 向使潛於草茅之下，甘為畎畝之人。

translations.literal: Had he only hid beneath thatch, content as a field hand—
translations.idiomatic: Had he only hidden under thatch and been content as a man behind the plow—

sentences.zh: 無讀書而學劍，莫抵掌以膏身，委明珠而樂賤，辭白璧以安貧，堯、舜不能榮其素樸，桀、紂無以汙其清塵。

translations.literal: no reading books and learning sword, never rubbing palms to anoint himself, yielding bright pearls to delight in low estate, declining white jade to dwell in poverty—Yao and Shun could not glorify such plainness, Jie and Zhou could not stain such clear dust.
translations.idiomatic: never reading books and learning the sword, never rubbing his palms to grease his way upward, yielding bright pearls to rejoice in low estate, declining white jade to rest in poverty—Yao and Shun could not have glorified such plainness, Jie and Zhou could not have stained such clear dust.

sentences.zh: 此窮何由而至，茲辱安所自臻。

translations.literal: Whence did this extremity come? Whence did this disgrace arise?
translations.idiomatic: Whence came this extremity? Whence this disgrace?

sentences.zh: 而今而後，不敢怨天而泣麟也。

translations.literal: From now on I dare not blame heaven or weep for the unicorn.
translations.idiomatic: From now on I dare not blame heaven or weep for the unicorn.

sentences.zh: 之推在齊有二子，長曰思魯，次曰敏楚，不忘本也。

translations.literal: Zhitui had two sons in Qi: the elder Siyu, the younger Minchu—names that forgot nothing of their roots.
translations.idiomatic: Zhitui had two sons in Qi: the elder Siyu, the younger Minchu—names that would not let them forget where they came from.

sentences.zh: 之推集在，思魯自為序錄。

translations.literal: Zhitui's collected works survive; Siyu wrote the preface and record himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhitui's collected works survive; Siyu wrote the preface and catalogue himself.

sentences.zh: 袁奭，字元明，陳郡人，梁司空昂之孫也。

translations.literal: Yuan Shuang, styled Yuanming, of Chen commandery, was grandson of Liang Minister of Works Yuan Ang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shuang, styled Yuanming, came from Chen commandery and was grandson of Liang Minister of Works Yuan Ang.

sentences.zh: 父君方，梁侍中。

translations.literal: His father Junfang was Liang attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His father Junfang had been Liang attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 奭，蕭莊時以侍中奉使貢。

translations.literal: Shuang, in Xiao Zhuang's time, as attendant-in-ordinary bore tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiao Zhuang's time Shuang served as attendant-in-ordinary on missions bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 莊敗，除琅邪王儼大將軍諮議，入館，遷太中大夫。

translations.literal: When Zhuang fell he was assigned to Prince of Langye Yan's staff as army counsellor, entered the hall, and was promoted grand palace counsellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuang fell he was attached to Prince of Langye Yan as army counsellor, entered the Forest of Literature Hall, and rose to grand palace counsellor.

sentences.zh: 韋道遜，京兆杜陵人。

translations.literal: Wei Daoxun was a man of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Daoxun came from Duling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖肅，隨劉義真渡江。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Su followed Liu Yizhen across the river.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Su followed Liu Yizhen when he crossed the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 祖崇，自宋入魏，寓居河南洛陽，官至華山太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chong, coming from Song into Wei, lived at Luoyang in Henan and rose to governor of Huashan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chong came from Song into Wei, settled at Luoyang in Henan, and rose to governor of Huashan.

sentences.zh: 道遜與兄道密、道建、道儒並早以文學知名。

translations.literal: Daoxun with his elder brothers Daomi, Daojian, and Daoru were all early famed for letters.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxun and his elder brothers Daomi, Daojian, and Daoru were all known early for literary talent.

sentences.zh: 道密，魏永熙中開府祭酒。

translations.literal: Daomi, in Wei's Yongxi era, was libationer of an opening establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Daomi, in Wei's Yongxi era, was libationer of an opening establishment.

sentences.zh: 因患恍惚，沉廢於家。

translations.literal: He suffered mental confusion and was confined at home.
translations.idiomatic: He fell into mental confusion and lived out his days confined at home.

sentences.zh: 道建，天保末卒司農少卿。

translations.literal: Daojian died at the end of Tianbao as vice minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Daojian died at the end of Tianbao while serving as vice minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 道儒，歷中書黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Daoru served through the posts of gentleman of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Daoru served as gentleman of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 道遜，武平初尚書左中兵，加通直散騎侍郎，入館，加通直常侍。

translations.literal: Daoxun, in early Wuping, was left military section chief in the Secretariat, added unhampered attendant of scattered cavalry, entered the hall, and was made unhampered regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In early Wuping Daoxun was left military section chief in the Secretariat, then added unhampered attendant of scattered cavalry, entered the hall, and became unhampered regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 江旰，字季，濟陽人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Gan, styled Ji, was a man of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gan, styled Ji, came from Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 祖柔之，蕭齊尚書右丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Rouzhi was director of the right section under Southern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Rouzhi had been Southern Qi's director of the right section.

sentences.zh: 叔父革，梁都官尚書。

translations.literal: His uncle Ge was Liang director of punishments at court.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Ge had been Liang director of punishments at court.

sentences.zh: 旰，梁末給事黃門郎，因使至淮南，為邊將所執，送鄴。

translations.literal: Gan, at the end of Liang, was gentleman of the Yellow Gate; on a mission to Huainan he was seized by a border general and sent to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Liang Gan was gentleman of the Yellow Gate; on a mission to Huainan he was seized by a border general and sent to Ye.

sentences.zh: 稍遷鄭州司馬，入館，除太尉從事中郎，轉太子家令。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to marshal of Zheng province, entered the hall, was made senior aide to the Grand Commandant, and transferred to crown prince household head.
translations.idiomatic: He rose gradually to marshal of Zheng province, entered the hall, became senior aide to the Grand Commandant, and was transferred to crown prince household head.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，逃還建業。

translations.literal: When Qi fell he fled back to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he fled back to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 終於都官尚書。

translations.literal: He died as director of punishments at court.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as director of punishments at court.

sentences.zh: 眭豫，字道閑，趙郡高邑人。

translations.literal: Sui Yu, styled Daoxian, was a man of Gaoyi in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Yu, styled Daoxian, came from Gaoyi in Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 父寂，梁北平太守。

translations.literal: His father Ji was Liang governor of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji had been Liang governor of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 道閑弱冠，州舉秀才。

translations.literal: Daoxian at cap maturity was nominated eminent scholar by his province.
translations.idiomatic: At cap maturity Daoxian was nominated eminent scholar by his province.

sentences.zh: 天保中，參議禮令，歷晉州道行臺郎、大理正、奉車都尉。

translations.literal: In Tianbao he joined discussion on ritual ordinances and served as Jin province expedition staff clerk, grand judge, and chariot-of-the-court commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao he took part in drafting ritual ordinances and served as Jin province expedition staff clerk, grand judge, and chariot-of-the-court commandant.

sentences.zh: 入館。

translations.literal: He entered the hall.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Forest of Literature Hall.

sentences.zh: 遷員外散騎常侍，尋兼祠部郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant and soon also director of the sacrifices department.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant and soon also director of the sacrifices department.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，卒於洛州司馬。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang of Sui he died as Lu province marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui's Kaihuang era he died while serving as marshal of Lu province.

sentences.zh: 豫宗人仲讓，天保時尚書左丞。

translations.literal: A clansman of Yu named Zhongrang was Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing in the Tianbao era.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had a kinsman, Zhongrang, who served as left vice director of the masters of writing in the Tianbao era.

sentences.zh: 朱才，字待問，吳都人。

translations.literal: Zhu Cai, styled Daiwen, was a man of the Wu capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Cai, styled Daiwen, came from the Wu capital.

sentences.zh: 蕭莊在淮南，以才兼散騎常侍，副袁奭入朝。

translations.literal: When Xiao Zhuang was at Huainan, he made Cai concurrently irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry and sent him as deputy to Yuan Shuang on a mission to court.
translations.idiomatic: While Xiao Zhuang held Huainan, he gave Cai the concurrent post of irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry and sent him as Yuan Shuang's deputy on a mission to court.

sentences.zh: 莊敗，留鄴。

translations.literal: When Zhuang was defeated, Cai remained at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuang fell, Cai stayed behind at Ye.

sentences.zh: 稍遷國子博士、諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to doctorate of the National University and remonstrance and review grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by degrees to doctorate of the National University and remonstrance and review grandee.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，客遊信都而卒。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, he traveled as a guest in Xindu and died there.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi fell he wandered as a guest in Xindu and died there.

sentences.zh: 荀仲舉，字士高，潁川人，世江南。

translations.literal: Xun Zhongju, styled Shigao, was a man of Yingchuan whose family had long dwelt south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zhongju, styled Shigao, was from Yingchuan; his house had lived for generations in the lands south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為南沙令，從蕭明於寒山被執。

translations.literal: In Liang service he was magistrate of Nansha; following Xiao Ming at Hanshan he was taken prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he was magistrate of Nansha; he followed Xiao Ming to Hanshan and was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 長樂王尉粲甚禮之。

translations.literal: Prince Changle Wei Can treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changle Wei Can honored him deeply.

sentences.zh: 與粲劇飲，嚙粲指至骨。

translations.literal: Drinking heavily with Can, he bit Can's finger down to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: Once, drinking hard with Can, he bit Can's finger to the bone.

sentences.zh: 顯祖知之，杖仲舉一百。

translations.literal: When Xianzu learned of it, he had Zhongju beaten one hundred strokes with the stick.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu heard of it and had Zhongju beaten one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，答云：「我那知許，當是正疑是麈尾耳。

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, he answered: "How was I to know? I must have mistaken it for a fly-whisk handle.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "How was I to know? I must have taken it for the handle of a fly-whisk.

sentences.zh: 」入館，除符璽郎。

translations.literal: " He entered the hall and was appointed gentleman of seals and credentials.
translations.idiomatic: " He entered the Forest of Literature Hall and was made gentleman of seals and credentials.

sentences.zh: 後以年老家貧，出為義寧太守。

translations.literal: Later, because he was old and his household poor, he was sent out as grand administrator of Yining.
translations.idiomatic: Later, old age and poverty at home sent him out as grand administrator of Yining.

sentences.zh: 仲舉與趙郡李概交款，概死，仲舉因至其宅，為五言詩十六韻以傷之，詞甚悲切。

translations.literal: Zhongju and Li Gai of Zhao commandery were close friends; when Gai died, Zhongju went to his house and composed a pentasyllabic poem in sixteen rhyme-groups to mourn him—the words were deeply sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongju and Li Gai of Zhao were close friends; when Gai died, Zhongju went to his house and wrote a pentasyllabic poem in sixteen rhyme-groups to mourn him—its language was piercingly sad.

sentences.zh: 世稱其美。

translations.literal: The age praised its beauty.
translations.idiomatic: His age praised its beauty.

sentences.zh: 蕭慤，字仁祖，梁上黃侯曄之子。

translations.literal: Xiao Min, styled Renzu, was son of Marquis Ye of Shanghuang in Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Min, styled Renzu, was the son of Liang's Marquis Ye of Shanghuang.

sentences.zh: 天保中入國，武平中太子洗馬。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he entered [Northern] Qi; in Wuping he was crown prince groom.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era he came into Qi; in Wuping he was crown prince groom.

sentences.zh: 古道子，河內人。

translations.literal: Gu Daozi was a man of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Daozi came from Henei.

sentences.zh: 父起，魏太中大夫。

translations.literal: His father Qi was Grand Master of Palace Counsel in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi had been grand master of palace counsel under Wei.

sentences.zh: 道子有幹局，當官以強濟知名，歷檢校御史、司空田曹參軍。

translations.literal: Daozi had administrative talent; in office he was known for forceful execution, and passed through posts as reviewing censor and household-census retainer in the Minister of Works' fields bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi had real administrative grip; in office he was known for driving affairs through by force, and served as reviewing censor and household-census retainer in the Minister of Works' fields bureau.

sentences.zh: 自袁奭等俱涉學有文詞。

translations.literal: From Yuan Shuang downward, all had dipped into learning and possessed literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuan Shuang on, all had touched learning and carried literary skill.

sentences.zh: 荀仲舉、蕭慤工於詩詠。

translations.literal: Xun Zhongju and Xiao Min excelled at poetic composition.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zhongju and Xiao Min were masters of verse.

sentences.zh: 慤曾秋夜賦詩，其兩句云「芙蓉露下落，楊柳月中疏」，為知音所賞。

translations.literal: Min once composed a poem on an autumn night; two of its lines ran, "Lotus dew falls away; willows thin out in the moon"—and connoisseurs prized them.
translations.idiomatic: Min once wrote a poem on an autumn night whose two lines ran, "Lotus dew falls; willows thin in the moon"—and men of taste prized them.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：九流百氏，立言立德，不有斯文，寧資刊勒？

translations.literal: Praise: The nine currents and the hundred schools set words and establish virtue—without this pattern of culture, upon what would carving and inscribing rely?
translations.idiomatic: Praise: The nine currents and the hundred schools set words and establish virtue—without this cultural pattern, what would carving and printing even serve?

sentences.zh: 乃眷淫靡，永言麗則，雅以正邦，哀以亡國。

translations.literal: Yet the age fixes on decadent excess and forever speaks of beautiful norms—the elegant rectifies a state; the elegiac destroys one.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the age dotes on lush excess and forever hymns beautiful norms: the elegant style rectifies a state; the elegiac style destroys one.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
